bugs.name: Aspergillus fumigatus
bugs.disease: Allergic bronchopulmonary disease in asthma or cystic fibrosis
bugs.micro: Ubiquitous mold with narrow septate hyphae branching at acute angles; immediate skin-prick wheal to its antigen, high specific IgE and serum precipitins; hyphae seen on special stains inside mucus plugs
bugs.presentation: 17-year-old with cystic fibrosis: 2 months of new wheeze and coughing up firm brown mucus plugs; FEV1 fell from 70% to 56% predicted despite usual airway clearance. Eosinophils 1,100/uL, total IgE 1,900 IU/mL. CT: mucus-filled dilated central bronchi.

bugs.name: Aspergillus fumigatus
bugs.micro: Mold with narrow septate hyphae branching at acute (about 45 degree) angles; conidiophores end in a fan-shaped head of spore chains; rarely grows in blood bottles, so serum galactomannan and tissue histology carry the diagnosis
bugs.presentation: 61-year-old man 3 months after mitral valve replacement, also on prednisone for lung disease: 5 weeks of temperatures to 38.4 C, then a sudden cold, pulseless left leg. TEE: 3 cm mass on the prosthesis. Six blood bottles show no growth; no animal or louse exposure.

bugs.name: Bartonella henselae
bugs.disease: Culture-negative endocarditis in a cat owner
bugs.micro: Small, poorly staining gram-negative bacilli; facultative intracellular in red cells and endothelial cells; silver (Warthin-Starry) stain of excised valve shows clumped bacilli; high IgG titer or valve PCR; carried by cats and their fleas
bugs.presentation: 51-year-old woman with known mitral regurgitation who fosters kittens, healed scratches on both hands: 3 months of low-grade fevers, fatigue, 6 kg weight loss. T 38.0 C, louder apical holosystolic murmur, spleen tip palpable. Six blood bottles sterile; no farm animals or lice.

bugs.name: Bartonella quintana
bugs.disease: Culture-negative endocarditis in a homeless person with lice
bugs.micro: Small, poorly staining gram-negative bacilli; facultative intracellular in red cells and endothelial cells; spread in body-louse feces; diagnosed by serology or PCR of excised valve tissue rather than culture
bugs.presentation: 48-year-old man living in a shelter with heavy alcohol use; lice in his clothing seams and scratched skin. 3 months of fevers, fatigue and 7 kg weight loss; new early diastolic murmur at the left sternal border; spleen tip palpable. Six blood bottles show no growth.

bugs.name: Bordetella pertussis
bugs.disease: Whooping cough in an unvaccinated young infant
bugs.micro: Small gram-negative coccobacillus; strict aerobe, slow-growing on Regan-Lowe charcoal agar; PCR of a nasopharyngeal swab; its toxin ADP-ribosylates Gi, raising cAMP and causing lymphocytosis; filamentous hemagglutinin binds ciliated cells
bugs.presentation: 7-week-old unvaccinated boy, afebrile: a week of cold symptoms, then bursts of 10-15 coughs without a breath, ending in vomiting, cyanosis and a 20-second pause in breathing. Well between bursts; lungs clear. WBC 32,000/uL with 80% lymphocytes.

bugs.name: Borrelia burgdorferi
bugs.micro: Large microaerophilic spirochete seen on Giemsa or silver stain but rarely cultured; Ixodes deer-tick vector (white-footed mouse reservoir); two-tier serology: enzyme immunoassay, then Western blot
bugs.presentation: 27-year-old woman hiked in Connecticut in June and pulled a small tick off her calf. 5 weeks later she is lightheaded with a left facial droop; HR 40. Telemetry shows the PR interval swinging from 0.32 s to complete block and back within minutes. No murmur.

bugs.name: Candida albicans
bugs.disease: Fungal endocarditis in a person who injects drugs
bugs.micro: Oval budding yeast with pseudohyphae (elongated buds that stay attached - not true hyphae); germ tube positive at 37 C; grows on routine blood agar and Sabouraud; normal skin, mouth and gut flora
bugs.presentation: 30-year-old woman who injects heroin: 3 weeks of fevers and fatigue despite 10 days of IV vancomycin plus piperacillin-tazobactam; T 38.6 C. Holosystolic murmur at the left lower sternal border, louder on inspiration; fluffy white lesions in both retinas. TEE: 2.4 cm mass.

bugs.name: Chlamydia trachomatis
bugs.micro: Obligate intracellular bacterium with almost no peptidoglycan, so it does not Gram stain; infectious elementary body, replicating reticulate body; cytoplasmic inclusions on Giemsa; NAAT of a nasopharyngeal swab; acquired in the birth canal
bugs.presentation: 6-week-old girl born vaginally, afebrile: 2 weeks of worsening cough and RR 62; she had sticky eye discharge at 10 days of age. Fine crackles, no wheeze, T 37.2 C. Eosinophils 900/uL; CXR: hyperinflation with bilateral interstitial streaks.

bugs.name: Corynebacterium diphtheriae
bugs.micro: Club-shaped gram-positive rods in V and palisade shapes with metachromatic granules on methylene blue; black colonies on tellurite agar, grown on Loeffler medium; Elek test confirms the phage-encoded toxin that inactivates EF-2
bugs.presentation: 7-year-old unvaccinated boy recently arrived from a refugee camp: sore throat, T 38.2 C, grey-white coating over both tonsils that bleeds when scraped. On day 10 he has a nasal voice, HR 44 with complete heart block and troponin I 1.8 ng/mL.

bugs.name: Corynebacterium species (diphtheroids)
bugs.micro: Pleomorphic, club-shaped gram-positive rods in V and palisade arrangements; catalase-positive; normal skin and upper-airway flora that make no toxin; enriched and isolated on Loeffler medium
bugs.presentation: 70-year-old man with a dual-chamber pacemaker placed 5 months ago: 4 weeks of low-grade temperatures and malaise; T 38.0 C, generator pocket not inflamed. TEE: 1.1 cm mobile mass on the right ventricular lead. Two of four blood bottles turn positive on day 3.

bugs.name: Coxiella burnetii
bugs.micro: Tiny pleomorphic coccobacilli that barely take the Gram stain; obligate intracellular, so routine blood cultures stay sterile; spore-like form survives in dust; diagnosed by serology (phase I IgG 1:800 or higher) or PCR
bugs.presentation: 60-year-old goat-dairy worker with a mechanical aortic valve placed 6 years ago: 6 months of night sweats, fatigue and 5 kg weight loss. T 37.9 C, finger clubbing, liver and spleen both palpable, new paravalvular leak murmur. Three sets of blood bottles sterile after 7 days.

bugs.name: Coxsackievirus B
bugs.micro: Non-enveloped, positive-sense single-stranded RNA enterovirus (picornavirus); fecal-oral and respiratory spread, peaking in summer and fall; detected by PCR of blood, stool or throat swab; injures myocytes directly and via cytotoxic T cells
bugs.presentation: 31-year-old woman in August, a week after a cold that also gave her two children fever and loose stools: sharp central chest pain, worse lying flat and on deep breaths. T 37.9 C, HR 102. ECG: diffuse concave ST elevation, PR depression; troponin, echo normal.

bugs.name: Coxsackievirus B
bugs.micro: Non-enveloped, positive-sense single-stranded RNA enterovirus (picornavirus); fecal-oral and respiratory spread, peaking in summer and fall; detected by PCR of blood, stool or throat swab; injures myocytes directly and via cytotoxic T cells
bugs.presentation: At a summer camp where several children are ill, a 12-year-old has T 38.9 C and sudden minutes-long spasms of stabbing lower-chest and upper-abdominal pain. Intercostal muscles are tender; ECG, troponin and chest film are normal. A camp-mate has aseptic meningitis.

bugs.name: Coxsackievirus B
bugs.disease: Viral myocarditis in a young adult
bugs.micro: Non-enveloped, positive-sense single-stranded RNA enterovirus (picornavirus); fecal-oral and respiratory spread, peaking in summer and fall; detected by PCR of blood, stool or throat swab; injures myocytes directly and via cytotoxic T cells
bugs.presentation: 17-year-old footballer whose teammates passed around a summer stomach bug 2 weeks ago: 3 days of exertional dyspnea, palpitations and chest discomfort. T 37.9 C, HR 124 with runs of extra beats, an S3, bibasal crackles. Troponin I 2.4 ng/mL; echo LVEF 35% with global hypokinesis.

bugs.name: Enterococcus faecalis
bugs.disease: Endocarditis after urinary or bowel instrumentation
bugs.micro: Gram-positive cocci in pairs and short chains; catalase-negative; Lancefield D; bile-esculin positive, grows in 6.5% NaCl and PYR-positive; capsule resists phagocytosis
bugs.presentation: 79-year-old man had a transurethral resection of the prostate 3 weeks ago and a bladder catheter for 10 days. Now 2 weeks of fatigue, T 38.3 C, HR 98 and a new apical holosystolic murmur radiating to the axilla; urinalysis 40 WBC/hpf. No dental work.

bugs.name: HACEK group
bugs.disease: Gram-negative native-valve endocarditis in a non-drug user
bugs.micro: Fastidious pleomorphic gram-negative bacilli and coccobacilli from normal mouth flora; need CO2-enriched incubation and often 5-10 days before blood bottles flag; capsule in some members resists phagocytosis
bugs.presentation: 66-year-old man with severe periodontitis who has never used drugs: 2 months of low-grade temperatures, 6 kg weight loss and a new apical holosystolic murmur. Blood bottles drawn on admission flag positive only on day 10 of incubation.

bugs.name: Haemophilus influenzae type b
bugs.micro: Small gram-negative coccobacilli that need factor X (hemin) and factor V (NAD): grow on chocolate agar, or on blood agar only as satellites around a coagulase-positive coccus; polyribosylribitol phosphate capsule is the vaccine target
bugs.presentation: 3-year-old boy whose parents declined all vaccines: well at bedtime, woke at 2 a.m. with T 39.4 C, sore throat and a soft high-pitched noise on breathing in. Refuses to swallow, saliva runs from his mouth, voice muffled, no cough; HR 160, SpO2 94%; lungs clear.

bugs.name: Legionella pneumophila
bugs.micro: Faintly staining thin gram-negative bacilli; extremely fastidious - grows only on buffered charcoal yeast extract agar with cysteine and iron, so routine blood bottles stay sterile; facultative intracellular; lives in amoebae in warm water
bugs.presentation: 70-year-old man with a bioprosthetic aortic valve placed 8 months ago at a hospital that later traced a cluster of lung infections to its hot-water system: 2 months of low-grade fevers, sweats, 4 kg weight loss. TEE: small mass on the prosthesis. Bottles sterile at day 7.

bugs.name: Listeria monocytogenes
bugs.disease: Bacteremia in a pregnant or immunosuppressed adult
bugs.micro: Short gram-positive rods; catalase-positive; tumbling motility at room temperature; narrow zone of beta hemolysis; grows at refrigerator temperature (cold enrichment); facultative intracellular, spreads cell to cell on actin tails
bugs.presentation: 31-year-old woman at 29 weeks' gestation ate unpasteurized queso fresco 10 days ago. Now T 38.7 C, myalgia, low back pain and loose stools; HR 108, fetal heart rate 172/min. No murmur, no urinary symptoms, no sick contacts.

bugs.name: Mycobacterium tuberculosis
bugs.micro: Slender acid-fast rods (Ziehl-Neelsen) that Gram stain poorly; obligate aerobe that takes weeks to grow on Lowenstein-Jensen; cord factor; caseating granulomas; pericardial fluid is a lymphocytic exudate with high adenosine deaminase
bugs.presentation: 38-year-old man from rural India with HIV, CD4 180/uL: 2 months of night sweats, evening fevers and 8 kg weight loss, then progressive dyspnea, ankle edema and ascites. JVP 14 cm, lungs clear. CT: pericardium 8 mm thick with a small effusion and patchy calcification.

bugs.name: Mycoplasma pneumoniae
bugs.disease: Atypical pneumonia in a school-age child or teen
bugs.micro: Smallest free-living bacterium; no cell wall, so not seen on Gram stain and unaffected by beta-lactams; sterol (cholesterol) in its membrane; slow growth on Eaton agar; IgM cold agglutinins lyse red cells at 4 C; PCR of a throat swab
bugs.presentation: 14-year-old boy at a boarding school where several classmates are ill: a week of malaise, headache, sore throat and nagging dry cough; T 38.2 C, SpO2 96%, scattered crackles. CXR: patchy bilateral interstitial infiltrates. Hb 10.9 g/dL with a positive direct antiglobulin test.

bugs.name: Nutritionally variant streptococci (Abiotrophia, Granulicatella)
bugs.disease: Culture-negative endocarditis after a tooth extraction
bugs.micro: Viridans-like oral gram-positive cocci in chains that cannot make pyridoxal: no growth on routine blood agar, but grow on B6-supplemented media or as tiny satellite colonies around a streak of a pyridoxal-secreting coagulase-positive coccus
bugs.presentation: 64-year-old woman with a bicuspid aortic valve: 6 weeks of low-grade temperatures and fatigue that began 2 weeks after a tooth extraction. Diastolic murmur at the left sternal border; ESR 70 mm/h. Routine aerobic and anaerobic blood bottles are still without growth at day 5.

bugs.name: Parainfluenza virus
bugs.micro: Enveloped, negative-sense RNA paramyxovirus carrying a hemagglutinin-neuraminidase (HN) glycoprotein and an F protein; droplet spread, autumn peaks; diagnosis is clinical, with PCR of a nasopharyngeal swab if needed
bugs.presentation: 2-year-old boy in October whose sister had a cold last week: 2 days of runny nose and low fever, then a harsh cough worse at night and a high-pitched noise on breathing in, louder when he cries. Hoarse voice; T 38.1 C, RR 34, SpO2 96%; not toxic, drinking well, no drooling.

bugs.name: Pseudomonas aeruginosa
bugs.disease: Chronic airway infection in cystic fibrosis
bugs.micro: Gram-negative rods; oxidase-positive, non-lactose fermenter, strict aerobe; blue-green pyocyanin pigment and grape-like odor on agar; exotoxin A inactivates EF-2; mucoid alginate strains in chronically infected airways
bugs.presentation: 16-year-old with cystic fibrosis: FEV1 fell from 78% to 55% predicted over a year, with daily thick green sputum, crackles over both upper lobes and clubbing. Eosinophil count and total IgE are normal. No wheeze, no brown mucus plugs.

bugs.name: Pseudomonas aeruginosa
bugs.disease: Gram-negative endocarditis in a person who injects drugs
bugs.micro: Gram-negative rods; oxidase-positive, non-lactose fermenter, strict aerobe; blue-green pyocyanin pigment and grape-like odor on agar; exotoxin A inactivates EF-2; mucoid alginate strains in chronically infected airways
bugs.presentation: 35-year-old man who injects crushed oxycodone tablets: 9 days of fevers to 39.4 C that persist after 5 days of IV vancomycin. Murmurs at the left lower sternal border and the apex; TEE shows masses on both tricuspid and mitral leaflets and a mitral ring abscess.

bugs.name: Respiratory syncytial virus
bugs.micro: Enveloped, non-segmented negative-sense RNA paramyxovirus; its F (fusion) protein merges infected cells into multinucleated giant cells and is the target of the monoclonal antibody nirsevimab; rapid antigen or PCR on a nasal swab
bugs.presentation: 2-month-old boy born at 32 weeks, in December, whose brother in daycare has a cold: 2 days of runny nose, now coughing, grunting and taking half his usual feeds. T 38.1 C, RR 64, SpO2 89%; subcostal retractions, wheeze and fine crackles on both sides.

bugs.name: Rickettsia rickettsii
bugs.micro: Small obligate intracellular gram-negative coccobacillus that takes the Gram stain poorly (use Giemsa); cannot make its own energy; grows in endothelial cytoplasm; dog tick vector with transovarial passage; IFA serology, PCR or skin biopsy
bugs.presentation: 8-year-old boy in Tennessee in June who plays in the woods with his dog: 4 days of T 39.5 C, severe headache, calf pain and vomiting. Today small red spots on the ankles and wrists only, with puffy hands and feet. Na+ 129 mEq/L, platelets 68,000/uL.

bugs.name: Staphylococcus aureus
bugs.disease: Acute tricuspid endocarditis in a person who injects drugs
bugs.micro: Gram-positive cocci in grape-like clusters; catalase-positive and coagulase-positive (plasma clots in the tube); beta-hemolytic golden colonies; fibronectin-binding proteins and clumping factor let it attach to a normal valve
bugs.presentation: 26-year-old woman who injects heroin and fentanyl: 3 days of rigors, T 39.8 C, cough with blood-streaked sputum and right pleuritic pain. HR 122, BP 98/60; fluctuant abscess at a groin injection site; new holosystolic murmur at the left lower sternal border, louder breathing in.

bugs.name: Staphylococcus aureus
bugs.micro: Gram-positive cocci in grape-like clusters; catalase-positive and coagulase-positive (plasma clots in the tube); beta-hemolytic golden colonies; fibronectin-binding proteins and clumping factor let it attach to a normal valve
bugs.presentation: 71-year-old man on hemodialysis, 3 weeks after a bloodstream infection from his catheter: T 38.6 C, constant back and upper abdominal pain, tender pulsatile mass above the umbilicus. CT: 4.8 cm saccular infrarenal aortic bulge with periaortic stranding, not present 6 months ago.

bugs.name: Staphylococcus epidermidis
bugs.disease: Early prosthetic valve endocarditis (within 2 months of surgery)
bugs.micro: Gram-positive cocci in clusters; catalase-positive but coagulase-negative; novobiocin-sensitive; gamma (non-hemolytic); slime-layer capsule builds a biofilm on catheters, joints and artificial valves
bugs.presentation: 67-year-old woman 5 weeks after mitral replacement with a mechanical prosthesis: 2 weeks of evening temperatures of 37.9-38.3 C, night sweats, fatigue; sternal wound healed. HR 96; new apical holosystolic murmur; TEE: paravalvular leak, small mobile mass on the sewing ring.

bugs.name: Streptococcus agalactiae (group B)
bugs.micro: Gram-positive cocci in chains; catalase-negative; beta-hemolytic; bacitracin-resistant; CAMP-test positive and hippurate-hydrolyzing; Lancefield B antigen; polysaccharide capsule; colonizes the maternal rectum and vagina
bugs.presentation: Term boy, 14 hours old: grunting, RR 74, T 38.3 C, poor feeding. His mother's rectovaginal screen at 36 weeks was positive, membranes ruptured 22 hours before delivery, and she received no antibiotics in labor. CXR: bilateral hazy granular opacities.

bugs.name: Streptococcus gallolyticus (S. bovis)
bugs.disease: Endocarditis with an occult colorectal cancer
bugs.micro: Gram-positive cocci in chains; catalase-negative; Lancefield D but not enterococcal: bile-esculin positive (agar turns black), yet no growth in 6.5% NaCl and PYR-negative
bugs.presentation: 68-year-old woman: 6 weeks of low-grade fevers and fatigue, 3 months of thinner stools with occasional dark blood; no dental work, catheters or procedures. T 38.0 C, pale, new apical holosystolic murmur; Hb 9.4 g/dL, MCV 72 fL.

bugs.name: Streptococcus pneumoniae
bugs.disease: Lobar pneumonia in an older adult
bugs.micro: Lancet-shaped gram-positive diplococci; catalase-negative; alpha-hemolytic; optochin-sensitive and bile-soluble (unlike oral alpha-hemolytic cocci); polysaccharide capsule swells with type-specific antiserum (quellung); IgA protease
bugs.presentation: 67-year-old man: 2 days of chills, T 39.4 C, right pleuritic pain and blood-streaked purulent sputum. RR 28, SpO2 91%. Dullness, bronchial breath sounds and more fremitus at the right base; WBC 19,000/uL; CXR: dense consolidation of the right lower lobe only.

bugs.name: Streptococcus pyogenes
bugs.disease: Acute rheumatic fever after untreated pharyngitis
bugs.micro: Gram-positive cocci in chains; catalase-negative; beta-hemolytic (oxygen-stable hemolysin S clears the plate); bacitracin-sensitive, PYR-positive; Lancefield A carbohydrate; M protein; raised ASO or anti-DNase B titer shows recent infection
bugs.presentation: 9-year-old girl, 3 months after an untreated sore throat: 4 weeks of clumsiness, dropping cups, crying spells, and quick involuntary jerks of the face and hands that vanish in sleep. New apical holosystolic murmur; afebrile; ESR 42 mm/h; no joint swelling.

bugs.name: Treponema pallidum
bugs.micro: Thin, tightly coiled spirochete too slender for Gram stain - seen by dark-field microscopy or silver stain; cannot be cultured; nonspecific RPR/VDRL screen confirmed by FTA-ABS; late disease obliterates the vasa vasorum (endarteritis)
bugs.presentation: 59-year-old man with several untreated sexually transmitted infections in his 20s: 4 months of hoarseness, a brassy cough and exertional dyspnea. BP 150/48; early diastolic murmur at the right upper sternal border. CXR: wide upper mediastinum, thin rim of calcium along the aorta.

bugs.name: Trichinella spiralis
bugs.micro: Roundworm whose larvae encyst in striated muscle as coiled larvae inside nurse cells, seen on muscle biopsy; marked eosinophilia and high CK; serology turns positive after 2-3 weeks; from undercooked pork or wild game
bugs.presentation: 41-year-old hunter ate undercooked bear sausage 3 weeks ago and had diarrhea that week. Now T 38.8 C, painful swollen calves and jaw muscles, palpitations and dyspnea. Eosinophils 4,800/uL (35%), CK 3,900 U/L, troponin I 0.9 ng/mL; ECG: diffuse T-wave inversion.

bugs.name: Trypanosoma cruzi
bugs.micro: Protozoan; in the acute phase a Giemsa-stained blood smear shows C-shaped trypomastigotes with an undulating membrane and a free flagellum; PCR also works; passed in reduviid (kissing) bug feces through the bite wound
bugs.presentation: 6-year-old boy from rural Bolivia who sleeps in a mud-walled, thatched house: 10 days ago a firm, painless red swelling appeared on his cheek where something bit him in his sleep. Now T 38.3 C, HR 140, swollen nodes in front of that ear and hepatosplenomegaly.

bugs.name: Trypanosoma cruzi
bugs.micro: Protozoan; parasitemia is low in chronic disease, so IgG serology replaces the smear; myocardial biopsy shows pseudocysts packed with non-flagellated amastigotes inside muscle fibers; reduviid (kissing) bug vector
bugs.presentation: 47-year-old woman who grew up in an adobe house in rural El Salvador: two faints this month and palpitations; for years she has regurgitated undigested food. HR 46. Holter: multiform PVCs and runs of ventricular tachycardia. Echo: LV apical aneurysm, EF 40%.

bugs.name: Viridans streptococci (S. mutans, S. sanguinis, S. mitis)
bugs.disease: Late prosthetic valve endocarditis (a year or more after surgery)
bugs.micro: Gram-positive cocci in chains; catalase-negative; alpha-hemolytic (green) colonies; optochin-resistant and bile-insoluble; bile-esculin negative and no Lancefield group; dextran makes them stick to fibrin-platelet clumps
bugs.presentation: 66-year-old woman with a bioprosthetic mitral valve placed 3 years ago had a deep dental scaling 6 weeks ago. Since then: low-grade temperatures, fatigue, 3 kg weight loss; T 38.1 C, HR 92, ESR 64 mm/h. TEE: 8 mm mobile mass on one prosthetic leaflet, no abscess.

bugs.name: Viridans streptococci (S. mutans, S. sanguinis, S. mitis)
bugs.disease: Subacute endocarditis on a damaged native valve after dental work
bugs.micro: Gram-positive cocci in chains; catalase-negative; alpha-hemolytic (green) colonies; optochin-resistant and bile-insoluble; bile-esculin negative and no Lancefield group; dextran makes them stick to fibrin-platelet clumps
bugs.presentation: 52-year-old woman who had rheumatic fever as a child in Pakistan had infected gums deep-scaled 6 weeks ago. Since then: temperatures to 38.4 C, night sweats, 4 kg weight loss. Louder apical holosystolic murmur, spleen tip palpable; Hb 10.6 g/dL; blood bottles positive in 36 h.

bugs.name: Wuchereria bancrofti
bugs.micro: Filarial nematode spread by mosquitoes; adult worms live in lymphatics; sheathed microfilariae circulate at night, so a Giemsa-stained thick blood smear drawn near midnight is diagnostic; circulating antigen test; eosinophilia
bugs.presentation: 34-year-old man from coastal Tamil Nadu: for 2 years, recurring 3-5 day attacks of fever with a painful red streak running down the inner thigh. Now a large painless scrotal swelling that lets light through, and a firm, non-pitting swelling of the left lower leg. Eosinophils 11%.

drugs.name: Abciximab / eptifibatide / tirofiban
drugs.mechanism: Block platelet glycoprotein IIb/IIIa so fibrinogen cannot cross-link platelets (the final common step); the antibody is off the US market, the two small molecules are reversible, short-acting continuous infusions.
drugs.adverseEffects: Bleeding that reproduces an inherited lack of the platelet fibrinogen receptor (Glanzmann); thrombocytopenia; kept for high thrombus risk, aspirin allergy or ADP-blocker intolerance.

drugs.name: ACE inhibitors (lisinopril, enalapril, ramipril, captopril)
drugs.mechanism: Block the enzyme that converts angiotensin I to II and also degrades bradykinin: less vasoconstriction, aldosterone and ADH; lower preload and afterload, less remodeling; efferent dilation protects diabetic kidneys.
drugs.adverseEffects: Bradykinin dry cough (the usual reason to switch to an AT1 blocker) and angioedema, a risk shared with the neprilysin combination; hyperkalemia; first-dose hypotension; renal failure in bilateral renal artery stenosis; fetal renal toxicity.

drugs.name: Adenosine
drugs.mechanism: Agonist at A1 (Gi) receptors in SA and AV nodes, causing transient AV block that terminates PSVT; half-life about 5 seconds, given by rapid IV push; antagonized by methylxanthines.
drugs.adverseEffects: Seconds-long flushing and hypotension (A2-Gs vasodilation), chest tightness and wheeze (A2B-Gq bronchoconstriction), a brief pause; blunted by theophylline and caffeine.

drugs.name: Alirocumab / evolocumab
drugs.mechanism: Monoclonal antibodies that bind circulating PCSK9 protein so it cannot send LDL receptors to lysosomes; receptors recycle and LDL and ApoB-100 drop sharply; SQ every 2 weeks or monthly on top of a maximal statin.
drugs.adverseEffects: Injection-site reactions (cold compress, topical hydrocortisone), hypersensitivity, myalgia with a statin; no proven cognitive harm since they do not cross the blood-brain barrier; expensive.

drugs.name: Aliskiren
drugs.mechanism: Direct renin inhibitor: blocks conversion of angiotensinogen to angiotensin I, so angiotensin II and aldosterone both fall; used only after the other RAAS blockers fail.
drugs.adverseEffects: Hyperkalemia and hypotension like other RAAS blockers; diarrhea; fetal toxicity; do not combine with an ACE inhibitor or AT1 blocker in diabetes (renal failure, hyperkalemia).

drugs.name: Amiodarone
drugs.mechanism: Iodinated Class III with broad action: K+, Na+ and Ca2+ channel block plus alpha and beta blockade; half-life about 60 days; CYP3A4 substrate that inhibits P450, raising digoxin, warfarin and statin levels.
drugs.adverseEffects: Pulmonary fibrosis (interstitial inflammation, type II pneumocyte hyperplasia), hypo- or hyperthyroidism, hepatotoxic metabolite, corneal deposits, blue-gray skin; get baseline chest X-ray, LFTs and thyroid panel.

drugs.name: Amlodipine / felodipine / nifedipine
drugs.mechanism: Block L-type Ca2+ channels in arteriolar smooth muscle only (Ca2+-calmodulin-MLCK chain), lowering TPR and afterload with little direct SA/AV-node effect; two are once daily, one treats hypertension in pregnancy.
drugs.adverseEffects: Reflex tachycardia (baroreceptor), flushing, headache, dizziness, ankle edema from arteriolar dilation, gingival overgrowth; grapefruit (CYP3A4) raises levels and worsens these effects.

drugs.name: ARBs (losartan, valsartan, candesartan)
drugs.mechanism: Block angiotensin II at the AT1 receptor while leaving bradykinin breakdown intact: lower afterload, preload, aldosterone and remodeling - the standard replacement when the converting-enzyme blocker causes cough.
drugs.adverseEffects: No bradykinin cough - patients with ACE-inhibitor cough are switched to it - and angioedema is rare; still hyperkalemia, first-dose dizziness, fetal kidney toxicity, renal failure with bilateral renal artery stenosis.

drugs.name: Aspirin
drugs.mechanism: Irreversibly acetylates COX-1 and COX-2; anucleate platelets cannot make new enzyme, so TXA2 is lost for their 7-10 day life, while endothelium recovers and keeps making prostacyclin at low dose.
drugs.adverseEffects: GI bleeding (loss of protective prostaglandins), bronchospasm from LOX shunting, Reye syndrome in children; overdose: respiratory alkalosis then metabolic acidosis (uncoupling) - give bicarbonate.

drugs.name: Bempedoic acid
drugs.mechanism: Oral prodrug activated in liver but not muscle; inhibits ATP citrate lyase upstream of HMG-CoA reductase, cutting cytosolic acetyl-CoA for cholesterol synthesis; LDL receptors rise; for statin-intolerant patients.
drugs.adverseEffects: Hyperuricemia and gout (competes at the renal urate transporter), tendon rupture (older adults, glucocorticoid or fluoroquinolone users); less myopathy than HMG-CoA reductase blockers.

drugs.name: Cangrelor
drugs.mechanism: IV direct-acting, reversible P2Y12 antagonist: no first-pass metabolism, onset within minutes and platelet function back about an hour after the infusion stops - used around PCI.
drugs.adverseEffects: Bleeding that wears off within about an hour of stopping the IV infusion, which makes it the bridge when surgery may follow.

drugs.name: Cholestyramine / colestipol / colesevelam
drugs.mechanism: Non-absorbed resins that bind bile acids in the gut and break enterohepatic recirculation; the liver up-regulates 7-alpha-hydroxylase and LDL receptors to make new bile acids, so LDL falls about 30%.
drugs.adverseEffects: Bloating, constipation, nausea; bind thyroxine, digoxin, warfarin, thiazides, estrogens and vitamins A, D, E, K - space doses several hours apart; acceptable in pregnancy and children.

drugs.name: Cilostazol
drugs.mechanism: PDE3 inhibitor in platelets and arterial smooth muscle: raises cAMP, inhibiting aggregation and dilating arteries and enhancing prostacyclin action; lengthens walking distance in intermittent claudication.
drugs.adverseEffects: Headache, diarrhea, palpitations and tachycardia; contraindicated in heart failure of any severity (oral PDE3 inhibition raised mortality); CYP3A4 and 2C19 inhibitors raise levels.

drugs.name: Clopidogrel
drugs.mechanism: Oral prodrug activated by hepatic CYP2C19; the active metabolite irreversibly blocks the platelet P2Y12 ADP receptor; given with aspirin after stenting and for unstable angina or NSTEMI.
drugs.adverseEffects: Bleeding (gums, stool); fails in CYP2C19 loss-of-function carriers or with omeprazole (2C19 inhibition) - change the PPI or switch to a direct-acting agent.

drugs.name: Conivaptan
drugs.mechanism: IV antagonist of vasopressin V1a receptors (vascular - lowers PVR) and V2 receptors (collecting duct - fewer aquaporins, free-water excretion); raises serum Na+ in euvolemic or hypervolemic hyponatremia.
drugs.adverseEffects: Overly rapid Na+ correction risks osmotic demyelination; infusion-site phlebitis; hypotension; strong CYP3A4 inhibitor with many interactions.

drugs.name: Digoxin
drugs.mechanism: Inhibits myocyte Na+/K+-ATPase, so the Na+/Ca2+ exchanger extrudes less Ca2+ (positive inotropy); also raises vagal tone (slower SA rate, AV-nodal block, long PR). Long half-life, narrow therapeutic index.
drugs.adverseEffects: Nausea, vomiting, diarrhea; yellow vision and halos; gynecomastia; delayed-afterdepolarization arrhythmias worsened by low K+ or Mg2+, high Ca2+, renal failure, verapamil, quinidine, amiodarone; antidote Fab fragments.

drugs.name: Dipyridamole
drugs.mechanism: Inhibits platelet phosphodiesterase and blocks cellular adenosine reuptake, raising cAMP and local adenosine - coronary vasodilation used for pharmacologic stress testing; antiplatelet when paired with aspirin.
drugs.adverseEffects: Worsened angina from coronary steal (dilates normal beds and diverts flow from ischemic ones); headache, flushing, dizziness, hypotension; effects reversed by aminophylline.

drugs.name: Disopyramide
drugs.mechanism: Class Ia Na+/K+ channel blocker with the strongest atropine-like (antimuscarinic) action of its subclass; removes the vagal brake on the AV node, so it is given with an AV-nodal blocker.
drugs.adverseEffects: Urinary retention, dry mouth and eyes, constipation, dilated pupils and tachycardia; faster AV conduction unless paired with an AV-nodal suppressant; QT prolongation.

drugs.name: Dobutamine
drugs.mechanism: Direct beta-1 agonist (Gs -> adenylyl cyclase -> cAMP -> PKA -> Ca2+ entry) that raises contractility with mild vasodilation; IV for acute decompensated HF and cardiogenic shock; also a stress-test agent.
drugs.adverseEffects: Tachycardia, ventricular ectopy and arrhythmias, angina from higher O2 demand, blood pressure swings; tolerance after 48-72 hours of infusion.

drugs.name: Dofetilide / ibutilide
drugs.mechanism: Pure Class III: block the rapid delayed-rectifier K+ current, delaying phase 3 without touching phase 0 or resting potential; reverse use-dependent; one oral, one IV, for AF and atrial flutter.
drugs.adverseEffects: Marked QT prolongation and torsades with no beta-blocker effects; ECG monitoring for at least 4 hours after the IV infusion, or about 3 days in hospital while the oral agent is started and dosed to renal function.

drugs.name: Dopamine
drugs.mechanism: Dose-dependent agonist: low dose D1 (renal and splanchnic vasodilation, preserves GFR and renal blood flow), medium dose beta-1 (inotropy), high dose alpha-1 (vasoconstriction); IV in acute HF and shock.
drugs.adverseEffects: Tachyarrhythmias; intense vasoconstriction with limb ischemia at high doses; tissue necrosis if it extravasates (infiltrate phentolamine); nausea and vomiting.

drugs.name: Dronedarone
drugs.mechanism: Non-iodinated analogue of the broad-spectrum Class III drug: blocks K+, Na+ and Ca2+ channels with some beta and alpha blockade, but carries no iodine atoms; used to keep sinus rhythm in AF.
drugs.adverseEffects: Much less thyroid, corneal and skin toxicity than its iodinated parent; QT prolongation; raises mortality in advanced or recently decompensated HF and in permanent AF; liver injury.

drugs.name: Eplerenone / finerenone
drugs.mechanism: Selective mineralocorticoid receptor antagonists with little androgen or progesterone receptor binding; the newer one is nonsteroidal, the most selective, and slows progression of chronic kidney disease.
drugs.adverseEffects: Hyperkalemia and acidosis (monitor K+, especially with ACEi/ARB or NSAIDs) without gynecomastia or impotence - the switch when breast enlargement appears on the older agent; costlier.

drugs.name: Esmolol
drugs.mechanism: IV beta-1 selective antagonist hydrolyzed by red-cell esterases; half-life about 9 minutes, so the effect is titratable and ends minutes after stopping - acute rate control (e.g. arrhythmia from theophylline overdose).
drugs.adverseEffects: Hypotension and bradycardia that resolve within minutes of stopping the infusion; irritation or phlebitis at the infusion site.

drugs.name: Ethacrynic acid
drugs.mechanism: Thick-ascending-limb Na+/K+/2Cl- cotransporter blocker that is not a sulfonamide (contains no sulfur) - the option when a patient with sulfa allergy needs a high-ceiling diuretic.
drugs.adverseEffects: The most ototoxic drug of its class (hearing loss, tinnitus); hypokalemia, hypomagnesemia, hyperuricemia, GI upset; no cross-reaction in sulfa-allergic patients.

drugs.name: Evinacumab
drugs.mechanism: Monoclonal antibody against angiopoietin-like protein 3 (ANGPTL3), lifting its brake on lipoprotein lipase and endothelial lipase; lowers LDL without needing LDL receptors - monthly IV infusion for homozygous FH.
drugs.adverseEffects: Infusion reactions and anaphylaxis - given in a monitored facility and can be premedicated; nasopharyngitis and flu-like symptoms; embryo-fetal toxicity.

drugs.name: Ezetimibe
drugs.mechanism: Blocks the Niemann-Pick C1-Like 1 (NPC1L1) sterol transporter at the small-intestine brush border, cutting cholesterol absorption into chylomicrons; adds about 25% LDL lowering to a statin.
drugs.adverseEffects: Generally mild - GI upset and a small rise in liver enzymes when combined with a statin (check LFTs); occasional muscle aches.

drugs.name: Flecainide / propafenone
drugs.mechanism: Class Ic: block open Na+ channels and unbind very slowly - greatest phase 0 slowing and marked QRS widening with minimal change in action potential duration; one also blocks cardiac ryanodine receptors (used in CPVT).
drugs.adverseEffects: Higher mortality after MI or with structural heart disease (CAST); proarrhythmic wide-QRS ventricular tachycardia; negative inotropy worsens heart failure.

drugs.name: Furosemide / bumetanide / torsemide
drugs.mechanism: Sulfonamide 'high-ceiling' diuretics: block the Na+/K+/2Cl- cotransporter in the thick ascending limb, losing the lumen-positive potential so Ca2+ and Mg2+ are wasted; raise PGE2 and venodilate, cutting preload.
drugs.adverseEffects: Ototoxicity (additive with aminoglycosides, cisplatin, vancomycin), hypokalemic alkalosis, low Mg2+ and Ca2+, hyperuricemia, sulfa allergy; NSAIDs blunt the effect; low K+ potentiates digoxin.

drugs.name: Gemfibrozil / fenofibrate
drugs.mechanism: Synthetic PPAR-alpha ligands: change gene transcription to raise lipoprotein lipase (ApoC-II up, ApoC-III down) and hepatic fatty-acid oxidation, degrading VLDL - TG fall about 35%; also suppress 7-alpha-hydroxylase.
drugs.adverseEffects: Cholesterol gallstones (less bile acid made, bile relatively rich in cholesterol); myopathy and rhabdomyolysis, especially combined with a statin, with renal injury.

drugs.name: Hydralazine
drugs.mechanism: Direct arteriolar dilator (raises smooth-muscle cGMP) that lowers afterload with little venous effect; hepatically acetylated; paired with a venodilating NO donor for HFrEF survival; IV for severe preeclampsia.
drugs.adverseEffects: Lupus-like syndrome in slow acetylators; reflex tachycardia (can provoke angina) and salt and water retention, so it often needs a beta blocker and a diuretic; headache, flushing.

drugs.name: Hydrochlorothiazide / chlorthalidone / indapamide
drugs.mechanism: Block the Na+/Cl- cotransporter in the distal convoluted tubule and enhance Ca2+ reabsorption there; volume contraction paradoxically lowers urine output in nephrogenic DI; used for HTN, HF and Ca2+ stones.
drugs.adverseEffects: Hyperglycemia, hyperlipidemia, hyperuricemia, hypercalcemia, hyponatremia, hypokalemic alkalosis; sulfa allergy, photosensitivity; raise lithium levels; low K+ potentiates digoxin.

drugs.name: Inclisiran
drugs.mechanism: Small interfering RNA taken up by hepatocytes that degrades PCSK9 mRNA, so the protein is never made and LDL receptors rise; SQ injection only twice a year.
drugs.adverseEffects: Mild injection-site reactions, arthralgia and bronchitis; being a liver-targeted siRNA rather than an antibody, systemic hypersensitivity is uncommon; clinic-given twice yearly.

drugs.name: Ivabradine
drugs.mechanism: Selective block of the If (funny) current in SA-node pacemaker cells: slows heart rate without changing contractility, conduction or action potential duration; for HF or stable angina when a beta blocker cannot be used.
drugs.adverseEffects: Bradycardia (watch for AV block); transient bright spots in the visual field from retinal Ih channel block; avoid in pregnancy; CYP3A4 inhibitors such as grapefruit raise levels.

drugs.name: Labetalol / carvedilol
drugs.mechanism: Combined alpha-1 and nonselective beta antagonists: alpha block dilates arterioles while beta block prevents reflex tachycardia; one is an HFrEF survival drug with antioxidant action, the other treats hypertension in pregnancy.
drugs.adverseEffects: Orthostatic hypotension and dizziness from alpha-1 block, bradycardia, fatigue, fluid retention while titrating in HF; bronchospasm possible because beta-2 is blocked too.

drugs.name: Lidocaine
drugs.mechanism: Class Ib given IV: binds activated and inactivated Na+ channels and dissociates fast, acting mainly in depolarized ischemic ventricle; shortens action potential and QT. Also an amide local anesthetic.
drugs.adverseEffects: Dose-related CNS toxicity - perioral and limb paresthesias progressing to seizures; CYP450 substrate, so azole antifungals raise its level.

drugs.name: Lomitapide
drugs.mechanism: Oral inhibitor of microsomal triglyceride transfer protein (MTP), blocking assembly of ApoB-48 chylomicrons in gut and ApoB-100 VLDL in liver; for homozygous FH (LDL > 500 mg/dL) despite PCSK9-directed therapy.
drugs.adverseEffects: Hepatotoxicity from hepatic fat accumulation with raised aminotransferases (restricted REMS program), GI upset and steatorrhea, pregnancy category X, CYP3A4 interactions, more toxicity with statins.

drugs.name: Magnesium sulfate
drugs.mechanism: IV divalent cation that blocks Ca2+ influx into the cytosol, suppressing early and delayed afterdepolarizations - first line for torsades and for digitalis-induced arrhythmias, even with a normal serum level.
drugs.adverseEffects: Flushing and hypotension during infusion; at high serum levels, loss of deep tendon reflexes, respiratory depression, bradycardia and heart block (reverse with IV calcium); caution in renal failure.

drugs.name: Metoprolol / atenolol / bisoprolol
drugs.mechanism: Beta-1 selective antagonists used orally for long-term therapy with no partial agonist or vasodilator action: flatten phase 4 in SA/AV node, lower contractility and renin release (Class II); two of the three cut mortality in HFrEF.
drugs.adverseEffects: AV block and bradycardia are the main concern; fatigue; rebound tachycardia or angina if stopped abruptly; spare the airways at usual doses but can mask hypoglycemia.

drugs.name: Mexiletine
drugs.mechanism: Oral Class Ib: rapid-dissociation block of inactivated Na+ channels in depolarized ventricular tissue, shortening the action potential - the by-mouth counterpart of the IV post-MI agent.
drugs.adverseEffects: GI intolerance is the main limit - nausea, vomiting, heartburn (take with food); tremor and dizziness at higher doses.

drugs.name: Milrinone
drugs.mechanism: IV PDE3 inhibitor in myocardium and vascular smooth muscle: stops cAMP breakdown without acting on any receptor, so contractility rises while arterioles and veins dilate (inodilator); acute decompensated HF.
drugs.adverseEffects: Hypotension from vasodilation, atrial and ventricular arrhythmias, headache; accumulates in renal impairment (dose by renal function); long-term oral PDE3 inhibition raised HF mortality.

drugs.name: Nebivolol
drugs.mechanism: Highly beta-1 selective antagonist that also stimulates endothelial nitric oxide release, adding vasodilation without any alpha blockade.
drugs.adverseEffects: Fatigue, bradycardia, headache and dizziness; erectile dysfunction and bronchospasm are less common than with older beta blockers, thanks to high beta-1 selectivity plus NO release.

drugs.name: Nesiritide
drugs.mechanism: Recombinant B-type natriuretic peptide: activates the membrane-bound (particulate) guanylyl cyclase receptor, raising cGMP for venous and arterial dilation plus natriuresis; formerly given IV in acute decompensated HF.
drugs.adverseEffects: Hypotension and worsening renal function - kidney harm without a survival benefit is why it was abandoned.

drugs.name: Niacin
drugs.mechanism: Inhibits lipolysis in adipocytes, so less free fatty acid reaches the liver - less TG and VLDL secretion and lower LDL; gives the largest HDL rise of any lipid drug (30-40%).
drugs.adverseEffects: Prostaglandin-mediated flushing and itching (pretreat with aspirin or use slow release), hyperglycemia, hyperuricemia and gout, worsened peptic ulcer, myositis with a statin; avoid in pregnancy.

drugs.name: Nitroglycerin / isosorbide dinitrate / isosorbide mononitrate
drugs.mechanism: Bioactivated by glutathione-S-transferase and a mitochondrial aldehyde enzyme to release NO -> guanylyl cyclase -> cGMP -> smooth-muscle relaxation, mainly venous: preload and O2 demand fall; sublingual route skips first pass.
drugs.adverseEffects: Throbbing headache, orthostatic hypotension with reflex tachycardia, salt and water retention; tolerance with continuous use (needs an 8- to 12-hour drug-free interval each day); severe hypotension with PDE5 inhibitors.

drugs.name: Nitroprusside
drugs.mechanism: Short-acting IV NO donor (an iron-cyanide complex) that dilates arterioles and venules equally, lowering afterload and preload at once - for hypertensive emergency and acute HF.
drugs.adverseEffects: Cyanide and its metabolite thiocyanate accumulate with high doses, long infusions or renal impairment - confusion, flushed pink skin, dyspnea, lactic acidosis - treated with hydroxocobalamin or sodium thiosulfate; profound hypotension.

drugs.name: Omega-3 fatty acids (EPA/DHA, icosapent ethyl)
drugs.mechanism: Long-chain polyunsaturated lipids acting as PPAR-alpha agonists, stimulating lipoprotein lipase to clear VLDL; the purified single-component product also lowers ApoC-III; antithrombotic (less TXA2, more prostacyclin).
drugs.adverseEffects: Bleeding and easy bruising, worse with aspirin, clopidogrel or anticoagulants; fishy aftertaste, belching and GI upset; the purified prescription product raises atrial fibrillation risk.

drugs.name: Phenytoin
drugs.mechanism: Antiseizure drug with Class Ib action: use-dependent block of inactivated Na+ channels that shortens the action potential; rarely used for arrhythmias today; induces hepatic CYP enzymes.
drugs.adverseEffects: Gingival overgrowth, hirsutism and nystagmus; ataxia at high levels; teratogenic; many interactions from CYP induction.

drugs.name: Pindolol / acebutolol
drugs.mechanism: Beta blockers with intrinsic sympathomimetic activity - partial agonists, one nonselective and one beta-1 selective: block catecholamine surges yet stimulate the receptor at rest, so resting heart rate falls little.
drugs.adverseEffects: Can worsen angina, post-MI ischemia and heart failure by raising cardiac workload - avoid in those patients; less resting bradycardia than other agents of the class.

drugs.name: Prasugrel
drugs.mechanism: Oral irreversible P2Y12 prodrug whose activation does not depend on CYP2C19, so platelet inhibition is faster, stronger and more consistent than with the 2C19-activated agent; ACS with PCI.
drugs.adverseEffects: More bleeding than the 2C19-activated agent; contraindicated after a prior stroke or TIA (intracranial bleeding) and generally avoided at age 75 or older.

drugs.name: Procainamide
drugs.mechanism: Class Ia: open-state Na+ block plus K+ block (QRS and QT both lengthen), with M2 and alpha-1 blockade; N-acetylated (phase II) to an active metabolite. Used for AF with an accessory pathway.
drugs.adverseEffects: Lupus-like syndrome (arthralgia, facial rash, antihistone antibodies) in slow acetylators; hypotension from alpha-1 block; QT prolongation and torsades.

drugs.name: Propranolol / nadolol / timolol
drugs.mechanism: Nonselective beta-1 and beta-2 antagonists without partial agonism or alpha block: slow SA/AV node and contractility, and block hepatic glycogenolysis and bronchial and vascular beta-2 relaxation; rate control in thyroid storm.
drugs.adverseEffects: Bronchospasm in asthma or COPD, hypoglycemia with blunted warning signs, worse claudication in PVD, bradycardia; overdose gives bradycardia, AV block, hypotension, low glucose - treat with glucagon.

drugs.name: Quinidine
drugs.mechanism: Class Ia cinchona alkaloid: blocks open Na+ channels (QRS widens) and K+ channels (QT lengthens) plus cardiac M2 receptors; also inhibits renal P-glycoprotein, raising digoxin levels.
drugs.adverseEffects: Tinnitus, headache and dizziness (like the antimalarial it comes from); antibody-mediated thrombocytopenia and hepatitis; QT prolongation with torsades; raises digoxin levels.

drugs.name: Ranolazine
drugs.mechanism: Blocks the late inward Na+ current in myocytes, so less Ca2+ enters via the Na+/Ca2+ exchanger and wall tension and O2 use fall without lowering heart rate or BP; chronic angina, not first line.
drugs.adverseEffects: QT prolongation (partial K+ channel block), constipation, nausea, dizziness; levels and QT risk rise with CYP3A inhibitors such as azole antifungals and grapefruit.

drugs.name: Sacubitril-valsartan
drugs.mechanism: Combination of a prodrug that inhibits neprilysin, so natriuretic peptides persist (natriuresis, vasodilation), with an AT1 receptor blocker; improves survival and cuts hospitalizations in HFrEF.
drugs.adverseEffects: Hypotension, hyperkalemia, renal dysfunction; angioedema - never start within 36 hours of an ACE inhibitor, because neprilysin also breaks down bradykinin.

drugs.name: Semaglutide
drugs.mechanism: GLP-1 receptor agonist: glucose-dependent insulin release, less glucagon, slower gastric emptying and central appetite suppression; the weight loss helps obesity-related HF (HFpEF).
drugs.adverseEffects: Nausea, vomiting, diarrhea; pancreatitis and gallbladder disease; thyroid C-cell tumor warning (avoid with medullary thyroid cancer or MEN2); hypoglycemia mainly with insulin or sulfonylureas.

drugs.name: SGLT2 inhibitors (dapagliflozin, empagliflozin, canagliflozin)
drugs.mechanism: Block Na+-glucose cotransport in the proximal tubule: glycosuria plus natriuresis and osmotic diuresis lower preload and afterload; cut HF hospitalization and CV death in HFrEF and HFpEF; A1c falls up to about 1%.
drugs.adverseEffects: UTIs and genital yeast infections (glucose in the urine), volume depletion, euglycemic ketoacidosis; avoid when creatinine clearance is below about 20-30 mL/min.

drugs.name: Sotalol
drugs.mechanism: Nonselective beta blocker (Class II) that also blocks delayed-rectifier K+ channels (Class III), prolonging the action potential and QT; renally cleared; used for atrial fibrillation.
drugs.adverseEffects: Dose-related QT prolongation and torsades, worst at slow rates, plus beta-2 effects - wheezing in COPD or asthma - and bradycardia; dose by renal function.

drugs.name: Spironolactone
drugs.mechanism: Steroidal competitive antagonist of the aldosterone (mineralocorticoid) receptor in collecting-duct principal cells that also blocks androgen receptors; used in HF, hyperaldosteronism, acne and hirsutism.
drugs.adverseEffects: Gynecomastia, impotence and menstrual changes (anti-androgen); hyperkalemia with metabolic acidosis, worse with ACEi/ARB, NSAIDs or K+ supplements - check K+ periodically.

drugs.name: Statins (atorvastatin, rosuvastatin, simvastatin, pravastatin)
drugs.mechanism: Competitive inhibitors of HMG-CoA reductase, the rate-limiting step of cholesterol synthesis; hepatocytes up-regulate LDL receptors and LDL falls 25% to 50% or more, dose-dependent; proven to cut cardiac deaths.
drugs.adverseEffects: Myalgia, myopathy and rhabdomyolysis (check CK; possible CoQ10 depletion), raised aminotransferases (stop if >3x ULN), slight glucose rise; levels rise with azoles, macrolides, grapefruit; no pregnancy.

drugs.name: Ticagrelor
drugs.mechanism: Oral, direct-acting (not a prodrug), reversible P2Y12 antagonist - needs no hepatic activation, so it still works when CYP2C19 is impaired; taken twice daily with aspirin after ACS or PCI.
drugs.adverseEffects: Bleeding (more than the 2C19-activated agent) and dyspnea; bradyarrhythmias and ventricular pauses; raised uric acid; costlier; high-dose aspirin blunts its benefit.

drugs.name: Ticlopidine
drugs.mechanism: The original oral ADP (P2Y12) receptor blocker: an irreversible prodrug, largely abandoned because of its blood-count toxicity.
drugs.adverseEffects: Neutropenia appearing weeks into therapy (sore throat, fever, flu-like illness) - needs CBC monitoring; also TTP and bleeding.

drugs.name: Trimetazidine
drugs.mechanism: Metabolic modulator: inhibits myocardial fatty-acid oxidation, shifting the ischemic heart to glucose oxidation (more ATP per O2 used); not approved in the US.
drugs.adverseEffects: New or worsened parkinsonian symptoms - tremor, rigidity, gait disturbance - the safety concern behind its lack of US approval.

drugs.name: Verapamil / diltiazem
drugs.mechanism: Class IV: L-type Ca2+ channel block in SA/AV node and myocardium as well as arterioles (one agent more cardiac than the other) - flatter phase 4, longer AV-nodal refractory period, less contractility.
drugs.adverseEffects: Bradycardia and AV block, hypotension without reflex tachycardia, constipation, raised digoxin levels; contraindicated in HFrEF and pre-excited AF; overdose raises glucose (IV calcium, insulin).

drugs.name: Vericiguat
drugs.mechanism: Oral stimulator of soluble guanylyl cyclase that raises cGMP independent of nitric oxide (and sensitizes the enzyme to NO); cuts HF hospitalization after a worsening episode of HFrEF.
drugs.adverseEffects: Hypotension, headache, dizziness, reflex tachycardia; never combine with NO donors or PDE5 inhibitors; no tolerance, so no drug-free interval is needed; embryo-fetal toxicity.

correlates.name: 22q11.2 deletion (DiGeorge) syndrome
correlates.presentation: A 3-day-old boy admitted for a murmur and mild cyanosis becomes jittery, then has a focal seizure. He has small low-set ears, a small jaw, wide-set eyes and an opening in the roof of his mouth. HR 160, SpO2 85%.
correlates.workup: Ca2+ 6.2 mg/dL, phosphate 8.0, PTH low; lymphocytes 900/uL with very few T cells; chest film: no thymic shadow above the heart; echo: a conotruncal (outflow-tract) defect.
correlates.management: IV calcium gluconate for the seizure, then oral calcium and calcitriol; irradiated, CMV-negative blood products only; hold live vaccines until T-cell function is known; repair the heart lesion surgically.

correlates.name: Abdominal aortic aneurysm
correlates.presentation: A 70-year-old man with 45 pack-years of smoking, whose brother had emergency vascular surgery at 68, feels well at his annual visit. BP 138/84, pulse 72. Deep palpation above the umbilicus finds a non-tender mass that pushes the examiner's fingers apart with each heartbeat.
correlates.workup: Screening ultrasound: infrarenal aorta 4.6 cm across (normal ~2 cm; >3 cm is abnormal), renal arteries spared. Repeat ultrasound 6 months later: 0.2 cm larger.
correlates.management: Stop smoking (the top modifiable risk factor); statin, antiplatelet and BP control; serial ultrasound. Elective endovascular or open repair at >5.5 cm in men (>5.0 cm in women) or growth >0.5 cm in 6 months or >1 cm per year.

correlates.name: Abetalipoproteinemia
correlates.presentation: 10-year-old boy with greasy, bulky, foul stools and poor growth since infancy now walks unsteadily on a wide base, has lost his ankle reflexes and his position and vibration sense, and cannot see well at dusk. Height and weight below the 3rd percentile; parents are first cousins.
correlates.workup: Total cholesterol 40, TG 10 mg/dL; no apoB-48 or apoB-100 - chylomicrons, VLDL, IDL and LDL all absent; smear: RBCs with irregular thorny projections; vitamin E very low, INR 1.6; duodenal biopsy: lipid-stuffed enterocytes.
correlates.management: Restrict long-chain fat and use medium-chain triglycerides (absorbed straight into portal blood); high-dose fat-soluble vitamins - vitamin E above all, plus A, D and K - to halt the nerve and retinal damage.

correlates.name: Accidental hypothermia
correlates.presentation: A 58-year-old man with alcohol use disorder is found asleep outdoors on a January night. Rectal temperature 29 C (84 F), pulse 38, BP 88/52, RR 8. He is confused, has stopped shivering, and his skin is cold and pale; pupils react sluggishly.
correlates.workup: ECG: slow rhythm with prolonged PR, QRS and QT and an extra upright deflection right at the end of each QRS, lifting the start of the ST segment, most obvious in the inferior and lateral leads. K+ 4.6 mEq/L, glucose 62 mg/dL.
correlates.management: Handle gently (rough movement can trigger VF); remove wet clothing; passive then active external rewarming, warmed IV fluids, and extracorporeal rewarming if in arrest; continue resuscitation until rewarmed.

correlates.name: ACE inhibitor angioedema
correlates.presentation: A 52-year-old Black man started on a new antihypertensive 3 weeks ago wakes with swelling of his lips and tongue that has grown over 2 hours; his voice is muffled but there is no stridor. No hives, itching or wheeze; BP 148/90, SpO2 97%. No prior episodes or family history.
correlates.workup: Non-pitting, non-itchy swelling of lips and tongue without urticaria; C4 normal, C1-esterase level and function normal; tryptase normal. Mechanism: bradykinin is no longer broken down.
correlates.management: Protect the airway first; stop the drug for good and switch to an ARB; icatibant (bradykinin B2 receptor blocker) can help; antihistamine, epinephrine and glucocorticoid as needed, though they work less well for bradykinin swelling.

correlates.name: ACE inhibitor cough
correlates.presentation: A 61-year-old woman started a new blood-pressure pill 6 weeks ago and since then has a persistent dry, tickling hack, worse at night, with no sputum, fever, postnasal drip, heartburn or wheeze. She has never smoked. Lungs clear; nose and throat normal.
correlates.workup: CXR normal; spirometry normal; no eosinophilia. The hacking stops within 1-4 weeks of withdrawing the drug and returns on rechallenge - bradykinin and substance P are no longer broken down.
correlates.management: Stop the drug and switch to an ARB, which blocks the AT1 receptor without touching ACE or bradykinin; antitussive syrups will not help.

correlates.name: Acute decompensated heart failure
correlates.presentation: A 74-year-old man with known EF 30% ate salty holiday meals and ran out of furosemide a week ago. Tonight he woke gasping and now sits bolt upright using his neck muscles. BP 172/98, HR 112, RR 32, SpO2 86%; warm hands; JVP 14 cm, crackles to mid-lung, S3, 3+ leg edema.
correlates.workup: BNP 1,850 pg/mL; troponin slightly up and flat; creatinine 1.5; Na+ 134. Chest film: enlarged heart, fluffy bilateral perihilar alveolar opacities, small effusions. ECG: sinus rhythm at 112, no new ST elevation.
correlates.management: Sit him up; oxygen or noninvasive positive-pressure ventilation; IV loop diuretic at or above the home dose; IV nitroglycerin while BP is high; find the trigger; restart and optimize guideline therapy once dry; follow-up within 7 days.

correlates.name: Acute infective endocarditis in a person who injects drugs
correlates.presentation: 31-year-old woman who uses heroin intravenously: 4 days of rigors, T 39.9 C, HR 124, BP 96/58, pleuritic chest pain. Holosystolic murmur at the left lower sternal border that grows louder on inspiration; large v waves in the neck veins; track marks on both forearms.
correlates.workup: Blood cultures 3/3: gram-positive cocci in clusters, coagulase-positive. TTE: 1.8 cm mobile mass on a tricuspid leaflet with severe regurgitation. CT chest: multiple peripheral nodules, several cavitating. WBC 18,500/uL.
correlates.management: Blood cultures before antibiotics, then IV vancomycin (switch to an anti-staphylococcal penicillin if methicillin-sensitive); surgery for persistent bacteremia, abscess or a large mobile mass; addiction treatment.

correlates.name: Acute limb ischemia
correlates.presentation: A 76-year-old woman with atrial fibrillation who stopped her anticoagulant 2 weeks ago has 3 hours of sudden severe right leg pain. The leg is pale and cold from mid-calf down, with a femoral but no popliteal or pedal pulse; toe sensation is dulled but she can still move them.
correlates.workup: Hand-held Doppler: no arterial signal from the popliteal artery down; venous signals present. ECG: no P waves, R-R intervals vary with no pattern. CT angiogram: abrupt popliteal cutoff at a pre-existing plaque with few collaterals.
correlates.management: Immediate IV unfractionated heparin; urgent imaging to choose catheter-directed tPA with mechanical thrombectomy vs surgical embolectomy - restore flow before paralysis (~6 h); long-term anticoagulation for the cardiac source.

correlates.name: Acute pericarditis
correlates.presentation: 29-year-old man, 10 days after a cold: 2 days of sharp retrosternal pain that worsens lying flat or breathing deeply, radiating to the left trapezius ridge. T 38.0 C, HR 104, BP 126/78; a scratchy, three-part sound at the left sternal border. No prior MI or heart surgery.
correlates.workup: ECG: concave ST elevation in I, II, aVL, aVF and V2-V6 with PR depression (PR elevation in aVR) and no reciprocal ST depression. Troponin normal; CRP 48 mg/L; echo: small effusion, normal wall motion.
correlates.management: High-dose NSAID (ibuprofen or aspirin) plus colchicine for 3 months to cut recurrence; limit strenuous exercise; avoid anticoagulants; admit if the effusion is large, temperature is high or troponin rises.

correlates.name: Acute pulmonary embolism, hemodynamically stable
correlates.presentation: 58-year-old woman 6 days after a knee replacement: sudden breathlessness and sharp right chest pain on deep breaths; anxious. Temp 37.8 C, HR 112, RR 26, BP 132/80, SpO2 91% on room air; lungs mostly clear; left calf larger than right.
correlates.workup: ABG: PaO2 62, PaCO2 31, wide A-a gradient; ECG: sinus tachycardia with nonspecific ST-T changes; CT angiogram: filling defects in right lower-lobe segmental arteries; RV normal size; troponin normal.
correlates.management: Anticoagulate now - LMWH or a factor Xa inhibitor (rivaroxaban, apixaban) for at least 3 months; no thrombolysis while normotensive; IVC filter only if anticoagulation is contraindicated; image the legs for the source.

correlates.name: Acute respiratory distress syndrome
correlates.presentation: A 46-year-old man admitted 2 days ago with severe gallstone pancreatitis becomes rapidly breathless and blue. RR 36, HR 122, BP 104/66, SpO2 84% on a 15-L non-rebreather; diffuse crackles in both lungs; JVP not raised, no S3, no leg edema.
correlates.workup: ABG on FiO2 1.0: PaO2 80 mmHg (PaO2/FiO2 80), PaCO2 50, pH 7.28. Chest film: diffuse bilateral alveolar opacities, normal heart size. Echo: normal LV function; wedge pressure 12 mmHg; BNP 60 pg/mL.
correlates.management: Treat the cause; intubate with low tidal volumes (6 mL/kg ideal weight), plateau pressure below 30 and adequate PEEP; prone positioning when PaO2/FiO2 is below 150; conservative fluids once shock resolves.

correlates.name: Acute rheumatic fever
correlates.presentation: 10-year-old boy recently arrived from Nepal had an untested sore throat 3 weeks ago. Now T 38.6 C and painful hot swelling that moved from right knee to left ankle to right wrist over 5 days, each joint settling as the next flared, and a new apical holosystolic murmur.
correlates.workup: ASO 960 Todd units, anti-DNase B raised; ESR 96 mm/h, CRP 11 mg/dL; ECG: PR 0.24 s; echo: mitral regurgitation with thickened leaflets. Throat culture now grows nothing.
correlates.management: Penicillin to eradicate the organism; acetaminophen until the diagnosis is secure, then high-dose aspirin or NSAIDs (steroids for severe carditis); then long-term monthly IM benzathine penicillin prophylaxis.

correlates.name: Alcoholic cardiomyopathy
correlates.presentation: A 48-year-old man who has drunk about 12 beers a day for 20 years has 2 months of worsening exertional breathlessness, orthopnea and leg swelling; no chest pain ever. BP 128/84, HR 108; JVP 12 cm, S3, apex displaced to the anterior axillary line; reddened palms.
correlates.workup: Echo: dilated left ventricle with global hypokinesis, EF 25%. Coronary angiogram: normal. MCV 104 fL, GGT 310 U/L, AST 112 with ALT 48; thiamine low-normal.
correlates.management: Complete abstinence - ventricular function often recovers; guideline reduced-EF therapy (ACE inhibitor or ARNI, beta blocker, MRA, SGLT2 inhibitor, diuretic); give thiamine, since its deficiency causes an indistinguishable dilated heart.

correlates.name: Allergic bronchopulmonary aspergillosis
correlates.presentation: 34-year-old man with asthma since childhood, poorly controlled for 6 months despite inhaled steroids: wheeze, low-grade fevers, and he coughs up firm brownish plugs. T 37.9 C, SpO2 94%; scattered wheeze and crackles whose location changes from one visit to the next.
correlates.workup: Eosinophils 1,600/uL; total IgE 2,800 IU/mL; immediate skin reaction and precipitating IgG to a heat-tolerant mold; plugs hold septate hyphae branching at acute angles. CT: dilated, mucus-filled central bronchi; infiltrates come and go.
correlates.management: Oral prednisone tapered over months plus itraconazole to cut the fungal load; follow total IgE to judge response and catch relapse; keep optimizing the asthma regimen; anti-IgE or anti-IL-5 antibody if steroid-dependent.

correlates.name: Allergic rhinitis with postnasal drip
correlates.presentation: A 62-year-old woman who never smoked has 2 weeks of dry cough, worse at night, with a stuffy, runny nose and constant throat clearing; an over-the-counter antihistamine helped. Afebrile, RR 14, SpO2 98%; normal vesicular breath sounds; mucus streaking down the back of the throat.
correlates.workup: Clinical diagnosis - no imaging needed. Lungs and peak flow normal. Nose: pale, swollen turbinates with clear discharge; back of the throat studded with raised lymphoid bumps. She takes no blood-pressure medicine.
correlates.management: Intranasal corticosteroid plus a second-generation antihistamine; avoid the trigger allergen; saline nasal rinses; reassess if the cough lasts beyond 8 weeks.

correlates.name: Alpha-1 antitrypsin deficiency
correlates.presentation: 45-year-old woman who has never smoked: 6 years of slowly worsening breathlessness that now limits housework; her brother needed a lung transplant at 50. Afebrile, BP 122/76, SpO2 92%; hyperresonant chest, faint breath sounds at both bases, prolonged expiration, liver edge firm.
correlates.workup: FEV1/FVC 0.50, no change after albuterol; DLCO 45%. CT: uniform destruction of whole lobules, worst in the lower lobes. Serum elastase-inhibitor level 25 mg/dL (low); Pi typing ZZ. ALT 84; liver biopsy: PAS-positive globules in hepatocytes.
correlates.management: Check the inhibitor level and Pi type, and test siblings; strict smoke avoidance; standard bronchodilators and vaccines; IV augmentation with pooled human inhibitor if FEV1 is under 65%; watch the liver; transplant when end-stage.

correlates.name: Amaurosis fugax (transient monocular blindness)
correlates.presentation: A 72-year-old man who smokes had 5 minutes in which the vision in his right eye went dark and then fully returned. The left eye was normal throughout, and he had no weakness, numbness or speech trouble. A bruit is heard over the right carotid.
correlates.workup: Fundus: a bright yellow refractile plaque lodged at a retinal arteriole branch point; otherwise normal. Carotid duplex: ~75% narrowing of the right internal carotid (peak systolic velocity 250 cm/s), on the same side as the affected eye.
correlates.management: Antiplatelet therapy and a statin; endarterectomy of the same-side internal carotid for a symptomatic high-grade lesion; smoking cessation. Urgent work-up, because the next embolus may reach the brain.

correlates.name: Amiodarone pulmonary toxicity
correlates.presentation: A 71-year-old former smoker started a long-half-life antiarrhythmic after an arrest from VT 14 months ago. He now has 2 months of dry cough, exertional breathlessness and low-grade fever. SpO2 91% on room air; fine bibasilar crackles; no JVD or leg edema.
correlates.workup: CT: bilateral peripheral reticular and ground-glass opacities. PFTs restrictive, DLCO 45% predicted. BNP 60 pg/mL; EF unchanged at 40%. Biopsy: interstitial inflammation with type II pneumocyte hyperplasia.
correlates.management: Stop the drug (it lingers for months) and give glucocorticoids; switch to another antiarrhythmic. Prevention: baseline and yearly chest X-ray, PFTs in some, extra caution in smokers.

correlates.name: Amiodarone-induced hypothyroidism
correlates.presentation: A 69-year-old woman started on an iodinated antiarrhythmic after a VF arrest 8 months ago now has fatigue, 5 kg weight gain, constipation, dry skin, thinning hair and constant chilliness. Pulse 54, BP 128/84; ankle reflexes relax slowly.
correlates.workup: TSH 18 mIU/L, free T4 0.6 ng/dL, T3 low with reverse T3 high (blocked T4-to-T3 conversion); ALT mildly raised; slit lamp: fine whorled corneal deposits.
correlates.management: Levothyroxine replacement; the antiarrhythmic can usually be continued if still needed; check a thyroid panel and LFTs at baseline and periodically while on it.

correlates.name: Aortic regurgitation
correlates.presentation: A 52-year-old man has a year of breathlessness lying flat and waking at night gasping. BP 168/48, pulse 88; apical impulse broad and displaced left. A soft, high-pitched early diastolic decrescendo murmur at the left sternal border is loudest leaning forward in expiration.
correlates.workup: Echo: diastolic backflow jet from a three-cusp valve into the LV; root 4.2 cm; LV end-diastolic diameter 7.0 cm (eccentric hypertrophy), EF 50%. The murmur grows louder with handgrip and softer on inspiration; an S3 is present.
correlates.management: Afterload reduction (ACE inhibitor, ARB or dihydropyridine) for hypertension and symptoms; valve replacement when symptomatic, EF <55% or LV end-systolic diameter >5 cm; repair the root if dilated.

correlates.name: Aortoiliac occlusive disease (Leriche syndrome)
correlates.presentation: A 58-year-old man with 40 pack-years of smoking has a year of aching in both buttocks, hips and thighs after 2 blocks of walking that resolves within minutes of standing still. Femoral pulses are faint on both sides, pedal pulses absent; both legs are cool with sparse hair.
correlates.workup: Ankle-brachial ratio 0.60 right and 0.55 left. CT angiogram: occlusion of the infrarenal aorta extending into both common iliac arteries, with large lumbar and epigastric collaterals.
correlates.management: Risk-factor control, statin, antiplatelet and supervised exercise; for disabling symptoms, endovascular stenting of the distal aorta and both iliacs or aortobifemoral bypass.

correlates.name: Arrhythmogenic right ventricular cardiomyopathy (incl. Naxos)
correlates.presentation: A 24-year-old man collapses playing soccer and is revived with one shock; for a year exercise has brought on palpitations and a pounding heart. A cousin died suddenly at 30. Since childhood the skin of his palms and soles has been thick and hard. BP 118/74; heart exam normal.
correlates.workup: ECG: T-wave inversion V1-V3, a small notch at the very end of the QRS in V1; monitored VT with left bundle branch block shape and superior axis. MRI: thin, enlarged, poorly moving right ventricle with fatty replacement; LV near normal.
correlates.management: ICD (the usual treatment); no competitive or endurance exercise; beta blocker or an antiarrhythmic (sotalol, amiodarone) and catheter ablation for recurrent VT; screen first-degree relatives.

correlates.name: Aspirin-exacerbated respiratory disease
correlates.presentation: 38-year-old woman whose wheeze began at 30, with years of blocked nose and no sense of smell. 40 minutes after ibuprofen for a sprained ankle: wheeze, chest tightness, flushed face, red eyes, itchy welts on her trunk. RR 26, SpO2 93%; pale, glistening masses in both nostrils.
correlates.workup: Eosinophils 900/uL; skin tests to aeroallergens negative; urine leukotriene E4 high. CT: every sinus opacified, with polyps. FEV1 rises 18% after albuterol. A supervised oral challenge with a COX-1 inhibitor reproduces the attack.
correlates.management: Treat the attack like any asthma flare; then avoid all COX-1-blocking NSAIDs (acetaminophen under 1 g or celecoxib is usually safe); leukotriene modifier (montelukast, zileuton); nasal steroids, polyp surgery; desensitize if needed.

correlates.name: Atrial fibrillation
correlates.presentation: A 72-year-old woman with hypertension and diabetes who drinks 3-4 glasses of wine nightly has a week of palpitations and fatigue. Pulse 128 and irregular, apical rate higher than radial, BP 136/82. Two months ago she had a brief spell of left arm weakness.
correlates.workup: ECG: narrow QRS at 128/min with no discernible P waves, a fine chaotic baseline, and R-R intervals that vary beat to beat with no repeating pattern; PR unmeasurable. TSH normal. Echo: left atrium 4.6 cm.
correlates.management: Rate control first (metoprolol or diltiazem; digoxin add-on) or rhythm control (amiodarone, sotalol, flecainide); anticoagulate (DOAC or warfarin) for CHA2DS2-VASc >=2; DC cardioversion if unstable; pulmonary vein isolation is definitive.

correlates.name: Atrial flutter
correlates.presentation: A 67-year-old man with COPD and hypertension has 2 days of palpitations and mild breathlessness. Pulse 150 and regular, BP 128/80; the rate does not drift with rest or fluids. Carotid sinus massage drops the rate abruptly to 75 for a few seconds, then it returns to 150.
correlates.workup: ECG: regular narrow QRS at 150/min; between complexes the baseline is replaced by continuous, uniform negative deflections at 300/min, best seen in II, III and aVF, with no flat segment between them (2:1 conduction).
correlates.management: Rate is hard to control with drugs; anticoagulate by the same stroke-risk score used for fibrillation; synchronized cardioversion if unstable; cure = catheter ablation of the cavotricuspid isthmus.

correlates.name: Atrial septal defect
correlates.presentation: A 6-year-old girl sent by her school nurse feels well but is at the 10th percentile for weight and tires before her friends. Soft 2/6 systolic ejection murmur at the left upper sternal border, low mid-diastolic rumble at the lower left border; S2 split wide in both breath phases.
correlates.workup: ECG: right axis deviation, rsR' in V1. Chest film: enlarged right heart, prominent pulmonary arteries, more lung markings. Echo: 14-mm opening mid-wall between the upper chambers, left-to-right flow, dilated right atrium and ventricle.
correlates.management: Small openings: watch and wait - many close on their own. Significant shunt, right-heart enlargement or poor growth: transcatheter device closure or surgery.

correlates.name: AV nodal reentrant tachycardia
correlates.presentation: A 28-year-old woman has had episodes of pounding palpitations for 2 years that start and stop abruptly, with lightheadedness; between attacks she feels well. Now: pulse 186 and regular, BP 108/70, alert and oriented.
correlates.workup: ECG: regular narrow QRS at 186/min, no P wave before the QRS, a small retrograde deflection at the end of each QRS. ECG between attacks normal (PR 160 ms, no pre-excitation). EP study: dual pathways within the AV node.
correlates.management: Vagal maneuvers (Valsalva, carotid massage), then rapid IV adenosine 6 mg; synchronized cardioversion if unstable; long term, catheter ablation of the slow pathway (fast-pathway ablation risks AV block).

correlates.name: Bartter syndrome
correlates.presentation: A 3-year-old boy, born at 33 weeks after a pregnancy with excess amniotic fluid, has poor weight gain (below the 3rd percentile), large urine volumes with constant thirst, and salt craving. BP 88/50; no vomiting, no diuretic exposure.
correlates.workup: K+ 2.6 mEq/L, HCO3- 32, Mg2+ 1.7 (low-normal); urine Cl- 80 mEq/L; urine calcium high (Ca/creatinine 0.6); ultrasound: calcium deposits in both renal medullas; renin and aldosterone high; urine diuretic screen negative.
correlates.management: Potassium chloride and salt supplements; an NSAID such as indomethacin to blunt the excess renal prostaglandin output; potassium-sparing diuretic; follow growth.

correlates.name: Beta blocker overdose
correlates.presentation: 16-year-old girl brought in 2 h after swallowing a handful of her grandmother's blood-pressure pills; drowsy, wheezing and short of breath. HR 45, BP 90/60, RR 24, SpO2 94%; diffuse expiratory wheezes; normal pupils. Fingerstick glucose 55.
correlates.workup: ECG: sinus bradycardia at 45 with PR 240 ms (first-degree AV block) and a narrow QRS; glucose 55 mg/dL (hepatic glycogen breakdown blocked); K+ 5.0; digoxin level undetectable; acetaminophen and aspirin screens negative.
correlates.management: IV glucagon bolus then infusion (raises cAMP downstream of the blocked receptor); atropine, IV fluids and dextrose; high-dose insulin with dextrose and catecholamines if refractory; pacing; inhaled bronchodilator for the wheeze.

correlates.name: Bicuspid aortic valve
correlates.presentation: A 46-year-old man has a year of exertional breathlessness; his father had the same murmur. BP 134/80 in the arm and 140/84 in the legs. A sharp early systolic click is followed by a crescendo-decrescendo murmur at the right 2nd intercostal space radiating to the carotids.
correlates.workup: Echo: two unequal cusps, the larger with a midline raphe where calcium is heaviest; orifice area 1.1 cm2; ascending aorta dilated to 4.6 cm. Familial cases: NOTCH1 variant.
correlates.management: Serial echo of the leaflets and ascending aorta; replacement when severe and symptomatic - usually in the 40s-50s, ~30 years earlier than with three normal cusps; repair the ascending aorta if enlarged; echo-screen first-degree relatives.

correlates.name: Bronchiectasis
correlates.presentation: 52-year-old woman who had a necrotizing pneumonia at age 6: 10 years of daily cough bringing up cupfuls of foul yellow-green sputum, worst on rising, repeated chest infections, blood-streaked sputum twice this month. Afebrile; clubbed fingers; coarse crackles at both bases.
correlates.workup: CT: lower-lobe bronchi wider than their companion artery, not tapering, seen within 1 cm of the pleura; thick walls, some mucus-filled. Sputum: H. influenzae, later Pseudomonas. Sweat chloride 22 mmol/L; eosinophils and IgE normal.
correlates.management: Daily airway clearance (chest percussion, postural drainage); culture-guided antibiotics for flares, long-term macrolide if 3 or more a year; vaccines; bronchial artery embolization for major bleeding; resect a localized segment.

correlates.name: Bronchiolitis
correlates.presentation: 4-month-old girl in February, born at 35 weeks, sharing a room with a 9-month-old cousin: 3 days of cough and runny nose, now feeding poorly, breathing fast. T 37.9 C, HR 166, RR 48, SpO2 90%; nasal flaring, retractions, diffuse wheeze and crackles. Her first wheeze.
correlates.workup: Nasal swab PCR: RSV. Chest film usually unnecessary; if taken: hyperinflation, flat diaphragms, peribronchial thickening, no lobar opacity. No personal or family atopy.
correlates.management: Supportive: nasal suctioning, hydration, oxygen if SpO2 is below 90%, high-flow if tiring; avoid bronchodilators, corticosteroids and antibiotics; nirsevimab before the next RSV season for at-risk infants.

correlates.name: Brugada syndrome
correlates.presentation: A 35-year-old man who moved from Thailand 2 years ago faints at home while febrile (39.2 C) with influenza and wakes within a minute. He has no chest pain and takes no drugs. BP 122/78, pulse 96, SpO2 98%; heart and lungs normal on exam.
correlates.workup: ECG: in V1-V2 (faintly V3) only, a high take-off 3-mm ST elevation sloping straight down into an inverted T wave, with an rSR'-like pattern; no reciprocal depression; less marked once afebrile. Troponin normal; echo structurally normal.
correlates.management: Treat fever promptly; ICD for patients with syncope or arrest; avoid sodium-channel blockers (procainamide, flecainide, propafenone), tricyclics, lithium, bupivacaine, propofol, cocaine and heavy alcohol.

correlates.name: Calcific aortic stenosis
correlates.presentation: A 78-year-old man has 6 months of exertional chest pressure and fainted once while gardening. BP 124/94. A harsh crescendo-decrescendo systolic murmur at the right 2nd intercostal space radiates to both carotids and softens with Valsalva; an S4 is heard.
