correlates.workup: Echo: heavily calcified three-cusp valve with nodules in the sinuses and no commissural fusion; valve area 0.8 cm2, mean gradient 46 mmHg; concentric LV hypertrophy, EF 60%. ECG: high precordial voltage.
correlates.management: Symptomatic severe disease = valve replacement (surgical or transcatheter); no drug alters the course; avoid vasodilators and volume depletion that cut preload.

correlates.name: Calcium channel blocker overdose
correlates.presentation: 58-year-old woman found drowsy 3 h after swallowing a handful of her husband's extended-release pills for BP and heart-rate control. HR 42, BP 70/40, RR 16, SpO2 97%; lungs clear, no wheeze; warm, dry skin. Fingerstick glucose 310; she does not have diabetes.
correlates.workup: ECG: sinus bradycardia with PR 280 ms sliding into a junctional rhythm, narrow QRS, normal QTc; glucose 310 mg/dL (insulin release from islet cells blocked); K+ 4.2; lactate 4; digoxin level undetectable.
correlates.management: IV fluids and atropine; IV Ca2+ (chloride or gluconate); high-dose insulin with dextrose; vasopressors; glucagon may help; pacing, lipid emulsion or ECMO if refractory; whole-bowel irrigation for extended-release pills.

correlates.name: Cardiac amyloidosis
correlates.presentation: A 78-year-old man who had surgery for numb hands on both sides 6 years ago now has 8 months of breathlessness, leg swelling and lightheadedness on standing; his BP pills were stopped as his pressure fell. BP 98/62 lying, 80/54 standing; JVP 12 cm; soft S3, no murmur.
correlates.workup: ECG: low QRS voltage in limb leads, yet echo shows a 17-mm septum and 16-mm posterior wall; EF 50%, big atria, stiff filling. Pyrophosphate scan: intense heart uptake; free light chains normal. Biopsy: Congo red-positive, birefringent.
correlates.management: Tafamidis (stabilizes the misfolding transport protein); careful diuretics; avoid digoxin and nondihydropyridine calcium channel blockers; anticoagulate any AF; pacemaker for conduction disease.

correlates.name: Cardiac fibroma (Gorlin syndrome)
correlates.presentation: 12-year-old boy who has had three basal cell carcinomas excised from his face and back and jaw cysts removed at age 10, with a large head: he collapses while playing soccer. HR 170 on arrival.
correlates.workup: ECG: monomorphic ventricular tachycardia. CMR: single 4 cm solid, non-contractile mass inside the LV free wall with central calcification and uniform late gadolinium enhancement. Germline PTCH1 mutation (chromosome 9q).
correlates.management: Surgical resection if it causes arrhythmia or obstruction (it does not regress); ICD or antiarrhythmic drug if unresectable; dermatologic surveillance, strict sun protection and avoidance of radiotherapy.

correlates.name: Cardiac myxoma
correlates.presentation: 44-year-old woman: 3 months of dyspnea that worsens when she stands and eases lying down, two near-faints on standing, 5 kg weight loss, T 37.9 C, aching joints. Apical diastolic rumble that is louder sitting up and fades lying flat; no rheumatic fever history.
correlates.workup: Echo: 5 cm mobile left atrial mass on a stalk attached to the septum near the fossa ovalis, prolapsing into the mitral orifice in diastole. ESR 68 mm/h, Hb 10.8 g/dL, IL-6 high. Biopsy: stellate cells in a loose mucopolysaccharide matrix.
correlates.management: Prompt surgical excision with its septal attachment (risk of embolism and sudden obstruction); PRKAR1A testing and screening of relatives (Carney complex) if skin pigmentation, endocrine overactivity or recurrence.

correlates.name: Cardiac rhabdomyoma (tuberous sclerosis)
correlates.presentation: 5-month-old boy with clusters of sudden flexion jerks of the trunk and arms on waking, three oval pale patches on his back, and a soft systolic murmur. A prenatal ultrasound had shown masses inside the heart.
correlates.workup: Echo: multiple well-circumscribed bright nodules in both ventricular walls and the septum, no outflow obstruction. EEG: chaotic high-voltage slowing with multifocal spikes. MRI: cortical tubers, subependymal nodules.
correlates.management: Observe with serial echo - most regress during infancy; treat arrhythmia medically; surgery only for outflow obstruction; mTOR inhibitor (everolimus) for complications; TSC1/TSC2 testing and kidney imaging.

correlates.name: Cardiac tamponade
correlates.presentation: 61-year-old woman with metastatic lung adenocarcinoma: a week of worsening breathlessness and dull chest fullness, now lightheaded and sweaty. BP 84/62, HR 128, RR 26, SpO2 96% on room air; neck veins distended to the jaw; lungs clear; no leg swelling, no recent MI or procedure.
correlates.workup: ECG: sinus tachycardia with low-voltage QRS. CXR: enlarged cardiac silhouette, clear lung fields. Echo: large circumferential effusion, right atrial and right ventricular collapse in diastole, plethoric IVC that does not narrow.
correlates.management: Emergent echo-guided pericardiocentesis; IV fluid bolus while preparing; avoid diuretics, nitrates and positive-pressure ventilation where possible; send fluid for cytology; pericardial window if it recurs.

correlates.name: Cardiogenic shock
correlates.presentation: 64-year-old man 6 hours into a large anterior STEMI: confused, with cold, clammy gray skin, mottled knees and urine output 10 mL/h. BP 76/50 despite a 500 mL fluid bolus, HR 122, RR 30, SpO2 88%; JVP 10 cm; crackles over both lower lung halves; S3.
correlates.workup: Lactate 5.8, creatinine rising; echo: anterior and apical akinesis, EF 20% (over 40% of the LV lost), no new murmur, no effusion, normal RV; PA catheter: PCWP 28 mmHg, cardiac index 1.5 L/min/m2, high SVR.
correlates.management: Emergent revascularization of the culprit artery (PCI); norepinephrine for pressure plus dobutamine for contractility; mechanical support (intra-aortic balloon pump, Impella, ECMO) if needed; no beta blockers or nitrates while hypotensive.

correlates.name: Catecholaminergic polymorphic VT
correlates.presentation: A 10-year-old boy has fainted three times - twice while running in soccer matches and once when a dog frightened him. A cousin died suddenly during a race at 12. Between events his exam, BP and pulse are normal; he takes no medications.
correlates.workup: Resting ECG normal (QTc 420 ms); echo and cardiac MRI normal. Treadmill test: ventricular ectopy appears above ~120/min and escalates to runs of wide complexes whose axis flips beat to beat. Genetics: RyR2 variant.
correlates.management: Beta blocker (nadolol) to blunt the adrenergic trigger; add flecainide, which also blocks the leaky ryanodine receptor, if events persist; restrict strenuous exercise; ICD for recurrence despite drugs.

correlates.name: Central diabetes insipidus
correlates.presentation: A 34-year-old woman, 2 days after transsphenoidal removal of a pituitary tumor, passes 7 L of pale urine a day and wakes hourly to drink ice water. BP 118/72, HR 92; mucosa dry after a period kept NPO; no history of high blood sugar.
correlates.workup: Na+ 149 mEq/L, serum osm 305, urine osm 120 mOsm/kg, specific gravity 1.002; glucose 96. Fluid restriction: urine osm stays below 150 as Na+ rises. After desmopressin, urine osm climbs to 600 (more than doubles).
correlates.management: Desmopressin (intranasal or oral) - the test is also the treatment; free access to fluids; follow Na+, which can fall too low if she keeps drinking heavily on desmopressin.

correlates.name: Centriacinar emphysema
correlates.presentation: 62-year-old man, 45 pack-years, seen in clinic: 4 years of steadily worsening breathlessness, now after 1 flight of stairs; little cough or sputum; 6 kg weight loss over 2 years. BMI 19, RR 22, SpO2 95% on room air; hyperresonant chest, faint breath sounds; no edema or cyanosis.
correlates.workup: FEV1/FVC 0.55, no reversal; TLC 125%, RV 180%; DLCO 38%. ABG: pH 7.45, PaCO2 33, PaO2 72 mmHg. Hct 44%. CXR: hyperlucent lungs worst in the upper lobes, flat diaphragms, narrow vertical heart. Serum elastase-inhibitor level normal.
correlates.management: Stop smoking (the only step that slows decline); long-acting bronchodilators; pulmonary rehab and vaccines; lung-volume-reduction surgery or bullectomy for upper-lobe disease with poor exercise tolerance; transplant if end-stage.

correlates.name: Chagas cardiomyopathy
correlates.presentation: 49-year-old man raised in an adobe house in rural Bolivia: a year of exertional dyspnea, palpitations and one faint, plus long-standing trouble swallowing and bowel movements only every 10 days. JVP 10 cm, an S3, ankle edema.
correlates.workup: ECG: right bundle branch block plus left anterior fascicular block, multiform PVCs. Echo: dilated LV, EF 30%, thin apical aneurysm with thrombus; coronaries normal. Serology positive on two assays; barium: dilated aperistaltic esophagus.
correlates.management: Guideline heart-failure therapy (ACE inhibitor or ARNI, beta blocker, MRA); anticoagulate for the apical thrombus; amiodarone or ICD for ventricular arrhythmia; antiparasitic drugs cannot undo established damage; transplant if refractory.

correlates.name: CHARGE syndrome
correlates.presentation: Term newborn boy who turns blue while feeding and pinks up when he cries. Gaps in the lower iris of both eyes, small cup-shaped low ears, failed newborn hearing screen, very small penis, and a loud systolic murmur.
correlates.workup: CT: bony-membranous blockage at the back of both nasal passages. Echo: conotruncal defect. Retinal exam: gaps in the retina and optic disc. Calcium normal, thymus present; FISH for 22q11.2 negative. Sequencing: pathogenic CHD7 variant.
correlates.management: Oral airway first (newborns breathe through the nose), then surgical opening of the nasal passages; repair the heart defect; hearing aids and vision follow-up; counsel 50% recurrence if a parent is affected, otherwise under 1-5%.

correlates.name: Cholesterol gallstones
correlates.presentation: 41-year-old woman, BMI 34, who lost 12 kg on a very-low-calorie diet this year: 4 episodes in 2 months of steady right upper-abdominal pain 1-2 h after fatty meals, lasting 2-3 h, with nausea, spreading to the right shoulder blade. Afebrile, mild RUQ tenderness, no jaundice.
correlates.workup: Ultrasound: several mobile echogenic foci in the gallbladder casting acoustic shadows; normal wall; bile duct not dilated; LFTs, lipase and WBC normal. Stones are yellow - bile held more sterol than its bile salts and lecithin could carry.
correlates.management: Elective laparoscopic cholecystectomy for symptomatic stones; smaller low-fat meals meanwhile; ursodeoxycholic acid only for poor surgical candidates; note fibrates add the same risk by cutting bile acid synthesis.

correlates.name: Chronic bronchitis
correlates.presentation: 58-year-old woman, 50 pack-years, 20 years in a textile mill: cough with grey-white sputum most mornings at least 3 months a year for 5 years; three chest infections needing antibiotics in 2 years; breathless only lately. SpO2 86% at rest; rhonchi and wheeze; mild ankle edema.
correlates.workup: ABG: pH 7.36, PaCO2 54, HCO3- 30, PaO2 52 mmHg. Hct 56%. FEV1/FVC 0.62, no reversal; DLCO normal. Echo: dilated right ventricle, PA systolic 50 mmHg. Histology: mucous glands fill 70% of the bronchial wall; goblet-cell-rich bronchioles.
correlates.management: Stop smoking; oxygen at least 15 h/day (PaO2 55 or less, or 59 with Hct above 55% or right heart strain); long-acting bronchodilators, inhaled steroid if flares are frequent; pulmonary rehab, vaccines; antibiotics for infective flares.

correlates.name: Chronic limb-threatening ischemia
correlates.presentation: A 74-year-old man with diabetes and 50 pack-years of smoking has 2 months of right forefoot pain that wakes him at night and eases when he hangs the foot over the side of the bed. The foot is cool, thin-skinned and hairless with a dry black tip on the second toe; no pedal pulses.
correlates.workup: Ankle-brachial ratio 0.28 on the right; toe pressure 20 mmHg. CT angiogram: multilevel occlusion of the superficial femoral and tibial arteries with collaterals. Toe wound dry, necrotic and sharply demarcated.
correlates.management: Revascularization (angioplasty/stenting or surgical bypass) plus wound care; continue statin, antiplatelet and smoking cessation; amputation if unsalvageable - at 1 year about 25% lose the leg and 25% die of cardiovascular causes.

correlates.name: Chronic mitral regurgitation
correlates.presentation: A 61-year-old man has 2 years of exertional fatigue and now needs 3 pillows to sleep. Pulse 92 and irregular. A high-pitched blowing holosystolic murmur at the apex radiates to the left axilla and buries S1; it gets louder with handgrip and does not get louder with inspiration.
correlates.workup: Echo: systolic backflow jet into an enlarged left atrium (5.2 cm) through leaflets that fail to meet on a dilated annulus; LV dilated, EF 58%; pulmonary artery systolic pressure 50 mmHg. Bibasilar crackles on chest exam.
correlates.management: Surgical repair (preferred over replacement) once symptomatic or when EF falls to <=60% or LV end-systolic diameter reaches >=4 cm; diuretics for congestion; rate control and anticoagulation for the irregular rhythm.

correlates.name: Chronic respiratory acidosis from CO2 retention
correlates.presentation: 60-year-old man with ALS diagnosed 2 years ago: months of morning headaches, broken sleep, daytime sleepiness and a weak cough; no change this week. RR 22 with shallow breaths, SpO2 89% on room air, neck muscles working, lungs clear, no wheeze, BMI 23.
correlates.workup: ABG pH 7.32, PCO2 62, HCO3- 31 - HCO3- up ~7 for a 22 mmHg PCO2 rise (~0.3 per mmHg); Cl- 96; urine NH4+ high; FVC 45% predicted; chest x-ray clear.
correlates.management: Nocturnal bilevel noninvasive positive-pressure ventilation; avoid opioids, benzodiazepines and high-flow O2 (target SpO2 88-92%); lower PCO2 gradually - fast correction leaves a post-hypercapnic metabolic alkalosis.

correlates.name: Chronic venous insufficiency
correlates.presentation: A 58-year-old cashier (BMI 34) who stands all day has years of heavy, aching legs that swell by evening and ease with elevation; no prior clot. Both shins have dilated tortuous veins and brown, thick, itchy skin, and a shallow weeping ulcer sits above the right medial malleolus.
correlates.workup: Ankle-brachial ratio 1.05. Venous duplex: reflux lasting >0.5 s through incompetent great saphenous and perforator valves on both sides; deep veins compress fully with no old thrombus and no iliac compression.
correlates.management: Compression stockings, leg elevation, walking to work the calf pump, weight loss and NSAIDs for pain; wound care for the ulcer; sclerotherapy or endovenous ablation for refractory varicosities.

correlates.name: Coarctation of the aorta
correlates.presentation: A 14-year-old boy at a sports physical has BP 162/94 in the right arm and 104/70 in the leg, and gets calf cramps when running. Femoral pulses are weak and arrive later than the radial pulse; a systolic murmur is heard over the left back between the shoulder blades.
correlates.workup: Chest film: notches on the undersides of posterior ribs 4-8. ECG: left ventricular hypertrophy. MRI: discrete narrowing of the descending thoracic arterial trunk just past the left subclavian origin, with large intercostal collaterals.
correlates.management: Refer to cardiology whenever femoral pulses are weak or absent; balloon angioplasty with stent or surgical resection; long-term BP control and surveillance for re-narrowing and aneurysm; a duct-dependent newborn gets prostaglandin E1 first.

correlates.name: Community-acquired pneumonia in a child
correlates.presentation: 9-year-old boy with known moderate persistent wheeze: 2 days of T 39.2 C, shaking chills and a wet cough. Pale, sweaty, capillary refill 3 s, RR 32, SpO2 93%. Over the right lower back: dullness to percussion, louder voice transmission, crackles and rhonchi.
correlates.workup: CXR: dense right lower lobe opacity with air bronchograms and no hyperinflation; WBC 21,000/uL, CRP 14 mg/dL. Ultrasound: small parapneumonic effusion. Blood culture drawn before antibiotics.
correlates.management: Age-directed empiric antibiotics (high-dose amoxicillin for a lobar picture; add a macrolide for atypical features at school age); admit if hypoxic; thoracentesis if the effusion grows; watch for a triggered wheeze flare.

correlates.name: Complete atrioventricular canal defect
correlates.presentation: A 2-month-old girl with Down syndrome feeds slowly, sweats and has gained only 300 g since birth. RR 70, HR 168, SpO2 95%; crackles at both bases, liver 3 cm below the ribs; holosystolic murmur at the left lower sternal border and apex with a mid-diastolic rumble.
correlates.workup: ECG: superior QRS axis (about -90 degrees), PR 180 ms. Chest film: large heart, heavy lung markings. Echo: a low gap between the upper chambers continuous with an inlet gap between the lower chambers, under one shared leaking valve.
correlates.management: Treat heart failure (diuretics, high-calorie feeds) and refer for surgical repair at 3-6 months - this lesion always needs it, before lung pressures become fixed and the shunt reverses.

correlates.name: Compression atelectasis
correlates.presentation: A 58-year-old woman with metastatic breast cancer has 3 weeks of increasing breathlessness and dry cough; no fever. RR 28, HR 104, SpO2 90%. Right side: dull to percussion from mid-back down, absent breath sounds and fremitus, reduced expansion; trachea pushed toward the left.
correlates.workup: Chest film: large right pleural opacity with a curved upper border, airless lung above it, mediastinum shifted left. Thoracentesis: bloody exudate (protein ratio 0.7, LDH ratio 0.8) containing malignant cells.
correlates.management: Therapeutic thoracentesis (about 1.5 L at a time) lets the lung re-expand; for recurrence, pleurodesis or an indwelling pleural catheter; treat the cancer. The lung recovers once the pleural space is cleared.

correlates.name: Congenital heart block (neonatal lupus)
correlates.presentation: A fetal heart rate of 55 was noted at 24 weeks in a mother with years of dry eyes, dry mouth and joint pain. The term newborn has HR 58 and regular, BP 64/40, is pink and feeds well. At 3 weeks scaly, ring-shaped red patches appear around the eyes.
correlates.workup: ECG: regular P waves at 140/min with no fixed relation to regular, narrow QRS complexes at 55/min. Platelets 80,000/uL. Mother's serum: anti-Ro/SSA and anti-La/SSB IgG positive.
correlates.management: Monitor; permanent pacemaker if symptomatic, in heart failure, wide QRS or rate persistently under about 55. Rash and low counts fade as maternal antibody clears, but the conduction damage usually stays; fetal echo in later pregnancies.

correlates.name: Congenital long QT syndrome
correlates.presentation: A 12-year-old boy who has worn hearing aids in both ears since infancy faints for the second time during gym class and comes round within a minute. His older brother died suddenly at 14; his parents are healthy. He takes no medications. Exam between events normal; pulse 64.
correlates.workup: ECG: sinus rhythm, QTc 530 ms with broad T waves; K+ 4.3 mEq/L, Mg2+ 2.1 mg/dL, Ca2+ 9.4 mg/dL, TSH normal. Genetics: biallelic KCNQ1 variants (reduced slow delayed-rectifier K+ current).
correlates.management: Beta blocker (propranolol or nadolol) to prevent torsades; avoid every QT-prolonging drug and keep K+ and Mg2+ normal; limit competitive sport; ICD after arrest or syncope despite beta blockade; ECG-screen relatives.

correlates.name: Constrictive pericarditis
correlates.presentation: 58-year-old man treated for pulmonary TB in his 30s and with CABG 6 years ago: 8 months of fatigue, abdominal swelling and leg edema. JVP 16 cm that rises further on inspiration; ascites; liver 4 cm below the costal margin; lungs clear; no murmur.
correlates.workup: CT: pericardium 7 mm thick with calcified plaques. Echo: normal LV wall thickness, EF 60%, septum shifts toward the LV on inspiration, mitral inflow varies >25% with breathing. Cath: equal LV and RV diastolic pressures. BNP only 110 pg/mL.
correlates.management: Diuretics for congestion; anti-inflammatory therapy only if markers show active inflammation; surgical pericardiectomy for chronic calcific disease; treat TB if still active.

correlates.name: Contraction atelectasis
correlates.presentation: A 60-year-old man treated for tuberculosis 20 years ago has slowly worsening breathlessness and a small chronic cough; no fever or weight loss now. RR 20, SpO2 93%. The right upper chest is flattened and moves less, dull, with harsh breath sounds; trachea pulled to the right.
correlates.workup: Chest film: shrunken right upper lobe with dense streaky scarring and calcified nodes; trachea and hilum pulled up and right. CT: thick scar around narrowed, distorted bronchi, none dilated. Sputum acid-fast smears and cultures negative x3.
correlates.management: Not reversible - neither airway clearance nor drainage re-expands scarred lung; treat symptoms (bronchodilators, vaccines, prompt treatment of infections); resection only for recurrent infection or bleeding.

correlates.name: COPD exacerbation
correlates.presentation: A 75-year-old man with 75 pack-years (quit 6 months ago) has coughed for 6 months; this week it is worse, with more, thicker sputum and breathlessness crossing a room; no fever. RR 28, HR 104, SpO2 87%; pursed lips, hyperresonant chest, faint breath sounds, wheeze.
correlates.workup: ABG: pH 7.31, PaCO2 58, HCO3- 29, PaO2 55 mmHg (acute rise on chronic retention). Chest film: flat diaphragms, large retrosternal air space, midline trachea, no infiltrate or collapsed lung. Spirometry when stable: FEV1/FVC 0.52, FEV1 40%.
correlates.management: Controlled oxygen to SpO2 88-92%; nebulized short-acting beta agonist plus ipratropium; prednisone 40 mg for 5 days; antibiotic for purulent sputum; bilevel noninvasive ventilation for pH below 7.35 with a high PaCO2; intubate if failing.

correlates.name: Cor pulmonale
correlates.presentation: A 69-year-old man with 6 years of worsening dry cough and breathlessness from scarred lungs now has 3 months of leg swelling and right upper quadrant ache, no orthopnea. SpO2 85% on room air; clubbing; fine late-inspiratory basal crackles; JVP 14 cm; parasternal lift, loud P2.
correlates.workup: Echo: dilated, thick right ventricle, flattened septum, PA systolic pressure 58 mmHg; normal left ventricle (EF 60%) and left atrium. FVC 55%, FEV1/FVC 0.86, DLCO 35%. CT: basal subpleural cystic scarring. ECG: right axis deviation.
correlates.management: Treat the underlying lung disease and correct hypoxemia - long-term supplemental oxygen is the key step; cautious diuretics for edema; pulmonary rehabilitation; refer for lung transplant evaluation.

correlates.name: Costochondritis
correlates.presentation: A 28-year-old woman has 5 days of sharp left front chest pain that began after she moved furniture; twisting, deep breaths and lying on that side worsen it, exertion does not. HR 76, BP 118/74, SpO2 99%; pressing the 3rd-4th left rib cartilages reproduces the pain exactly.
correlates.workup: ECG: normal sinus rhythm, no ST or T changes; troponin negative twice; chest film normal; ESR normal; no swelling of the joints on exam.
correlates.management: Reassure once the cardiac and other dangerous causes are excluded; NSAIDs, local heat and a break from the provoking activity; gentle stretching; it settles over weeks.

correlates.name: Croup
correlates.presentation: A 2-year-old boy had a runny nose and low fever for 5 days; for 24 h, worse at night, he has a harsh cough, a hoarse voice and a high-pitched noise on breathing in when upset. T 38.1 C, RR 36, SpO2 96%; mild suprasternal retractions; no drooling, sits comfortably, drinks well.
correlates.workup: Clinical diagnosis. If a neck film is taken: frontal view shows narrowing of the airway just below the vocal cords; lateral view shows a normal epiglottis and normal space behind the pharynx. Viral swab: parainfluenza.
correlates.management: One dose of oral dexamethasone (0.6 mg/kg) for every severity; nebulized racemic epinephrine for noisy breathing at rest, then observe 2-4 h for rebound; keep the child calm on a parent's lap.

correlates.name: Culture-negative endocarditis
correlates.presentation: 55-year-old sheep farmer with a bicuspid aortic valve: 4 months of evening temperatures, sweats and 7 kg weight loss. T 38.2 C, early diastolic murmur at the left sternal border, hepatosplenomegaly, clubbing. He has taken no antibiotics.
correlates.workup: Three sets of blood bottles show no growth after 7 days. TEE: 8 mm mass on an aortic cusp. Phase I IgG to Coxiella burnetii 1:3,200; PCR of blood confirms. ESR 90 mm/h; ALT mildly raised.
correlates.management: Draw extra bottles before any antibiotic; serology/PCR for Coxiella, Bartonella and other fastidious agents; for the Q fever form, doxycycline plus hydroxychloroquine for 18 months or more; surgery if the valve is destroyed.

correlates.name: Cyanide toxicity from nitroprusside
correlates.presentation: 62-year-old man with diabetes and CKD (creatinine 3.1) on day 2 of a continuous IV vasodilator infusion started for a BP of 200/100: now confused and short of breath, with flushed red skin. BP 118/70, HR 116, RR 30, SpO2 98% on room air, no cyanosis; then a seizure.
correlates.workup: pH 7.18, HCO3- 9, gap 28, lactate 11 mmol/L; PaO2 normal but central venous O2 saturation 88% (tissues cannot extract O2 - cytochrome c oxidase blocked); osmolar gap and ketones normal; thiocyanate level high.
correlates.management: Stop the infusion; 100% O2; IV hydroxocobalamin (binds the toxin to form cyanocobalamin, vitamin B12, excreted in urine) and/or sodium thiosulfate (sulfur donor); switch to a different IV antihypertensive.

correlates.name: Cystic fibrosis
correlates.presentation: 15-month-old boy: chronic wet cough, two pneumonias (one admission), weight below the 3rd centile despite a big appetite, and bulky, greasy, foul-smelling stools. Nasal polyps; RR 36; scattered coarse crackles. Older sibling died in infancy of bowel obstruction.
correlates.workup: Sweat chloride 92 mmol/L on two occasions (positive above 60); newborn screen showed high immunoreactive trypsinogen; fecal elastase 40 ug/g; homozygous F508del. Sputum grows coagulase-positive cocci.
correlates.management: Daily airway clearance (chest physiotherapy, nebulized dornase alfa, hypertonic saline); aggressive antibiotics for flares; pancreatic enzymes, vitamins A, D, E, K, high-calorie diet; CFTR modulator when eligible; do not restrict activity.

correlates.name: Deep vein thrombosis
correlates.presentation: 63-year-old woman 8 days after a right hip replacement, sent home without prophylaxis: 2 days of aching, warm swelling of the right calf and thigh. Temp 37.6 C, HR 92, SpO2 98%, no chest pain or breathlessness. Right calf 4 cm larger than the left, with pitting edema.
correlates.workup: Compression ultrasound (test of choice): right popliteal and femoral segments do not collapse under the probe and hold echogenic clot with no Doppler flow; contrast venography (gold standard) not needed; platelets and creatinine normal.
correlates.management: Anticoagulate - LMWH or apixaban/rivaroxaban for 3 months for a provoked clot; early walking; IVC filter only if anticoagulation is impossible; consider looking for silent clot in the lungs; prophylaxis after future surgery.

correlates.name: Diabetic dyslipidemia
correlates.presentation: 58-year-old man with type 2 diabetes for 8 years, poorly controlled (A1c 9.6%), BMI 33, inactive, eats large carbohydrate-heavy meals; no symptoms, here for annual labs. BP 128/78; no skin or tendon deposits; thyroid normal; his siblings have normal lipids.
correlates.workup: Fasting TG 340, HDL 31, LDL 152 mg/dL with many small dense LDL particles; apoB high; glucose 214; TSH, creatinine and urine albumin normal. Insulin resistance drives hepatic VLDL overproduction while lipoprotein lipase activity falls.
correlates.management: Moderate- to high-intensity statin (all patients with diabetes aged 40-75); tighten glucose control, which itself lowers TG; weight loss, exercise, less refined carbohydrate and alcohol; fibrate or omega-3 only if TG stays >=500.

correlates.name: Diabetic ketoacidosis
correlates.presentation: 56-year-old woman with type 1 diabetes for 15 years; a viral illness brought fever, anorexia and vomiting and she cut back her insulin. Now short of breath with deep, fast breathing (RR 30), HR 118, BP 100/60, dry mucous membranes, poor skin turgor, diffuse abdominal tenderness.
correlates.workup: pH 7.07, PCO2 18, HCO3- 5 (1.2 rule predicts PCO2 17 - simple, compensated); Na+ 132, Cl- 94, K+ 5.9 - gap 33; glucose 650 mg/dL; serum osm ~305; urine glucose and ketones positive; beta-hydroxybutyrate high.
correlates.management: IV isotonic saline first; regular insulin infusion once K+ is above 3.3; add K+ to fluids when K+ falls below ~5.3 (total-body K+ is depleted); add dextrose at glucose ~250 and keep insulin running until the gap closes; treat the trigger.

correlates.name: Diffuse esophageal spasm
correlates.presentation: A 52-year-old woman has 6 months of intermittent squeezing pain behind the sternum lasting minutes, set off by cold drinks or large bites, sometimes with food sticking - solids and liquids alike. No weight loss; pain never comes with exertion. HR 72, BP 126/78; exam normal.
correlates.workup: ECG and exercise treadmill test normal; troponin negative. Endoscopy and 24-h pH study normal. Manometry: 30% of wet swallows trigger premature, simultaneous contractions, with normal lower-sphincter relaxation.
correlates.management: Exclude cardiac ischemia first; avoid trigger foods and cold drinks; smooth-muscle relaxants (calcium channel blocker or nitrate) or a low-dose tricyclic for pain; botulinum toxin or myotomy if refractory.

correlates.name: Digoxin toxicity
correlates.presentation: An 83-year-old woman with heart failure and AF takes furosemide, lisinopril and a rate-control drug started years ago. After 4 days of diarrhea she has nausea, vomiting, poor appetite, fatigue and new confusion. Pulse 48 and regular, BP 108/64.
correlates.workup: ECG: regular junctional rhythm at 48 despite known AF, frequent ventricular bigeminy, sagging down-sloping ST depression. K+ 2.9 mEq/L, Mg2+ 1.4 mg/dL, creatinine 2.1 mg/dL; serum drug level 3.6 ng/mL.
correlates.management: Drug-specific antibody Fab fragments for dangerous arrhythmia, K+ >5 or end-organ effects; replace K+ and give magnesium (protects against torsades); stop the drug and interacting agents (amiodarone, verapamil, quinidine).

correlates.name: Dilated cardiomyopathy (idiopathic/familial)
correlates.presentation: A 38-year-old man has 3 months of worsening exertional breathlessness, orthopnea and ankle swelling. His father died suddenly at 45; an aunt had a heart transplant. Rare alcohol, no drugs or chemotherapy, no recent illness. BP 100/68, HR 108; cool hands, apex displaced, S3.
correlates.workup: Echo: all four chambers enlarged, thin walls, global hypokinesis, EF 22%, mitral leak from annular stretch. Coronary angiogram, TSH, ferritin, thiamine normal. Gene panel: truncating titin (TTN) variant. Biopsy: nonspecific.
correlates.management: Guideline reduced-EF therapy (ARNI, beta blocker, MRA, SGLT2 inhibitor, diuretic); anticoagulate for AF or mural thrombus; ICD for sudden-death prevention; echo screening of first-degree relatives; transplant if refractory.

correlates.name: Diphtheritic myocarditis
correlates.presentation: 8-year-old unvaccinated girl from a conflict zone had a sore throat, T 38.3 C and marked swelling of the front of her neck 12 days ago. Now fatigue, a nasal voice, fluid coming out of her nose when she drinks, and HR 42; BP 94/60.
correlates.workup: ECG: complete heart block with a wide escape rhythm; troponin I 2.1 ng/mL; echo: LVEF 40%. Throat swab on tellurite agar: black colonies of club-shaped gram-positive rods; Elek test confirms toxin production.
correlates.management: Antitoxin at once on clinical suspicion (it neutralizes only unbound toxin) plus erythromycin or penicillin; temporary pacing; droplet isolation; vaccinate contacts and, after recovery, the patient.

correlates.name: Distal (type 1) renal tubular acidosis
correlates.presentation: 34-year-old woman with 2 years of gritty dry eyes and a dry mouth comes in with left flank pain spreading to the groin and 3 weeks of muscle weakness. BP 118/76, HR 88. Both parotid glands are enlarged; left costovertebral angle tenderness.
correlates.workup: Na+ 139, Cl- 115, HCO3- 15 - gap 9; K+ 2.7; urine pH 6.8 although blood pH is 7.30; urine Na+ + K+ - Cl- = +20 (positive: NH4+ excretion low); CT: bilateral calcium phosphate stones and medullary calcification; anti-Ro/La positive.
correlates.management: Oral alkali, ideally potassium citrate (corrects the acidemia, replaces K+ and raises urine citrate to prevent stones); replete severe hypokalemia before giving alkali; treat the underlying autoimmune disease.

correlates.name: Diuretic-induced hypokalemia
correlates.presentation: A 70-year-old woman with heart failure had her furosemide raised from 20 to 80 mg daily 3 weeks ago. Now weak, cramping and constipated, dizzy on standing. BP 98/60 lying, 84/54 standing, HR 96; dry mucous membranes, no edema.
correlates.workup: K+ 2.9 mEq/L, HCO3- 33, Mg2+ 1.8; 24-h urine K+ 55 mmol (renal loss) and urine Cl- 60 mEq/L; renin high. ECG: low-amplitude T waves with ST depression.
correlates.management: Lower or stop the loop dose; oral KCl preferred (chloride depletion responds to KCl); use a comorbidity to help - add spironolactone, an ACE inhibitor/ARB or beta blocker if indicated; replace Mg2+; recheck weekly until stable.

correlates.name: Doxorubicin cardiomyopathy
correlates.presentation: A 52-year-old woman who finished breast cancer chemotherapy with an intercalating agent 10 months ago (cumulative 480 mg/m2) has 6 weeks of orthopnea, waking breathless at night and nocturia. Pulse 112, BP 102/68; bibasilar crackles, an S3, JVP 10 cm.
correlates.workup: Echo: dilated LV with global hypokinesis, EF 30% (55% before chemotherapy); valves normal; coronary angiography normal. Endomyocardial biopsy (rarely needed): myocyte vacuolization and myofibril loss.
correlates.management: Standard HFrEF therapy (ACE inhibitor/ARB/ARNI, beta blocker, MRA, SGLT2 inhibitor, diuretic); do not re-expose - injury is dose-dependent and largely irreversible. Prevention: baseline and periodic echo, cumulative dose limits.

correlates.name: Dressler syndrome
correlates.presentation: 47-year-old man 2 months after a stent for a lateral STEMI, on dual antiplatelet therapy: 4 days of chest pain worse on breathing in, with low-grade fevers and malaise. Temp 38.3 C, HR 98, BP 128/80; scratchy sound over the lower sternum; lungs clear, no edema.
correlates.workup: WBC 13,200; ESR 70 mm/h, CRP high; ECG: diffuse concave ST elevation in nearly all leads with PR depression and no reciprocal change, plus old Q waves in I and aVL from the prior infarct; CK-MB normal; echo: small effusion, EF unchanged.
correlates.management: Anti-inflammatory therapy - high-dose aspirin (the NSAID of choice after MI) or colchicine, which also cuts recurrence; glucocorticoids only if refractory; continue antiplatelet therapy; follow the effusion.

correlates.name: Drug-induced lupus
correlates.presentation: A 63-year-old man taking hydralazine with isosorbide dinitrate for heart failure for 9 months has 6 weeks of aching joints, muscle pain, low-grade fever and pleuritic chest pain, with a faint rash over his cheeks. No oral ulcers, no edema, normal mental status.
correlates.workup: ANA 1:640 with anti-histone antibodies; anti-dsDNA negative; C3 and C4 normal; urinalysis bland, creatinine 0.9 mg/dL. Slow-acetylator genotype. Small exudative pleural effusion.
correlates.management: Stop the offending drug (hydralazine, procainamide, isoniazid) - symptoms usually fade over weeks; NSAIDs for joint and serosal pain, a short glucocorticoid course if severe; substitute an alternative drug.

correlates.name: Dyslipidemia secondary to hypothyroidism
correlates.presentation: 46-year-old woman with 6 months of fatigue, 6 kg weight gain, constipation, feeling cold, dry skin and heavier periods. Puffy face, HR 54, ankle reflexes relax slowly after the tap; firm, nontender, enlarged thyroid. Her LDL was normal 2 years ago.
correlates.workup: LDL 205 mg/dL (110 two years ago), IDL increased, TG mildly up (190), HDL normal; TSH 22 mU/L, low free T4, anti-TPO positive; CK mildly high (650). Fewer hepatic LDL receptors explain the rise.
correlates.management: Levothyroxine first, then recheck lipids in 6-8 weeks - LDL usually falls back toward baseline; add a statin only if it stays high, since statins started in an untreated low-thyroid state carry more muscle toxicity.

correlates.name: Dyslipidemia secondary to nephrotic syndrome
correlates.presentation: 34-year-old man with 6 weeks of puffy eyes each morning, swollen legs by evening, foamy urine and 5 kg weight gain. BP 132/84; pitting edema to the knees; no rash, joint pain or visible blood in the urine.
correlates.workup: Albumin 1.9 g/dL; urine protein 7.5 g/day with oval fat bodies, no RBC casts; total cholesterol 380, LDL 270, TG 320, HDL 38 mg/dL (low oncotic pressure drives hepatic VLDL/apoB output); TSH normal; biopsy: podocyte foot-process effacement.
correlates.management: Treat the glomerular disease (e.g. glucocorticoids); ACE inhibitor or ARB to cut protein loss; salt restriction and a loop diuretic for edema; statin if lipids stay high; consider anticoagulation when albumin is very low.

correlates.name: Early post-MI fibrinous pericarditis
correlates.presentation: 64-year-old man on day 2 after a large anterior STEMI reperfused late: new sharp chest pain, different from his infarct pain, that is worse with deep breaths. Temp 37.8 C, HR 92, BP 124/76; a scratchy, three-part sound at the left sternal border; lungs clear.
correlates.workup: ECG: anterior ST elevation persists, plus new mild ST elevation and PR depression outside that territory; troponin falling, CK-MB not re-elevated; echo: thin rim of pericardial fluid, no chamber collapse; histology: neutrophils and fibrin.
correlates.management: Usually settles within days; high-dose aspirin for pain (preferred over other NSAIDs and steroids, which can impair scar healing this early); colchicine may be added; reassess any anticoagulant if the effusion grows.

correlates.name: Ebstein anomaly
correlates.presentation: A newborn whose mother took lithium for bipolar disorder throughout pregnancy is blue (SpO2 80%) and breathing fast. HR 150, RR 66; soft holosystolic murmur at the left lower sternal border, louder with inspiration; liver 3 cm below the ribs; no arm-leg pulse difference.
correlates.workup: Chest film: the heart fills nearly the whole chest (cardiothoracic ratio 0.8); dark lungs. Echo: right AV valve leaflets set low inside the right ventricle; huge right atrium, small right ventricle, severe leak, right-to-left ASD flow.
correlates.management: Prostaglandin E1 to keep the ductus open while lung resistance falls; treat heart failure; surgical valve repair or reconstruction; screen the ECG for an accessory conduction pathway.

correlates.name: Eisenmenger syndrome
correlates.presentation: A 24-year-old woman raised abroad was told of a loud heart murmur as a baby but never treated. Now breathless on stairs, tired, and has coughed blood once; lips and nail beds blue, SpO2 82% at rest, fingers clubbed. Loud single S2, left parasternal lift; no loud murmur now.
correlates.workup: Hb 20.5 g/dL, Hct 62%. Echo: 1.5-cm opening in the wall between the lower chambers, flow now right to left; right ventricular pressure equals systemic. Cath: lung vascular resistance 14 Wood units, unchanged by nitric oxide.
correlates.management: Do not close the hole - it is now the right heart's relief valve; pulmonary vasodilators (endothelin antagonist, PDE-5 inhibitor); avoid pregnancy; phlebotomy only for symptomatic hyperviscosity; heart-lung transplant at end stage.

correlates.name: Elevated lipoprotein(a)
correlates.presentation: 44-year-old man, nonsmoker, BP 118/76, BMI 24, no diabetes, exercises daily and eats little saturated fat, has an MI; a standard lipid panel last year was unremarkable. His father and paternal uncle had MIs in their 40s. No tendon nodules or corneal rings.
correlates.workup: LDL 128, HDL 52, TG 110 mg/dL; TSH, glucose and A1c normal; a separate assay finds 210 nmol/L (high >125) of an LDL-like particle carrying an extra plasminogen-like glycoprotein; the level is genetically set and barely moves with diet.
correlates.management: Aggressive LDL lowering (high-intensity statin, then a PCSK9 inhibitor, which also cuts Lp(a) ~25%); niacin lowers Lp(a) but has not cut events; avoid trans fats; test first-degree relatives.

correlates.name: Embolic stroke from carotid atherosclerosis
correlates.presentation: 70-year-old former smoker with hypertension: 2 hours of slurred speech and weakness of the left arm and lower left face, still present on arrival. BP 176/94, HR 78 and regular; whooshing sounds heard over both sides of the neck; glucose 112.
correlates.workup: CT: no bleed; MRI: restricted diffusion in right MCA cortex; CT angiogram: 80% right ICA stenosis with an ulcerated plaque; ECG sinus rhythm. Plaque histology: thin fibrous cap, large lipid core, many macrophages, few smooth muscle cells.
correlates.management: IV alteplase or tenecteplase within 4.5 h if no bleed (BP <185/110 first); thrombectomy for a large-vessel occlusion; then antiplatelet, high-intensity statin, BP control and endarterectomy within ~2 weeks for symptomatic 70-99% stenosis.

correlates.name: Endocardial fibroelastosis
correlates.presentation: A 7-month-old girl has 6 weeks of fast breathing, sweating with feeds and poor weight gain (5th percentile). RR 64, HR 168, BP 82/50 in arms and legs with equal pulses; pale; gallop rhythm, soft apical holosystolic murmur, liver 4 cm below the ribs.
correlates.workup: Chest film: large heart, congested lungs. Echo: enlarged, poorly contracting left ventricle (EF 25%) lined by a thick, bright, opaque inner layer; mildly narrowed aortic valve. Biopsy: thick layer of collagen and elastic fibers.
correlates.management: Heart-failure therapy (diuretics, ACE inhibitor, beta blocker); relieve any associated lesion such as aortic valve obstruction; heart transplant if it progresses - many die of heart failure.

correlates.name: Endocarditis with an occult colorectal tumor
correlates.presentation: 74-year-old man with 2 months of fatigue, evening temperatures to 38.0 C and 5 kg weight loss; no recent dental work, catheters or procedures. New soft early diastolic murmur at the left sternal border; pale conjunctivae; no hepatosplenomegaly.
correlates.workup: Hb 9.1 g/dL, MCV 69 fL, ferritin 6 ng/mL, stool guaiac positive. Blood cultures 3/3: catalase-negative cocci in chains, bile-esculin positive, no growth in 6.5% NaCl, PYR-negative. TEE: 7 mm mass on an aortic cusp.
correlates.management: Organism-directed IV penicillin or ceftriaxone, then colonoscopy to find and remove the polyp or carcinoma that let the organism into the blood.

correlates.name: Endomyocardial fibrosis
correlates.presentation: A 14-year-old boy from rural Uganda has 6 months of a swelling abdomen, leg edema and breathlessness on exertion. BP 96/64, HR 110; JVP 14 cm, large liver, tense ascites, soft holosystolic murmur at the left lower sternal border; afebrile, no rash, no new medications.
correlates.workup: Eosinophils 300/uL. Echo: both ventricular apices filled in by dense bright tissue with layered thrombus; small cavities, huge atria, EF 55%, stiff filling. Biopsy: dense collagen scar of endocardium and subendocardium, little inflammation.
correlates.management: Cautious diuretics for congestion; anticoagulation for the mural thrombi; rate control of AF; surgical excision of the endocardial scar (endocardiectomy) with valve repair or replacement in selected patients.

correlates.name: Epiglottitis
correlates.presentation: 2-year-old girl who has never been vaccinated: 2 hours of T 38.9 C and harsh, noisy breathing in. Toxic-looking, with a muffled cry, drooling, suprasternal retractions; no cough, no witnessed choking, no sick contacts; lungs clear.
correlates.workup: Clinical diagnosis - do not lay her down, examine the throat or draw blood first. Once the airway is secure: beefy red, swollen supraglottic tissue at laryngoscopy; lateral neck film: rounded, thickened soft-tissue shadow above the larynx.
correlates.management: Keep her calm on a parent's lap; secure the airway in the OR with anesthesia and ENT ready; then IV ceftriaxone plus vancomycin and steroids; rifampin prophylaxis for household contacts if Hib grows.

correlates.name: Factor V Leiden
correlates.presentation: 24-year-old woman 4 months into an estrogen-containing pill: painful, swollen right calf after a 9-hour flight. Her father had a leg clot at 35 and an aunt had a lung clot after childbirth. HR 90, SpO2 99%; right calf 3 cm larger and tender.
correlates.workup: Ultrasound: right popliteal clot; antithrombin, protein C and protein S levels normal; clotting time fails to lengthen normally when activated protein C is added.
correlates.management: Anticoagulate 3-6 months (apixaban, rivaroxaban or LMWH); stop estrogen for good - progestin-only or nonhormonal contraception; no lifelong therapy after one provoked clot; prophylaxis around future surgery, pregnancy and postpartum.

correlates.name: Familial chylomicronemia (type I)
correlates.presentation: 7-year-old boy with his third bout of severe upper-abdominal pain and vomiting since age 3, each after a fatty meal; his sister has had similar attacks. Small yellow papules with red rims on the buttocks and elbows; liver and spleen enlarged. Lean, no diabetes; parents healthy.
correlates.workup: Lipase 1,100; TG 3,200 mg/dL; plasma left in the fridge overnight forms a creamy top layer over a clear bottom layer; LDL and HDL low; post-heparin lipoprotein lipase activity absent (or apoC-II missing); no early coronary disease in kin.
correlates.management: Very-low-fat diet (under 15-20% of calories) with medium-chain triglyceride oil; no alcohol or estrogen; fibrates, statins and omega-3s work poorly because the clearing enzyme is missing; treat pancreatitis episodes supportively.

correlates.name: Familial combined hyperlipidemia
correlates.presentation: 47-year-old man who had an MI at 46; BMI 29, BP 136/86. No tendon nodules, no palm-crease or elbow deposits. His father had an MI at 52; one sister has only a high cholesterol, a brother only high triglycerides, and his own pattern has shifted between checks.
correlates.workup: Total cholesterol 310, LDL 190, TG 420 mg/dL - VLDL and LDL both up; apoB 160 mg/dL, disproportionately high; VLDL-to-TG ratio normal (not remnant disease); apoE E3/E3; TSH, glucose and urine protein normal.
correlates.management: Lifestyle (weight loss, less saturated fat, sugar and alcohol) plus a high-intensity statin for LDL/apoB; add ezetimibe if needed and a fibrate or omega-3 for TG >=500; treat BP and glucose; screen first-degree relatives.

correlates.name: Familial dysbetalipoproteinemia (type III)
correlates.presentation: 52-year-old man, BMI 31, type 2 diabetes diagnosed last year, coronary stent at 48; now calf pain after walking 2 blocks. Firm, bumpy yellow plaques over both elbows and knees; Achilles tendons normal. A screening panel showed cholesterol and triglycerides both near 400.
correlates.workup: Total cholesterol 390 and TG 420 mg/dL - raised about equally; VLDL is unusually cholesterol-rich, with chylomicron remnants and IDL accumulating; LDL not high; apoE genotype E2/E2; TSH normal.
correlates.management: Treat triggers (weight, diabetes, hypothyroidism, alcohol); diet; statin and/or fibrate, to which it responds very well; aggressive vascular risk reduction because coronary and peripheral artery disease come early.

correlates.name: Familial hypercholesterolemia
correlates.presentation: 19-year-old man with 2 months of chest tightness when he runs; firm, painless nodules thicken both Achilles tendons. Father died of an MI at 41, grandfather at 50; his 14-year-old sister already takes a cholesterol pill. Nonsmoker, BMI 23, BP 118/72.
correlates.workup: Total cholesterol 325, LDL 250, HDL 45, TG 110 mg/dL; TSH, glucose, creatinine and urine protein normal; genetic test: loss-of-function LDL receptor mutation (or defective apoB-100, or gain-of-function PCSK9); homozygotes run LDL >500.
correlates.management: High-intensity statin plus diet; add ezetimibe, then a PCSK9 inhibitor if LDL stays high on maximal statin; homozygotes add lomitapide, evinacumab or LDL apheresis; screen relatives - affected children may start a statin at ~10.

correlates.name: Familial hypertriglyceridemia (type IV)
correlates.presentation: 38-year-old man with no symptoms whose fasting TG has run 350-500 mg/dL on several checks while LDL stayed normal; his mother and brother have the same pattern. BMI 27, waist 94 cm, BP 124/78; no skin or tendon deposits, no abdominal pain; 2 beers a week.
correlates.workup: Fasting TG 480 mg/dL from excess VLDL; LDL 105, HDL 42; fasting glucose 96, A1c 5.6%; TSH, creatinine and urine protein normal; refrigerated serum evenly cloudy with no creamy top layer; same pattern in first-degree relatives.
correlates.management: Lifestyle first - weight loss, less refined carbohydrate, sugar and alcohol, regular exercise; rule out secondary causes; fibrate or prescription omega-3 once TG is 500 or more to prevent pancreatitis; statin for overall ASCVD risk.

correlates.name: Fanconi syndrome
correlates.presentation: A 38-year-old man on a tenofovir-containing HIV regimen for 2 years has 4 months of aching hips and ribs, thirst, frequent urination and weakness. No diabetes. BP 124/78; ribs tender to pressure; proximal leg weakness.
correlates.workup: Phosphate 1.6 mg/dL with 24-h urine phosphate 900 mg; urine glucose 2+ while serum glucose is 88; amino acids in the urine; Cl- 112, HCO3- 17 (normal gap); K+ 3.0; uric acid low. Hip film: thin lucent bands across the femoral necks.
correlates.management: Stop the offending drug; replace phosphate, potassium and bicarbonate orally (large alkali doses), with active vitamin D for the bone disease; treat any underlying cause.

correlates.name: First-degree AV block
correlates.presentation: A 54-year-old marathon runner has a routine ECG before knee surgery. He feels well, with no dizziness, fainting or exercise limitation. Resting pulse 52 and regular, BP 118/72, normal exam.
correlates.workup: ECG: sinus rhythm at 52/min; PR interval 260 ms and identical in every beat; every P wave is followed by a narrow QRS; no non-conducted P waves on a 24-hour Holter.
correlates.management: No treatment; reassure. Review AV-nodal-slowing drugs (metoprolol, verapamil, diltiazem, digoxin) and recheck if symptoms or a further PR change appear.

correlates.name: Flail chest
correlates.presentation: A 46-year-old driver struck the steering wheel in a high-speed crash and is in severe pain; RR 32, HR 118, BP 128/80, SpO2 88% on a mask. A hand-sized area of his right lateral rib cage sinks in as he breathes in and bulges out as he breathes out; bony step-offs; crackling skin.
correlates.workup: Radiograph and CT: right ribs 4-7 each broken in two places, with contusion of the underlying lung and a small hemothorax; no pneumothorax yet. ABG: PaO2 58, PaCO2 48 mmHg.
correlates.management: Oxygen and aggressive analgesia (epidural or regional nerve block) so he can breathe deeply; airway clearance; noninvasive or mechanical ventilation if he tires or stays hypoxemic; surgical rib fixation in selected cases.

correlates.name: Fungal endocarditis
correlates.presentation: 47-year-old woman fed for 8 months through a tunneled central line after bowel resection, with many antibiotic courses: 3 weeks of temperatures to 38.6 C, then a sudden cold, pulseless right leg. New apical holosystolic murmur; fluffy white lesions in both retinas.
correlates.workup: TEE: 2.6 cm bulky mass on the mitral valve. Blood cultures grow oval budding yeast with pseudohyphae, germ-tube positive; beta-D-glucan raised. The femoral embolectomy clot contains the same organism.
correlates.management: Remove the central line; early valve surgery for the large mass and embolism; IV echinocandin or liposomal amphotericin B, then long-term oral fluconazole; dilated eye examination.

correlates.name: Giant cell myocarditis
correlates.presentation: A 42-year-old woman with ulcerative colitis has 3 weeks of rapidly worsening breathlessness and palpitations and has fainted twice; no preceding cold or new medication. BP 92/60, HR 124, JVP 14 cm, S3; repeated runs of a fast wide-complex rhythm on the monitor.
correlates.workup: ECG: runs of monomorphic VT, new high-grade AV block. Echo: EF 20% and falling despite therapy; coronaries normal. Biopsy: widespread myocyte necrosis with multinucleated cells among lymphocytes, eosinophils, plasma cells and macrophages.
correlates.management: Combined immunosuppression (high-dose steroids plus cyclosporine or a similar agent); ICD or pacing and mechanical circulatory support as needed; early heart-transplant referral - the outlook is poor.

correlates.name: Gitelman syndrome
correlates.presentation: A 22-year-old woman has years of salt craving, fatigue, leg cramps and occasional hand spasms. She takes no diuretic or laxative and does not vomit; growth and puberty were normal. BP 104/66, HR 76; no edema.
correlates.workup: K+ 2.8 mEq/L, HCO3- 31, Mg2+ 1.1 mg/dL with high urine Mg2+; urine Cl- 70 mEq/L; urine calcium very low (Ca/creatinine 0.02); renin and aldosterone high; urine diuretic screen negative.
correlates.management: Lifelong oral magnesium and potassium chloride supplements with liberal salt intake; add a potassium-sparing diuretic (amiloride or spironolactone) if K+ stays low.

correlates.name: Glanzmann thrombasthenia
correlates.presentation: 6-year-old girl whose parents are first cousins: nosebleeds lasting over an hour since infancy, gum bleeding with brushing, easy bruising and prolonged bleeding after a tooth extraction. No joint or muscle bleeds; normal growth; no enlarged liver or spleen.
correlates.workup: Platelets 290,000/uL, normal size on smear; PT and PTT normal; PFA closure time prolonged; no aggregation with ADP, collagen, epinephrine or thrombin but normal response to ristocetin; flow cytometry: absent GP IIb/IIIa (CD41/CD61).
correlates.management: Local measures and tranexamic acid for mucosal bleeds; platelet transfusion (HLA-matched when possible) or recombinant factor VIIa for serious bleeds or surgery; avoid aspirin and NSAIDs; iron for chronic losses.

correlates.name: Glomerulonephritis complicating endocarditis
correlates.presentation: 49-year-old man with 7 weeks of low-grade temperatures, 5 kg weight loss and a louder mitral regurgitation murmur now has cola-colored urine and ankle swelling. BP 152/94, T 38.0 C; spleen tip palpable. No recent sore throat or skin infection, no hemoptysis, no sinus disease.
correlates.workup: Creatinine 2.6 mg/dL (baseline 0.9); urine: dysmorphic RBCs, RBC casts, protein 1.2 g/day. C3 low; ANCA and anti-GBM negative. Blood cultures 3/3 alpha-hemolytic cocci in chains. Biopsy: granular IgG and C3 deposits.
correlates.management: Treat the valve infection with prolonged organism-directed IV antibiotics - the kidney lesion usually settles as circulating antigen clears; dose-adjust nephrotoxic drugs; immunosuppression is not first-line.

correlates.name: Goodpasture syndrome
correlates.presentation: 22-year-old man who smokes a pack a day: a week of coughing up blood and breathlessness, then 3 days of cola-colored urine and less of it. BP 158/94, RR 24, SpO2 90%, crackles in both lungs. No nasal or sinus symptoms, no rash, no joint pain.
correlates.workup: Hb 9.8; creatinine 4.2 (0.9 last month); urine RBC casts, 2+ protein; CXR bilateral airspace filling; serum IgG to the alpha-3 chain of type IV collagen; kidney biopsy: crescents in most glomeruli, no granulomas; ANCA negative.
correlates.management: Plasmapheresis to strip the circulating antibody, together with high-dose glucocorticoids and cyclophosphamide to stop its production; stop smoking; dialysis if renal failure progresses.

correlates.name: Granulomatosis with polyangiitis
correlates.presentation: 42-year-old man with 4 months of bloody nasal crusts, sinus pain and ear fullness that two antibiotic courses did not help; now coughing up blood with fevers and 5 kg weight loss. The bridge of his nose has sunk; both eyes red; BP 150/90.
correlates.workup: PR3-ANCA (c-ANCA) positive; CT chest: several nodules, some cavitating; urine RBC casts, creatinine 2.1; biopsy: necrotizing small-vessel vasculitis with poorly formed granulomas and irregular geographic necrosis; anti-GBM negative.
correlates.management: Induction with high-dose glucocorticoids plus rituximab or cyclophosphamide (plasmapheresis kept for severe lung bleeding or renal failure); maintenance with rituximab or azathioprine.

correlates.name: Heart failure with preserved ejection fraction
correlates.presentation: A 76-year-old woman with 20 years of hypertension, type 2 diabetes and a BMI of 36 has 8 months of breathlessness walking to her mailbox, 2-pillow orthopnea and ankle swelling. BP 164/92, HR 88 regular; JVP 10 cm, an S4, bibasilar crackles, 2+ pitting ankle edema.
correlates.workup: BNP 420 pg/mL. Echo: small, thick-walled left ventricle (septum 14 mm) contracting well, EF 62%; enlarged left atrium; slow, stiff relaxation with high filling pressures (E/e' 18); no valve disease, no outflow gradient.
correlates.management: Loop diuretic for congestion; SGLT2 inhibitor (fewer hospitalizations); control BP, diabetes, AF and coronary disease; GLP-1 agonist for obesity; MRA or ARNI may be considered - no fixed regimen as in reduced-EF failure.

correlates.name: Hereditary angioedema
correlates.presentation: A 19-year-old woman has had attacks since age 12 of painless, non-itchy swelling of a hand, the lips or eyelids lasting 2-4 days, plus bouts of severe crampy abdominal pain with vomiting, often after dental work or stress. Her father has the same. No hives; antihistamines fail.
correlates.workup: C4 low even between attacks; C1-esterase-inhibitor level and function low; C1q normal; tryptase normal. CT during an abdominal attack: edematous bowel wall with free fluid.
correlates.management: Acute attacks: icatibant (bradykinin B2 receptor antagonist) or C1-esterase-inhibitor concentrate, with airway protection - epinephrine and antihistamines do not work; prophylaxis before dental or surgical procedures.

correlates.name: Homocystinuria
correlates.presentation: 14-year-old boy, 188 cm with an arm span of 196 cm, a mild learning disability and worsening nearsightedness; both lenses are partly dislocated. Now a swollen, painful left calf after a 1-hour car ride. An uncle had a stroke at 30. Joints not hypermobile; no murmur.
correlates.workup: Plasma methionine 420 umol/L (normal <40) with low cystathionine and cystine; cystathionine beta-synthase activity low in cultured fibroblasts; ultrasound: left popliteal clot; echo: normal aortic root.
correlates.management: Trial of high-dose pyridoxine (vitamin B6) - about half respond; methionine-restricted, cysteine-supplemented diet; betaine; folate and B12; anticoagulate the clot and give prophylaxis around surgery and immobilization.

correlates.name: Humoral hypercalcemia of malignancy
correlates.presentation: A 64-year-old man with 50 pack-years of smoking has 3 weeks of thirst, polyuria, constipation and new confusion; he has lost 9 kg and coughed up blood twice. BP 102/64, HR 92; dry mucous membranes, drowsy but rousable.
correlates.workup: Ca2+ 14.3 mg/dL, phosphate 2.0, intact PTH 6 pg/mL (suppressed), PTH-related peptide elevated, 1,25-(OH)2 vitamin D normal; creatinine 1.8. ECG QTc 330 ms. CT: 5-cm central hilar mass; no lytic bone lesions.
correlates.management: IV normal saline first, 4-6 L over 24 h (volume depletion blocks renal calcium clearance); IV zoledronic acid to stop osteoclast resorption; then treat the tumor once stable.

correlates.name: Hyperkalemia in kidney failure
correlates.presentation: A 67-year-old man with diabetes and stage 4 CKD was started on lisinopril by his PCP and losartan by his cardiologist; he takes ibuprofen for knee pain and uses a salt substitute. Two days of leg weakness and palpitations. BP 158/90, HR 48; reflexes reduced.
correlates.workup: Repeat K+ 7.2 mEq/L, non-hemolysed; creatinine 3.8 mg/dL, BUN 64; CK normal. ECG: tall peaked T waves, flattened P waves, PR 240 ms, QRS 150 ms.
correlates.management: IV calcium gluconate first (protects conduction, does not lower K+); insulin with dextrose plus inhaled albuterol to shift K+; hemodialysis to remove it; stop the ACE inhibitor, ARB, NSAID and salt substitute; later patiromer.

correlates.name: Hypernatremia from inadequate water intake
correlates.presentation: An 80-year-old nursing-home resident with severe dementia who needs help with every cup has 3 days of fever, cough and fading responsiveness. T 38.6 C, HR 112, BP 104/62, RR 24; dry mouth, skin stays tented, flat neck veins; crackles at the right base; scant dark urine.
correlates.workup: Na+ 168 mEq/L, serum osm 350 mOsm/kg, urine osm 1,000 mOsm/kg (maximally concentrated), urine Na+ 10; BUN 45, creatinine 1.3; glucose 110. Chest film: right lower lobe consolidation.
correlates.management: Treat the pneumonia (e.g. piperacillin-tazobactam for aspiration); replace the calculated deficit with sodium-free D5W plus 1-1.5 L/day of ongoing losses; lower Na+ 4-6 mEq/L, never more than 10, per 24 h.

correlates.name: Hyperosmolar hyperglycemic state
correlates.presentation: A 72-year-old woman with type 2 diabetes who stopped her metformin has 10 days of heavy urination and thirst, then 2 days of drowsiness after a bladder infection; she now responds only to voice. HR 118, BP 96/58, RR 18 and unlabored; very dry mucosa; no ketone odor.
correlates.workup: Glucose 980 mg/dL, measured Na+ 140 (corrected about 154), serum osm 356 mOsm/kg; pH 7.36, HCO3- 22, anion gap 12; serum ketones trace; BUN 62, creatinine 2.0; urine glucose 4+.
correlates.management: Isotonic saline first (deficit often 8-10 L), then hypotonic fluid as the corrected Na+ allows; IV insulin infusion once fluids are running and K+ is >3.3; replace K+; treat the infection; bring osmolality down slowly.

correlates.name: Hypersensitivity myocarditis
correlates.presentation: A 45-year-old man started trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole 10 days ago for a skin infection. Now 2 days of fever, an itchy red rash over his trunk, palpitations and breathlessness on exertion. T 38.4 C, HR 118, BP 104/70; faint S3, no murmur.
correlates.workup: Eosinophils 1,800/uL (14%); troponin I 2.4 ng/mL; ECG: sinus tachycardia, nonspecific ST-T changes; echo: EF 40%; normal coronaries. Biopsy: perivascular lymphocytes and macrophages with many eosinophils, little myocyte necrosis.
correlates.management: Stop the culprit drug and avoid its class; corticosteroids; supportive heart-failure therapy; usually recovers once the drug is gone.

correlates.name: Hypertensive emergency
correlates.presentation: 52-year-old man who ran out of his blood-pressure pills 3 weeks ago: 1 day of headache, blurred vision and new confusion. BP 228/136 in both arms, HR 96. Fundi: flame-shaped retinal hemorrhages and blurred optic disc margins. Lungs clear, no murmur, equal pulses.
correlates.workup: Creatinine 2.4 mg/dL (1.0 last year); UA 2+ protein with RBCs; a few fragmented RBCs on smear; troponin normal; head CT no bleed; ECG: tall precordial QRS voltage with downsloping ST depression and T inversion in V5-V6.
correlates.management: ICU with an IV titratable agent (nicardipine, clevidipine, labetalol; nitroprusside an option); lower MAP no more than ~25% in the first hour, then toward 160/100 over 2-6 h; never normalize quickly; then oral regimen and adherence review.

correlates.name: Hypertriglyceridemia-induced acute pancreatitis
correlates.presentation: 45-year-old man with poorly controlled type 2 diabetes (A1c 11%) and BMI 34 who rarely drinks: 10 h of severe, constant upper-abdominal pain into the back with vomiting, worse lying flat. Temp 37.9 C, HR 118, BP 108/66; epigastric tenderness and guarding.
correlates.workup: Lipase 1,400 U/L (>3x upper limit); TG 2,400 mg/dL in a milky sample; glucose 380, A1c 11%; lipoprotein lipase and apoC-II normal; calcium normal; ultrasound: no stones, normal bile duct; CT: swollen, edematous pancreas.
correlates.management: NPO, generous IV fluids, analgesia; IV insulin infusion (with dextrose) to drive lipoprotein lipase and drop TG fast, plasmapheresis if severe; then a fibrate, glucose control and no alcohol to keep TG well below 500 mg/dL.

correlates.name: Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy
correlates.presentation: A 17-year-old basketball player faints in a sprint drill and is alert within seconds; hard exercise has caused chest tightness for months. BP 124/72, HR 64; forceful sustained apex, S4, brisk carotid pulse; harsh 3/6 systolic murmur at the lower left sternal edge, not in neck.
correlates.workup: ECG: very tall QRS voltage, deep narrow Q waves in II, III, aVF, V5-V6. Echo: septum 28 mm vs posterior wall 11 mm, small vigorous cavity (EF 75%), mitral leaflet pulled to the septum in systole, outflow gradient 60 mmHg.
correlates.management: Beta blocker (or verapamil) to slow and relax the heart; no competitive sport; avoid dehydration, diuretics, vasodilators and inotropes; ICD for sudden-death risk; septal myectomy or alcohol ablation; echo first-degree relatives.

correlates.name: Hypervolemic hyponatremia (heart failure, cirrhosis)
correlates.presentation: A 56-year-old man with 30 years of heavy drinking has 2 months of a growing belly and swollen legs; Na+ is 124 mEq/L. BP 98/60, HR 92; yellow sclerae, spider-like vessels on the chest, a tense abdomen with shifting dullness, 3+ pitting edema to the knees; alert and oriented.
correlates.workup: Na+ 124 mEq/L, serum osm 258, urine osm 450, urine Na+ 8 mEq/L (avid sodium retention); albumin 2.3 g/dL, bilirubin 3.4, INR 1.9; creatinine 1.0. Paracentesis: serum-to-fluid albumin gradient 1.8 g/dL.
correlates.management: Restrict fluid (about 1-1.5 L/day) and dietary sodium; spironolactone with furosemide for the edema and ascites; treat the underlying organ failure; never raise Na+ more than 10 mEq/L in 24 h.

correlates.name: Hypoalphalipoproteinemia
correlates.presentation: 41-year-old man, nonsmoker, BP 120/76, BMI 24, no diabetes, active, has exertional chest pressure and an abnormal stress test; his HDL has never been above 20 mg/dL. Brother had bypass surgery at 45. Exam normal - no corneal clouding, no neuropathy, spleen not felt.
correlates.workup: HDL 18 mg/dL with low apoA-I from accelerated apoA-I/A-II breakdown; LDL 110 and TG 120 mg/dL; esterified cholesterol fraction normal; no anemia or proteinuria; TSH normal; no anabolic steroid use.
correlates.management: No proven HDL-raising therapy: treat overall risk - high-intensity statin for LDL, aspirin for established coronary disease, exercise, no smoking; niacin and CETP inhibitors raise HDL without reducing events.

correlates.name: Hypokalemic periodic paralysis (thyrotoxic)
correlates.presentation: A 27-year-old Asian man wakes at 3 a.m., after a big pasta dinner and evening basketball, unable to lift his arms or legs; speech and breathing are normal. He has lost 6 kg in 2 months and sweats in cool rooms. HR 118, BP 136/70; proximal strength 2/5, reflexes absent.
correlates.workup: K+ 1.9 mEq/L; urine K+/creatinine 8 mEq/g (low - the kidney is conserving, so K+ has moved into cells); pH 7.40, HCO3- 24; TSH <0.01 mIU/L, free T4 4.1 ng/dL. Strength returns fully within hours as K+ normalizes.
correlates.management: Small, cautious KCl doses (K+ comes back out of cells - rebound high K+ is a risk); nonselective beta blocker such as propranolol; treat the overactive thyroid to stop attacks; avoid big carbohydrate meals.

correlates.name: Hypomagnesemia causing refractory hypokalemia
correlates.presentation: A 52-year-old man who drinks a fifth of vodka daily and takes omeprazole is admitted with vomiting. K+ is 2.8 mEq/L; after 3 days and 240 mEq of oral plus IV KCl it is 2.9. He has cramps, a fine tremor and palpitations. BP 128/80, HR 96.
correlates.workup: K+ 2.9 mEq/L after 3 days and 240 mEq of KCl; Mg2+ 1.0 mg/dL (normal 1.7-2.2); urine K+ 45 mmol/day despite low serum K+; Ca2+ 7.9 mg/dL. ECG: flat T waves, ST depression, an extra positive wave after each T, QTc 510 ms; no VT on telemetry.
correlates.management: Give IV magnesium sulfate along with the KCl - K+ will not hold until magnesium is replaced; cardiac monitoring if K+ runs >10 mmol/h, never as a bolus; recheck K+ and Mg2+ every 4-6 h; address the alcohol and stop the PPI.

correlates.name: Hypoplastic left heart syndrome
correlates.presentation: A 5-day-old boy sent home well on day 2 is brought in gray, limp and feeding poorly over 12 hours. HR 190, RR 72, BP 48/30 in arms and legs, capillary refill 5 s; arm and leg pulses equally weak; SpO2 82%; liver 4 cm below the ribs. A sepsis workup has begun.
correlates.workup: pH 7.02, HCO3- 8, lactate 9 mmol/L; cultures pending. Chest film: big heart, congested lungs. Echo: tiny, barely contracting left ventricle, pinhole mitral and aortic valves, 3-mm ascending aorta filled backward from a narrowing ductus.
correlates.management: Prostaglandin E1 infusion at once to reopen the ductus - the only route to the body - and call cardiology; avoid excess oxygen; staged surgery (Norwood, then Glenn, then Fontan) or transplant.

correlates.name: Idiopathic pulmonary hemosiderosis
correlates.presentation: 5-year-old girl with 8 months of on-and-off cough, blood-streaked sputum, tiredness, pallor and poor weight gain. HR 120, RR 30, SpO2 93%; pale conjunctivae; fine crackles at both bases. Normal BP; no blood in urine, no sinus disease, normal stools.
correlates.workup: Hb 7.9, MCV 64, low ferritin; CXR: diffuse bilateral infiltrates that come and go; BAL: Prussian-blue-positive macrophages; ANCA, anti-GBM, ANA negative; normal UA and creatinine; biopsy: alveolar blood, no vasculitis or capillaritis.
correlates.management: Exclude every other cause of alveolar bleeding first; systemic glucocorticoids for acute bleeds, then long-term immunosuppression (prednisone, azathioprine) to prevent recurrence; iron replacement and transfusion as needed.

correlates.name: Inflammatory abdominal aortic aneurysm
correlates.presentation: A 63-year-old male smoker has 3 months of a dull ache in the mid-abdomen and low back, fatigue and 6 kg of weight loss; he is afebrile. BP 142/88, pulse 80. A tender, pulsatile mass is felt above the umbilicus.
correlates.workup: ESR 88 mm/h, CRP 64 mg/L, creatinine 1.8 mg/dL. CT: 5.4 cm infrarenal aorta wrapped in a thick enhancing rind that tethers the duodenum and left ureter (hydronephrosis). Histology: adventitial fibrosis with macrophages and giant cells.

correlates.name: Innocent murmur of childhood
correlates.presentation: A 4-year-old girl seen for ear pain and a fever of 39.2 C has a grade 2/6 low-pitched, musical systolic ejection sound at the left lower sternal border, louder lying down, softer sitting up. Active, growing on the 50th percentile; normal pulses; S2 splits normally.
correlates.workup: Clinical diagnosis. If checked: ECG and chest film normal; echo shows a structurally normal heart. The sound fades when she is afebrile.
correlates.management: Reassure the family and recheck when she is well; no echocardiogram or cardiology referral unless the sound is grade 4 or louder, harsh, has a thrill, or growth or symptoms suggest heart disease.

correlates.name: Ischemic cardiomyopathy (HFrEF from coronary disease)
correlates.presentation: A 65-year-old man with hypertension, diabetes, high cholesterol and 40 pack-years had hours of crushing chest pain into his left arm a year ago but never sought care. Two weeks of worsening exertional dyspnea, 4-pillow orthopnea. BP 118/76, HR 96; JVP 12 cm, S3, leg edema.
correlates.workup: ECG: Q waves in V2-V4. Echo: dilated left ventricle, thin akinetic anterior wall and apex, EF 30%. Chest film: enlarged heart. Catheterization: occluded proximal left anterior descending artery and an 80% right-sided lesion.
correlates.management: ARNI (sacubitril-valsartan), evidence-based beta blocker, MRA and SGLT2 inhibitor, plus a loop diuretic for congestion; aspirin and high-intensity statin; consider revascularization; ICD if EF stays 35% or less after 3 months of therapy.

correlates.name: Kawasaki disease
correlates.presentation: An 18-month-old boy has had fever to 40.2 C for 6 days, unchanged after 3 days of amoxicillin for a red ear; he is miserable and hard to settle. Both eyes are red with no discharge, lips red and dry, a blotchy rash covers his trunk, the backs of his hands are puffy. HR 160.
correlates.workup: WBC 17,000, Hb 9.8, platelets normal now (700,000 in week 2), ESR 80, CRP 12 mg/dL, albumin 2.9; urine 20 WBC/hpf with a sterile culture; rapid strep negative. Echo: dilated left anterior descending coronary artery (z-score +3).
correlates.management: IVIG within 10 days of fever onset plus high-dose aspirin, then low-dose aspirin for 6-8 weeks (indefinitely if aneurysms form); second IVIG, steroids or anti-TNF if fever persists; serial echocardiograms.

correlates.name: LCAT deficiency
correlates.presentation: 34-year-old woman whose vision has slowly clouded; both corneas show a diffuse grayish haze, densest at the rims. A year of fatigue, pallor, frothy urine and ankle swelling. BP 146/92. Two siblings have the same eye change; no neuropathy, spleen not enlarged.
correlates.workup: HDL 8 mg/dL; plasma cholesterol mostly unesterified (ester fraction <10%); normocytic anemia with target cells; urine protein 3 g/day, creatinine 1.6; kidney biopsy: lipid deposits and foam cells in the glomeruli.
correlates.management: No approved specific therapy: low-fat diet, ACE inhibitor or ARB to slow proteinuric kidney disease, dialysis or kidney transplant for renal failure, corneal transplant for severe clouding; manage cardiovascular risk.

correlates.name: Left ventricular hypertrophy
correlates.presentation: A 61-year-old Black man with 20 years of poorly controlled hypertension has mild exertional breathlessness. BP 178/104, pulse 72. The apical impulse is sustained and displaced laterally, and an S4 is heard just before S1; there is no murmur and no family history of sudden death.
correlates.workup: ECG: S in V1 + R in V5 = 42 mm (>5 large boxes), R in aVL 13 mm, down-sloping ST depression with T inversion in V5-V6. Echo: concentric wall thickening to 1.4 cm, normal valves, EF 65%.
correlates.management: Firm BP control (ACE inhibitor or ARB, thiazide, calcium channel blocker), which can regress the wall thickening; salt restriction and weight loss; look for other hypertensive end-organ damage.

correlates.name: Left ventricular pseudoaneurysm
correlates.presentation: 68-year-old man 10 days after an inferolateral MI that was reperfused late: vague chest discomfort and breathlessness. BP 112/70, HR 90; a new to-and-fro murmur at the apex; neck veins normal; no fever, no positional chest pain.
correlates.workup: Echo/cardiac MRI: a sac off the inferolateral wall joined to the LV by a narrow neck (much smaller than the sac's diameter); its wall is pericardium and organized clot with no myocardium; Doppler flow in during systole, out in diastole.
correlates.management: Urgent surgical repair even if symptoms are mild - this is a contained tear that can rupture completely at any time; control BP meanwhile and avoid anticoagulation where possible.

correlates.name: Libman-Sacks endocarditis
correlates.presentation: A 31-year-old woman with a sun-sensitive facial rash, painful swollen finger joints and two miscarriages has a new soft apical systolic murmur after a brief episode of right-hand weakness. Temp 37.1 C; no injection drug use, no weight loss.
correlates.workup: ANA 1:640, anti-dsDNA positive, low C3 and C4, lupus anticoagulant positive. Three blood cultures negative. TEE: several 2-4 mm sessile masses on both the atrial and ventricular surfaces of the mitral leaflets, with a mild leak.
correlates.management: Treat the underlying autoimmune disease (hydroxychloroquine, immunosuppression as needed); anticoagulate with warfarin when antiphospholipid antibodies or emboli are present; surgery only for severe valve dysfunction.

correlates.name: Lobar pneumonia in an adult
correlates.presentation: An 18-year-old college student has 24 h of fever to 39.4 C, shaking chills, cough with yellow-green sputum and worsening breathlessness. RR 26, HR 112, SpO2 91%. Right front lower chest: dull to percussion, more fremitus, crackles, bronchial breath sounds instead of vesicular.
correlates.workup: WBC 18,500 with 88% neutrophils; procalcitonin raised. Chest film: dense right middle lobe opacity with air-filled bronchi running through it, blurring the right heart border; no effusion. Sputum: lancet-shaped gram-positive diplococci.
correlates.management: Antibiotics: healthy outpatient - amoxicillin or doxycycline; hypoxemic or CURB-65 of 2 or more - admit for ceftriaxone plus azithromycin; oxygen to SpO2 above 92%; fluids and antipyretics.

correlates.name: Loeffler endomyocarditis
correlates.presentation: A 45-year-old man has 3 months of weight loss, night sweats, an itchy rash, cough and breathlessness, then 2 days of right-arm weakness. No new drugs, no travel. BP 104/70, HR 102; JVP 12 cm, apical holosystolic murmur, enlarged liver and spleen, 2+ edema.
correlates.workup: WBC 24,000 with eosinophils 11,000/uL, high for 6 months; FIP1L1-PDGFRA fusion in blood; troponin up. Echo: thick endocardium at both apices with large mural thrombi, small cavities, EF 55%. Biopsy: eosinophil infiltrate, myocyte necrosis.
correlates.management: Imatinib for the PDGFRA-driven clone (glucocorticoids otherwise) to bring eosinophils down; anticoagulate for the mural thrombi; diuretics; late surgical thrombus and scar removal with valve replacement.

correlates.name: Loeys-Dietz syndrome
correlates.presentation: A 14-year-old boy of average height, with widely spaced eyes and recurrent neck pain, has a dilated aortic root found at a sports physical. His sister had an aortic tear at 22. His lenses are normal and his skin is of normal thickness.
correlates.workup: Echo: aortic root 4.4 cm (z-score +4). Head-to-pelvis MR angiography: markedly tortuous neck and head arteries with branch-artery aneurysms. Genetic testing: TGFBR2 variant; FBN1 negative.
correlates.management: Beta blocker or losartan; serial imaging of the whole arterial tree; prophylactic aortic root surgery earlier than in fibrillin disease, because aneurysms here dissect at smaller sizes and younger ages.

correlates.name: Lyme carditis
correlates.presentation: 24-year-old man who hiked in Massachusetts in July: a red patch on his thigh spread to 15 cm 4 weeks ago, then faded untreated. Now 2 days of lightheadedness, fatigue and an aching knee. HR 38, BP 104/66; no murmur, no edema, no recent sore throat.
