correlates.workup: Telemetry: PR 0.30 s progressing to complete heart block with a narrow escape rhythm, then back to first-degree block within minutes. Troponin mildly raised; echo normal. Two-tier serology positive: immunoassay, then IgM/IgG Western blot.
correlates.management: Admit to telemetry; IV ceftriaxone, switching to oral doxycycline once the PR is under 0.30 s; temporary pacing if needed - the block almost always resolves, so a permanent pacemaker is usually unnecessary.

correlates.name: Lymphangiosarcoma (Stewart-Treves)
correlates.presentation: A 66-year-old woman has had a swollen, firm right arm since a mastectomy with axillary node dissection 14 years ago. Over 6 weeks, several painful purple-red nodules and a bruise-like patch have appeared and spread over the upper arm without any injury.
correlates.workup: Skin biopsy: atypical endothelial cells lining irregular, interconnecting vascular channels that dissect through dermal collagen; endothelial markers (CD31) positive.
correlates.management: Wide resection - often amputation of the limb - because it spreads fast and the prognosis is poor. Any new or rapidly changing skin lesion on a chronically swollen limb gets a biopsy.

correlates.name: Lymphatic filariasis
correlates.presentation: A 56-year-old farmer who recently arrived from rural Bangladesh has 3 years of progressive swelling of his right leg. The leg is massively enlarged, firm and tough, with thick, folded, warty skin; it does not pit and does not go down with elevation.
correlates.workup: Blood smear drawn around midnight, Giemsa stain: long, sheathed, cylindrical microfilariae; eosinophils 12%; circulating filarial antigen positive.
correlates.management: Diethylcarbamazine (often with albendazole) for the parasite; lifelong limb care - skin hygiene to prevent infection, compression, elevation and exercise; surgical debulking for severe late swelling.

correlates.name: Marfan syndrome
correlates.presentation: A 19-year-old college basketball player, 6 ft 7 in and slender, is referred after his father died suddenly at 41. He has worn thick glasses for nearsightedness since age 8 and a brace for scoliosis; he does well in school. BP 118/64; a click is heard at the apex in mid-systole.
correlates.workup: Echo: aortic root 4.7 cm at the sinuses with mitral leaflets bowing into the left atrium in systole. Plasma homocysteine normal. Genetic testing: pathogenic FBN1 (fibrillin-1) variant, autosomal dominant.
correlates.management: Beta blocker (or losartan) to cut wall stress; echo every 6-12 months; prophylactic aortic root replacement at a smaller diameter than usual (~5 cm, sooner if growing fast); avoid contact sports and heavy isometric lifting.

correlates.name: Massive pulmonary embolism
correlates.presentation: 66-year-old man on day 4 of a hospital stay for a hip fracture, no prophylaxis given, suddenly collapses gasping while straining on the commode. BP 72/40, HR 132, RR 34, SpO2 82% on 6 L; neck veins distended; cold, mottled legs; lungs clear; heart sounds normal.
correlates.workup: Too unstable for CT: bedside echo shows a dilated, hypokinetic RV pushing the septum into a small, underfilled LV and no pericardial fluid; troponin and BNP elevated; ECG sinus tachycardia with a new rightward axis.
correlates.management: Systemic thrombolysis (tPA) at the bedside unless contraindicated; surgical or catheter clot removal if lysis fails or is contraindicated; heparin; cautious fluid and norepinephrine for BP; never send an unstable patient to the scanner.

correlates.name: May-Thurner syndrome
correlates.presentation: A 32-year-old woman has months of swelling of her entire left leg with varicose veins and a tight, aching leg when she exercises; now the left calf is tender and 4 cm larger than the right. The right leg is normal. No recent surgery, travel or cancer.
correlates.workup: Duplex: occlusive thrombus in the left femoral vein; the left common iliac vein is flattened between the overlying right common iliac artery and the lumbar spine (confirmed on CT venography or intravascular ultrasound).
correlates.management: Anticoagulate the clot (catheter-directed thrombolysis if extensive), then stent the left common iliac vein to relieve the outflow obstruction; compression stockings.

correlates.name: Meconium aspiration syndrome
correlates.presentation: Girl born at 41 weeks after fetal heart-rate decelerations, delivered through thick, dark green, foul-smelling amniotic fluid: limp with blue hands and feet, Apgar 5 and 6. In the NICU: grunting, nasal flaring, intercostal retractions, RR 70, deep chest, diffuse rhonchi.
correlates.workup: CXR: hyperinflated lungs, flattened diaphragms, coarse patchy streaky opacities, small right pneumothorax. ABG on 100% O2: pH 7.18, PaCO2 62, PaO2 38. Right-hand SpO2 92% vs foot 78%; echo: right-to-left shunt across the ductus.
correlates.management: Assisted ventilation and surfactant; antibiotics until sepsis is excluded; inhaled nitric oxide for the high pulmonary vascular resistance; ECMO if all of these fail.

correlates.name: Metabolic alkalosis from vomiting
correlates.presentation: 36-year-old woman who has vomited many times a day for 3 days with a stomach virus; light-headed on standing, leg cramps. BP 102/64 lying, 84/52 standing; HR 114; dry mucous membranes, flat neck veins. No diuretic or antacid use.
correlates.workup: ABG pH 7.50, HCO3- 37, PCO2 48 (0.6 x 13 predicts 47.8 - simple, compensated); Na+ 135, K+ 2.9, Cl- 84; urine Cl- 8 mEq/L (low despite a high urine Na+ from bicarbonaturia); renin and aldosterone high.
correlates.management: IV isotonic saline (the chloride-responsive kind) with KCl replacement; restoring volume removes the angiotensin II/aldosterone drive so the kidney can excrete the extra HCO3-; antiemetic and treat the cause.

correlates.name: Metabolic syndrome
correlates.presentation: 52-year-old man, sedentary office worker with no diabetes history, in for a check-up. Waist 107 cm (42 in), BMI 31, BP 136/86 on two visits; dark, velvety skin on the back of the neck. His father has type 2 diabetes.
correlates.workup: Fasting glucose 108 mg/dL, A1c 5.9%, fasting insulin high; TG 190, HDL 36, LDL 128 mg/dL; ALT, TSH and urine albumin normal.
correlates.management: Lifestyle first: 7-10% weight loss, 150+ min/week of moderate exercise, DASH or Mediterranean pattern low in refined carbohydrate and added sugar; then treat each component (statin, antihypertensive, metformin if glucose progresses).

correlates.name: Methanol or ethylene glycol poisoning
correlates.presentation: 45-year-old man with alcohol use disorder found confused in his garage beside an empty unlabeled jug, ~12 h after drinking from it. Deep, fast breathing (RR 28), HR 110, BP 130/80, afebrile, no tinnitus; says his vision is blurry. Glucose 92 on fingerstick.
correlates.workup: Na+ 140, Cl- 102, HCO3- 8 (gap 30), PCO2 21, pH 7.20; measured osm 330 vs calculated 290 (osmolar gap 40); ketones negative, lactate 2.8 - too small to explain the gap; aspirin level undetectable.
correlates.management: Fomepizole at once to block alcohol dehydrogenase (ethanol if unavailable); IV bicarbonate for severe acidemia; hemodialysis for severe acidosis, vision or kidney injury, or high levels; cofactors (folate; thiamine and pyridoxine).

correlates.name: Mitral annular calcification
correlates.presentation: A 74-year-old woman with 30 years of hypertension, dyslipidemia and stage 3 chronic kidney disease feels well. BP 162/88, pulse 70 and regular, afebrile. A soft grade 2/6 apical systolic murmur is heard; there is no diastolic rumble and no extra diastolic sound.
correlates.workup: Echo: a dense, irregular, stony ring of calcium in the fibrous annulus at the base of the posterior leaflet, with one ulcerated nodule; the leaflet tips are thin and mobile without commissural fusion; mild backflow.
correlates.management: No specific therapy for the deposit itself; treat it as a marker of atherosclerosis - control BP and lipids and evaluate for coronary disease; manage any associated leak or narrowing on its own merits.

correlates.name: Mitral valve prolapse
correlates.presentation: A 27-year-old thin woman has occasional palpitations and brief atypical chest twinges. A mid-systolic click at the apex is followed by a short late-systolic murmur; on standing the click moves toward S1 and the murmur lengthens, and a passive leg raise moves the click toward S2.
correlates.workup: Echo: thickened, redundant posterior leaflet bulging >2 mm above the annulus into the left atrium in systole, with elongated chordae and only a trace leak. Histology if excised: disorganized fibrosa and a proteoglycan-expanded spongiosa.
correlates.management: Reassurance and periodic echo while the leak stays trivial; beta blocker for palpitations; surgical repair if it progresses to severe regurgitation.

correlates.name: Multifocal atrial tachycardia
correlates.presentation: A 74-year-old man with severe COPD, admitted 2 days ago for an exacerbation, notices a racing, uneven heartbeat. Pulse 124 and irregular, BP 142/84, RR 24, SpO2 88% on 2 L. He is on nebulized albuterol and IV methylprednisolone.
correlates.workup: ECG: narrow QRS at 124/min, irregular; a P wave precedes every QRS, but the P waves take at least 3 different shapes with varying PR intervals, and the baseline between beats is flat. Mg2+ 1.3 mg/dL, K+ 3.2 mEq/L.
correlates.management: Treat the lung disease and hypoxemia; replace magnesium and potassium; verapamil (or diltiazem) if the rate needs slowing; cardioversion does not help.

correlates.name: Mycotic aneurysm
correlates.presentation: A 68-year-old man with diabetes has 10 days of fever to 39.4 C, chills and new constant back and abdominal pain, 3 weeks after a hospital stay for an infected foot ulcer with bacteremia. BP 132/80, pulse 108. A tender pulsatile mass is felt in the upper abdomen.
correlates.workup: WBC 18,000/uL; blood cultures: gram-positive cocci in clusters. CT angiogram: a new lobulated saccular outpouching of the infrarenal aorta with surrounding stranding and fluid (absent on CT a year ago). Transesophageal echo: normal valves.
correlates.management: Prolonged IV antibiotics guided by cultures plus early surgical debridement of the infected aorta with reconstruction - infected outpouchings expand and rupture quickly.

correlates.name: Neonatal respiratory distress syndrome
correlates.presentation: A boy born at 29 weeks to a mother with poorly controlled diabetes, who got no steroids before delivery, starts grunting, flaring his nostrils and pulling in between the ribs within minutes of birth, worsening over hours. RR 78, HR 168, SpO2 84% on room air; quiet breath sounds.
correlates.workup: Chest film: low lung volumes with a uniform fine granular haze in both lungs and air-filled bronchi standing out against it. ABG on 40% O2: pH 7.22, PaCO2 58, PaO2 42. Amniotic fluid lecithin-to-sphingomyelin ratio had been 1.2.
correlates.management: Early CPAP, then intubation with surfactant through the tube if oxygen needs rise; use the least oxygen that works (eye and lung injury); prevention: antenatal corticosteroids when delivery before 34 weeks is expected.

correlates.name: Nephrogenic diabetes insipidus
correlates.presentation: A 45-year-old woman with bipolar disorder, on lithium for 12 years, has 6 months of passing 6-8 L of urine daily and waking 4 times a night to drink. BP 122/76, HR 84; normal mental status. Blood sugar and calcium have been normal.
correlates.workup: Na+ 147 mEq/L, serum osm 302, urine osm 150 mOsm/kg; glucose 90, Ca2+ 9.4, K+ 4.0. Fluid restriction: urine osm stays below 200. After desmopressin, urine osm 160 (essentially unchanged); plasma ADH high.
correlates.management: Stop or switch the offending drug if psychiatry allows (damage may be permanent after years of exposure); amiloride to block its entry into collecting-duct cells; thiazide with a low-sodium, low-protein diet to cut urine volume.

correlates.name: Neurogenic claudication (lumbar spinal stenosis)
correlates.presentation: A 71-year-old man has burning, tingling pain in both buttocks and thighs when walking or standing; some days he manages 10 blocks, other days 3. Standing still does not help - he must sit or bend forward, and he cycles on a stationary bike pain-free. Pedal pulses 2+ bilaterally.
correlates.workup: Ankle-brachial ratio 1.1 on both sides. MRI of the low back: L4-L5 canal narrowed by facet and ligamentum flavum hypertrophy. Back extension reproduces the leg symptoms.
correlates.management: Physical therapy with flexion-based exercise, NSAIDs and weight loss; epidural steroid injection or decompressive laminectomy if disabling. No vascular work-up needed when pulses and ankle-brachial index are normal.

correlates.name: New left bundle branch block
correlates.presentation: A 64-year-old man with diabetes and hypertension has 40 minutes of crushing substernal pressure with sweating. BP 146/92, pulse 98. S2 is split in expiration and becomes single on inspiration. A routine ECG a year ago showed narrow QRS complexes.
correlates.workup: ECG: QRS 150 ms; V1-V3 wide and mainly negative with deep S waves; I, aVL and V6 broad, notched R waves; left axis deviation; ST-T opposite the main QRS deflection. Troponin rising.
correlates.management: Treat as a possible acute MI: aspirin, heparin and urgent coronary angiography with reperfusion while ischemic symptoms continue; compare every tracing with the old ECG.

correlates.name: Niemann-Pick disease type C
correlates.presentation: 9-year-old girl, normal until age 7, with 2 years of clumsiness, falling grades and slurred speech, plus spells of sudden limpness when she laughs. She cannot move her eyes up or down on command, though side-to-side gaze is full. Spleen palpable 3 cm below the costal margin.
correlates.workup: Lipid panel unremarkable; cultured skin fibroblasts: unesterified cholesterol trapped in lysosomes, bright on filipin staining; plasma oxysterols high; MRI: cerebellar atrophy.
correlates.management: No cure: miglustat (substrate reduction) can slow neurologic decline; supportive care - antiseizure drugs, physical, speech and feeding therapy; genetic counseling (autosomal recessive).

correlates.name: Non-anion-gap metabolic acidosis from diarrhea
correlates.presentation: 29-year-old man back from a trip abroad with 6 days of 10-12 watery stools a day; weak and thirsty. BP 98/60, HR 112, RR 24, dry mucous membranes; abdomen soft. No vomiting, no new medicines.
correlates.workup: Na+ 138, Cl- 114, HCO3- 14 - gap 10 (normal); K+ 3.0; pH 7.32, PCO2 28 (fits 1.2 rule); urine pH 5.0; urine Na+ 12, K+ 30, Cl- 67 (Na+ + K+ - Cl- = -25: NH4+ excretion intact); BUN 34, creatinine 1.4.
correlates.management: IV isotonic fluid (lactated Ringer or saline) with K+ replacement; oral bicarbonate or citrate only if acidemia is severe; oral rehydration and treatment of the cause once stable.

correlates.name: Nonalcoholic fatty liver disease
correlates.presentation: 49-year-old woman, BMI 36, with type 2 diabetes and hypertension, has fatigue and a dull ache under the right ribs. Drinks less than 1 drink a week; no hepatitis risk factors; no jaundice or confusion. A smooth, slightly enlarged hepatic edge is felt 3 cm below the costal margin.
correlates.workup: ALT 82, AST 54 (ALT > AST); alkaline phosphatase and bilirubin normal; hepatitis B and C negative; ultrasound: diffusely bright, echogenic hepatic parenchyma; biopsy: large triglyceride droplets pushing hepatocyte nuclei aside.
correlates.management: Gradual 7-10% weight loss with diet and exercise; control diabetes (GLP-1 agonist or pioglitazone help), lipids and BP; avoid alcohol; vaccinate against hepatitis A and B; stage fibrosis (FIB-4, elastography).

correlates.name: Nonbacterial thrombotic (marantic) endocarditis
correlates.presentation: 66-year-old woman with metastatic mucin-producing pancreatic adenocarcinoma: sudden right arm weakness and slurred speech, then left flank pain with hematuria 2 days later. T 36.9 C, HR 84; soft apical murmur; no injection drug use, no rash, no leg swelling.
correlates.workup: TEE: several 3-5 mm sessile masses along the closure line of otherwise normal mitral leaflets, no leaflet destruction. Blood bottles sterile x3 with no prior antibiotics. D-dimer 4.8 ug/mL; antiphospholipid antibodies and ANA negative.
correlates.management: Therapeutic heparin (unfractionated or low-molecular-weight; warfarin works poorly here); treat the underlying cancer; antibiotics are not indicated.

correlates.name: Noonan syndrome
correlates.presentation: 7-year-old boy at the 3rd height centile; his father is short with a similar face. Wide-set downslanting eyes, droopy lids, low-set ears, extra neck skin, sunken lower sternum, one undescended testis, bruises easily. Harsh systolic murmur at the left upper sternal border.
correlates.workup: Karyotype 46,XY. Echo: thickened, poorly mobile pulmonary valve with a 50 mmHg gradient; asymmetric septal thickening. PTT prolonged, factor XI low. Gene panel: pathogenic PTPN11 variant (RAS-MAPK pathway).
correlates.management: Gene panel or sequencing (karyotype is normal); balloon or surgical relief of the pulmonary valve gradient; serial echo for ventricular hypertrophy; clotting work-up before any surgery; growth hormone for height; counsel 50% recurrence.

correlates.name: NSTEMI
correlates.presentation: 66-year-old woman with diabetes and CKD: 3 hours of pressure in the chest and jaw at rest with nausea and sweating, not relieved by 2 SL nitroglycerin. BP 150/88, HR 104, SpO2 96%, lungs clear, no murmur.
correlates.workup: ECG: 2 mm horizontal ST depression in V3-V6 and T inversion in I and aVL, no ST elevation, no new bundle branch block; troponin I 0.9 ng/mL on arrival rising to 3.4 at 4 h; CK-MB up; echo: lateral hypokinesis.
correlates.management: Aspirin plus a P2Y12 inhibitor, heparin, beta blocker, nitrates, high-intensity statin, ACE inhibitor; never fibrinolysis; urgent angiography/PCI in 24-48 h - immediate if shock, refractory pain, new MR or septal defect, or sustained VT.

correlates.name: Obstructive sleep apnea
correlates.presentation: A 54-year-old man with BMI 38, a small receding jaw and BP 158/96 on three drugs dozes off at red lights and in meetings. His wife reports loud snoring and long pauses in his breathing at night; he wakes choking, with morning headaches. Neck 18 inches; crowded oropharynx.
correlates.workup: Overnight polysomnography: 34 events per hour in which airflow stops while the chest and abdomen keep straining; SpO2 dips to 78%; daytime drowsiness score 16/24. Hct 50%. Holter: paroxysms of AF.
correlates.management: Nightly CPAP; weight loss; no alcohol or sedatives at night; side positioning; oral jaw-advancement device or upper-airway surgery if CPAP fails; BP control improves with treatment.

correlates.name: Orthostatic hypotension from dehydration
correlates.presentation: An 18-year-old woman who drank alcohol last night, overslept and had nothing to eat or drink stands up in her 8 a.m. class, feels lightheaded and sweaty, and passes out for about 1 minute. Afebrile, HR 120, BP 132/72 seated; regular rhythm, no murmur; dry lips.
correlates.workup: Lying BP 128/76, HR 96; after 3 min standing BP 98/60, HR 132 with lightheadedness. ECG: sinus rhythm at 120, QTc 420 ms. BUN 24, creatinine 0.9, urine specific gravity 1.030; glucose 88 mg/dL.
correlates.management: Oral (or IV) fluids and salt; rise slowly from lying or sitting; avoid alcohol and skipped meals; reassure. Re-evaluate if an ECG shows a long QT or episodes happen with exercise.

correlates.name: Osmotic demyelination syndrome
correlates.presentation: A 61-year-old man who drinks heavily was admitted with Na+ 116 mEq/L, low for at least a week. He got large volumes of hypertonic saline and Na+ rose 18 mEq/L in 24 h. He brightened, then on day 3 had slurred speech, poor swallowing, double vision and weakness of all four limbs.
correlates.workup: Na+ 136 mEq/L on day 3 (116 on admission); glucose and calcium normal. MRI brain 2 weeks later: symmetric bright T2 lesion in the center of the pons, sparing its outer rim; CSF unremarkable.
correlates.management: Prevention is the treatment: in low Na+ present >48 h, raise it 4-6 and never more than 10 mEq/L in any 24 h; if it overshoots, re-lower Na+ with D5W and desmopressin; supportive care.

correlates.name: Papillary fibroelastoma
correlates.presentation: 69-year-old woman: two 20-minute episodes of right-hand weakness and word-finding trouble in the past month. Afebrile, BP 138/82, regular pulse, no murmur, no weight loss. Carotid duplex shows no stenosis; no cancer, no lupus, no recent procedures.
correlates.workup: TEE: 9 mm highly mobile mass on a short stalk on the aortic side of the right coronary cusp, with many fine frond-like arms; valve function normal. Blood cultures sterile, ESR normal. Histology: avascular fronds with collagen-elastic cores.
correlates.management: Surgical excision of left-sided lesions (they embolize to the brain and coronary ostia), usually sparing the valve; antiplatelet therapy if not operated; right-sided lesions are a harder risk-benefit call.

correlates.name: Papillary muscle rupture
correlates.presentation: 71-year-old man on day 4 after an inferior STEMI: sudden severe breathlessness, pink frothy sputum, cannot lie flat. BP 86/54, HR 124, RR 34, SpO2 84%; crackles to both apices; a new holosystolic apical murmur radiating to the axilla, which may be soft; no thrill.
correlates.workup: Echo: flail posterior mitral leaflet with a torn chordal head whipping into the left atrium and severe eccentric regurgitation; hyperdynamic LV; PCWP 32 mmHg with giant v waves; no O2 step-up from RA to RV; CXR: bilateral alveolar edema.
correlates.management: Afterload reduction (IV nitroprusside), intra-aortic balloon pump or other mechanical support, diuretics and ventilation as a bridge to emergent mitral valve repair or replacement, with coronary revascularization at the same time.

correlates.name: Paradoxical embolism (patent foramen ovale or ASD)
correlates.presentation: A 34-year-old woman has sudden right arm weakness and trouble finding words the day after a 14-hour flight; her left calf has been swollen and tender since she landed. BP 124/78, pulse 88 and regular; no murmur; no carotid bruits.
correlates.workup: MRI: acute left MCA-territory infarct. Leg duplex: left popliteal vein thrombus. Agitated-saline echo: bubbles reach the left atrium within 3 beats, more after Valsalva release. Carotid duplex and rhythm monitoring normal.
correlates.management: Antiplatelet therapy for the stroke and anticoagulation for the leg clot; percutaneous closure of the interatrial opening in selected young patients with no other cause found.

correlates.name: Patent ductus arteriosus
correlates.presentation: A baby born at 27 weeks, now 10 days old on CPAP, needs more oxygen, has had two apneic spells and is not tolerating feeds. HR 168, BP 52/24 (58/36 on day 3); active precordium; a new 2/6 murmur below the left clavicle that carries on past S2; liver edge normal.
correlates.workup: Echo: a 2.5-mm channel joining the descending aorta to the main pulmonary artery with continuous left-to-right flow; enlarged left atrium (LA:aortic root 1.8); reversed diastolic flow in the descending aorta. Chest film: more lung markings.
correlates.management: Indomethacin (or ibuprofen) to close it - the opposite of prostaglandin; restrict fluids; if that fails, catheter coil/device closure or surgical ligation.

correlates.name: Pectus excavatum
correlates.presentation: A 15-year-old boy notes his breastbone has sunk deeper during his growth spurt; on long runs he tires and gets breathless before teammates, with a racing heart. Average height, normal arm span and eyes. HR 88, BP 112/70; lower sternum 3 cm below the ribs; soft systolic murmur.
correlates.workup: CT: sternum displaced backward, transverse-to-AP chest ratio 4.2, right ventricle compressed. PFTs: total lung capacity 80% predicted. Exercise test: reduced peak O2 uptake. Echo: structurally normal heart and valves.
correlates.management: Mild or no symptoms: reassurance, posture and exercise - it need not end sport. Cardiac or lung compression or exercise limitation: surgical correction (minimally invasive bar or open repair); check for a connective-tissue disorder.

correlates.name: Pediatric asthma exacerbation
correlates.presentation: 9-year-old boy with eczema and a mother with hay fever: 10 hours of wheeze and breathlessness after a 3-day cold, not relieved by one home albuterol nebulizer. Speaks in short phrases with suprasternal retractions; RR 38, HR 128, SpO2 90%; expiratory wheeze in all fields.
correlates.workup: Peak flow 45% of personal best; after albuterol plus ipratropium: HR 90, RR 20, SpO2 98%. Interval history: daily symptoms at recess, waking with wheeze 2 nights a week, runs out of his rescue inhaler early. Eosinophils 600/uL.
correlates.management: Repeated nebulized albuterol with ipratropium, oral corticosteroid burst, oxygen to keep SpO2 above 92%; then a daily inhaled corticosteroid (moderate persistent step), trigger avoidance and a written green-yellow-red action plan.

correlates.name: Peripartum cardiomyopathy
correlates.presentation: A 34-year-old woman, 5 weeks after delivering twins, has 2 weeks of breathlessness lying flat, waking at night gasping, and more leg swelling than she had while pregnant. No prior heart disease. BP 112/74, HR 110, RR 24; JVP 11 cm, S3, bibasilar crackles.
correlates.workup: BNP 1,200 pg/mL; troponin normal; TSH normal. ECG: sinus tachycardia, no Q waves. Echo: dilated left ventricle with global hypokinesis, EF 28%, normal valves; an echo at 20 weeks of this pregnancy was normal.
correlates.management: Guideline reduced-EF therapy compatible with breastfeeding (beta blocker, enalapril, loop diuretic); anticoagulate if EF is very low; about half regain normal function, but it can recur - counsel about future pregnancy.

correlates.name: Peripheral artery disease with intermittent claudication
correlates.presentation: A 68-year-old woman with diabetes, hypertension and 30 pack-years of smoking stops halfway through her 1-mile walk with right upper-calf cramping; it settles after 3 minutes standing still and recurs at the same point every morning. Right popliteal and pedal pulses are weak.
correlates.workup: Highest right ankle pressure 93 / highest brachial 150 mmHg = ratio 0.62; left 0.95. Duplex: peak systolic velocity triples just beyond a popliteal plaque. No rest pain, no tissue loss.
correlates.management: Stop smoking; supervised graded walking; statin plus aspirin or clopidogrel; cilostazol (PDE3 inhibitor) for symptoms only; glucose and BP control. Stent or bypass if >70% stenosis with disabling symptoms, or rest pain or tissue loss.

correlates.name: Persistent truncus arteriosus
correlates.presentation: A 10-day-old boy breathes fast, sweats with feeds and is not regaining birth weight. Mildly blue: SpO2 88% in arm and leg alike. HR 170, RR 70, BP 70/30; harsh holosystolic murmur at the left sternal border, a single loud second heart sound, liver 3 cm below the ribs.
correlates.workup: Chest film: mildly enlarged heart with increased, streaky lung markings. ECG: both ventricles enlarged. Echo: one large vessel rides over a large VSD and gives off the coronary, pulmonary and systemic arteries; no separate pulmonary valve.
correlates.management: Surgical repair in the neonatal period (close the VSD, connect the right ventricle to the pulmonary arteries with a conduit); diuretics for heart failure meanwhile; screen for the 22q11.2 microdeletion.

correlates.name: Post-mastectomy lymphedema
correlates.presentation: A 54-year-old woman had left breast cancer surgery with axillary node dissection and radiation 3 years ago. Her left arm has swollen gradually: at first it pitted and went down overnight; now it is firm, heavy and only partly better with elevation. Skin intact, no masses.
correlates.workup: Mostly a clinical diagnosis: left arm 4 cm larger in circumference, non-tender, no skin lesions; venous duplex normal. Lymphoscintigraphy, if done, shows delayed tracer transit with dermal backflow.
correlates.management: Compression garments and exercise (muscle contraction moves lymph), manual decompressive therapy (gold standard), pneumatic compression and lymphatic OMT; liposuction for long-standing fat-rich swelling; prompt treatment of skin infection.

correlates.name: Post-thrombotic syndrome
correlates.presentation: 55-year-old man treated for a left femoral-popliteal clot 4 years ago: the left leg now swells, aches and feels heavy by evening and improves with elevation. Brown skin and hard, thickened tissue above the inner ankle, with a shallow weeping ulcer there; varicosities.
correlates.workup: Duplex: thickened, partly recanalized femoral and popliteal veins with reflux >1 s on standing (incompetent valves) and no fresh clot; ankle-brachial index 1.05 (arterial supply normal).
correlates.management: Graded compression stockings or multilayer bandages and leg elevation; ulcer wound care (hyperbaric therapy in selected cases); walking program; vascular surgery referral for the obstructed or refluxing segment.

correlates.name: Postsurgical hypoparathyroidism
correlates.presentation: A 46-year-old woman is 36 h past a total thyroidectomy for a large multinodular goiter. She has tingling of the lips and fingertips and cramping hands; her wrist and fingers flex into spasm when the BP cuff inflates. HR 88, BP 128/80; voice normal.
correlates.workup: Ca2+ 6.8 mg/dL with low ionized calcium, albumin 4.0, phosphate 6.2, intact PTH 4 pg/mL (low), Mg2+ 1.9, creatinine 0.8. ECG QTc 500 ms.
correlates.management: IV calcium gluconate with cardiac monitoring for symptoms; then oral calcium plus calcitriol; check and correct magnesium; lifelong calcium and vitamin D if gland function does not return.

correlates.name: Primary adrenal insufficiency
correlates.presentation: A 41-year-old woman with vitiligo and treated hypothyroidism has 4 months of fatigue, salt craving, nausea, 6-kg weight loss and dizziness on standing. Her skin has darkened, most in the palm creases and gums. BP 92/58 lying, 76/50 standing; HR 104.
correlates.workup: Na+ 128, K+ 5.9, HCO3- 19, glucose 64; urine Na+ 45 mEq/L despite volume depletion; 8 a.m. cortisol 2 ug/dL with ACTH 480 pg/mL (high); after cosyntropin, cortisol peaks at 4 ug/dL; renin high, aldosterone low.
correlates.management: Hydrocortisone plus fludrocortisone for life; in a crisis, IV hydrocortisone with isotonic saline and dextrose before any test result; teach stress dosing for illness and surgery.

correlates.name: Primary ciliary dyskinesia (Kartagener syndrome)
correlates.presentation: 28-year-old man seen for infertility: normal sperm count, but no sperm move. Lifelong daily wet cough, constant runny nose and sinus infections, ear tubes as a child, oxygen for 2 days after birth. Heart sounds loudest right of the sternum; crackles at both lung bases.
correlates.workup: CXR: cardiac apex and stomach bubble on the right. CT: dilated lower-lobe bronchi, opacified sinuses. Sweat chloride 18 mmol/L; nasal nitric oxide very low. Electron microscopy of a nasal brushing: outer dynein arms absent, cilia immotile.
correlates.management: Daily airway clearance and exercise; culture-guided antibiotics for flares; ENT care for sinus and ear disease; IVF with sperm injection (ICSI) for infertility; vaccines; counsel autosomal recessive inheritance (25% risk per sibling).

correlates.name: Primary hyperaldosteronism
correlates.presentation: A 44-year-old woman has BP 172/106 on repeat visits despite full-dose amlodipine; she takes no diuretic or laxative and eats no licorice. She reports muscle cramps, fatigue and constipation. No edema, no weight gain, no purple striae or central fat.
correlates.workup: K+ 2.9 mEq/L, HCO3- 31, Na+ 144; 24-h urine K+ 70 mmol (renal loss); plasma aldosterone 32 ng/dL with suppressed renin activity (aldosterone/renin ratio >30); CT: 1.5-cm left adrenal nodule.
correlates.management: Unilateral adenoma: laparoscopic adrenalectomy after adrenal vein sampling confirms the side; bilateral hyperplasia or poor surgical candidate: spironolactone or eplerenone; oral KCl until then.

correlates.name: Primary hyperparathyroidism
correlates.presentation: A 58-year-old woman has 8 months of fatigue, constipation, low mood and forgetfulness, and passed a kidney stone in the spring. She takes no thiazide, lithium or calcium supplement and has not lost weight. BP 138/84, HR 64; exam otherwise normal.
correlates.workup: Ca2+ 11.4 mg/dL (10.8-11.6 on every check for 2 years), phosphate 2.2, intact PTH 112 pg/mL (high), PTH-related peptide undetectable; creatinine 0.9; ECG QTc 350 ms. Neck scan: one focus of tracer uptake below the left thyroid lobe.
correlates.management: Surgical removal of the single overactive gland, especially with symptoms, stones, bone loss or Ca2+ >1 mg/dL above normal; meanwhile hydrate and avoid thiazides and high calcium intake.

correlates.name: Primary polydipsia
correlates.presentation: A 38-year-old man with schizophrenia on a stable antipsychotic is brought in by group-home staff, who say he drinks from the bathroom taps all day - about 12 L. Headache, nausea and fatigue. BP 126/78, HR 74; moist mucosa, normal skin turgor, no edema.
correlates.workup: Na+ 129 mEq/L, serum osm 250 mOsm/kg, urine osm 50 mOsm/kg (maximally dilute), urine Na+ 15; glucose, lipids, protein, TSH and cortisol normal. With fluid restriction the urine concentrates and Na+ recovers on its own.
correlates.management: Restrict intake and address the drinking behavior; emergent hypertonic saline only for seizures or coma, aiming +4-6 and never more than 10 mEq/L in 24 h; the kidney's large dilute output can overshoot, so recheck Na+ often.

correlates.name: Prosthetic valve endocarditis
correlates.presentation: 75-year-old man 7 weeks after surgical aortic replacement with a mechanical prosthesis: 3 weeks of evening temperatures to 38.3 C and fatigue. BP 118/50, new early diastolic murmur, INR 2.8. ECG: PR interval lengthened from 0.18 s to 0.28 s since discharge.
correlates.workup: Blood cultures 4/4: gram-positive cocci in clusters, catalase-positive, coagulase-negative, novobiocin-sensitive. TEE: paravalvular leak, a 1.2 cm abscess cavity in the aortic root and a mobile mass on the sewing ring.
correlates.management: Cultures before antibiotics; vancomycin plus rifampin for at least 6 weeks with gentamicin for the first 2; early redo surgery for the root abscess, dehiscence or new heart block.

correlates.name: Proximal (type 2) renal tubular acidosis
correlates.presentation: 67-year-old man started on acetazolamide for glaucoma 6 weeks ago now has tingling fingers, fatigue and mild nausea. BP 132/80, HR 80, RR 20; exam otherwise normal. No bone pain, no polyuria, no kidney disease history.
correlates.workup: Na+ 140, Cl- 113, HCO3- 16 - gap 11; K+ 3.3; urine pH 5.2 at steady state, rising above 7.5 with fractional HCO3- excretion >15% during an IV bicarbonate load; urine has no glucose (serum 94), no amino acids and normal phosphate.
correlates.management: Stop or replace the carbonic anhydrase inhibitor. When alkali is needed it takes large doses (10-15 mEq/kg/day) plus K+, because extra filtered HCO3- is simply wasted; a thiazide can help by mild volume contraction.

correlates.name: Pseudohyperkalemia
correlates.presentation: A 34-year-old man at a routine physical feels well and takes no medications. BP 122/78, HR 70, normal strength and reflexes. The draw took three sticks with a 25-gauge needle and a tight tourniquet while he pumped his fist; the tube sat 4 h before reaching the lab. K+ 6.4 mEq/L.
correlates.workup: Lab flags the specimen as moderately hemolysed. Creatinine 0.9 mg/dL, glucose 92, HCO3- 25. ECG: normal P waves, PR, QRS and T waves. Repeat K+ from a free-flowing large-bore draw in the other arm, run promptly: 4.3 mEq/L.
correlates.management: Treat the patient, not the number: repeat the level first with a clean draw (large-bore needle, never from a limb with a running IV - stop it 30 min and draw distal), get it to the lab fast; no calcium, insulin or binder.

correlates.name: Pseudohypoparathyroidism
correlates.presentation: An 11-year-old boy has months of tingling around the mouth and painful hand cramps, and had a brief generalized seizure last month. His height is below the 3rd percentile and his fourth and fifth fingers are short. No neck surgery, normal diet, no kidney disease.
correlates.workup: Ca2+ 6.9 mg/dL, phosphate 6.8, intact PTH 240 pg/mL (high), 25-OH vitamin D 34 ng/mL, Mg2+ 2.0, BUN and creatinine normal. ECG QTc 490 ms.
correlates.management: Oral calcium plus calcitriol (active vitamin D) to keep calcium low-normal, monitoring urine calcium; giving PTH would not help because target tissues do not respond to it.

correlates.name: Pulmonary arterial hypertension
correlates.presentation: 31-year-old woman with a year of worsening breathlessness and fatigue on exertion and two near-faints climbing stairs; her mother died at 40 of a similar illness. Never smoked, no heart or lung history. Loud P2, left parasternal lift, JVP 9 cm, mild ankle edema, lungs clear.
correlates.workup: ECG: right-axis deviation, tall R in V1; CXR: large central pulmonary arteries that taper fast toward the periphery; echo: dilated thick RV, normal LV; right heart cath: mPAP 48, wedge 9 mmHg; normal PFTs and V/Q scan.
correlates.management: Vasoreactivity test during right heart cath; pulmonary vasodilators (endothelin receptor antagonist, PDE-5 inhibitor, prostacyclin analog; high-dose CCB only if vasoreactive); diuretics and O2 as needed; lung transplant if refractory.

correlates.name: Pulmonary infarction
correlates.presentation: 71-year-old man with left heart failure (EF 25%), mostly in bed for 2 weeks, has 2 days of sharp right chest pain on breathing in, bright-red hemoptysis and a low fever. HR 104, RR 24, BP 118/74, SpO2 92%; a scratchy sound over the right lower chest; dull right base.
correlates.workup: CXR: pleural-based, wedge-shaped right lower-lobe opacity with its apex toward the hilum and a small effusion; CT angiogram: occluded subsegmental artery supplying that area; histology: hemorrhagic necrosis of alveolar walls.
correlates.management: Anticoagulate as for any lung-artery clot; analgesia for the pleuritic pain; optimize the heart failure (poor bronchial back-up flow let the tissue die); antibiotics only if the area becomes infected or cavitates.

correlates.name: Pulmonic regurgitation
correlates.presentation: A 24-year-old woman had repair of a cyanotic heart defect with a patch across her right ventricular outflow in infancy; she now tires with exercise. BP 118/76. A high-pitched early diastolic decrescendo murmur at the left 3rd intercostal space grows louder on inspiration.
correlates.workup: Cardiac MRI: wide diastolic backflow jet from the main pulmonary artery into a dilated right ventricle (end-diastolic volume 165 mL/m2) with normal LV size and a normal root. A late, palpable P2 at the left upper sternal border.
correlates.management: Serial MRI of RV size and function; pulmonary valve replacement (surgical or transcatheter) when symptomatic or the RV keeps dilating.

correlates.name: Pulmonic stenosis
correlates.presentation: A 22-year-old man has exertional chest tightness and fatigue. BP 118/74, pulse 72. A harsh, high-pitched crescendo-decrescendo systolic murmur at the left 2nd intercostal space radiates to the left shoulder and neck, louder on inspiration; S2 widely split; left parasternal heave.
correlates.workup: Echo: thickened, domed right ventricular outflow valve with dilation of the main pulmonary artery beyond it; peak gradient 64 mmHg; right ventricular hypertrophy. ECG: right axis deviation.
correlates.management: Percutaneous balloon valvuloplasty for a significant gradient or symptoms; surgical valvotomy if the leaflets are dysplastic; look for an underlying carcinoid or syndromic cause.

correlates.name: Refeeding syndrome
correlates.presentation: A 19-year-old woman with anorexia nervosa (BMI 13.8) is admitted and started on full-calorie tube feeds. On day 3 she becomes weak, breathless and confused, then has a seizure. BP 94/58, HR 118; new ankle swelling; her urine turns red-brown.
correlates.workup: Phosphate 0.8 mg/dL (2.9 on admission), K+ 2.9, Mg2+ 1.2, glucose 160; CK 9,800 U/L; 24-h urine phosphate 60 mg (kidney conserving - phosphate has moved into cells). ECG: frequent runs of ventricular ectopy.
correlates.management: Slow the feeds; IV phosphate (symptomatic and <1.0 mg/dL), plus K+ and Mg2+; thiamine before more carbohydrate; cardiac monitoring. In the next starved patient, start calories low and advance slowly.

correlates.name: Reinfarction after recent MI
correlates.presentation: 59-year-old man on day 5 after a STEMI treated with fibrinolysis alone (no stent): new crushing substernal pressure at rest for 40 minutes with sweating - not pleuritic, not positional - unrelieved by nitroglycerin. BP 132/84, HR 102, no new murmur, neck veins flat, lungs clear.
correlates.workup: ECG: new ST elevation in the original leads; troponin still high from the first infarct (it stays up 7-10 days), so it cannot answer the question; CK-MB, which had normalized by day 3, has risen again to 28 ng/mL.
correlates.management: Manage as a new ST-elevation event: aspirin, P2Y12 inhibitor, heparin and emergent angiography with PCI of the reoccluded artery; continue high-intensity statin and beta blocker.

correlates.name: Resorption atelectasis
correlates.presentation: A 64-year-old man on day 2 after upper abdominal surgery, on opioids and too sore to cough, has new breathlessness and T 37.9 C. RR 26, HR 108, SpO2 88% on 2 L. Left lower chest: dull, breath sounds absent, moves less; trachea pulled toward the left.
correlates.workup: ABG on 2 L: PaO2 56, PaCO2 38 mmHg. Chest film: dense, shrunken left lower lobe, raised left hemidiaphragm, heart and trachea shifted left, no air bronchograms. Bronchoscopy: mucus plug blocking the left lower lobe bronchus.
correlates.management: Chest physiotherapy, deep breathing and incentive spirometry, early mobilization, pain control that allows coughing; suction or bronchoscopic removal of the plug; CPAP; bronchodilators. Reverses once the airway is open.

correlates.name: Restrictive cardiomyopathy (idiopathic)
correlates.presentation: A 52-year-old woman has a year of fatigue, poor exercise tolerance, swelling legs and a growing abdomen, with only mild breathlessness. No chest radiation, heart surgery or pericarditis. BP 108/72, HR 98; JVP 16 cm, rising on inspiration; liver 4 cm down, ascites, 3+ edema.
correlates.workup: BNP 900 pg/mL. Echo: EF 60%, normal wall thickness, huge atria, slow tissue velocities (e' 4 cm/s), little respiratory variation. CT: pericardium 2 mm, no calcium. Biopsy: interstitial scarring only - no deposits, iron or granulomas.
correlates.management: Exclude constrictive pericarditis first (the correctable look-alike); careful diuretics - keep BP up without cutting output; control rate and anticoagulate for AF; heart transplant is often needed.

correlates.name: Reye syndrome
correlates.presentation: 7-year-old boy recovering from influenza who was given his grandfather's aspirin for fever. Five days later: relentless vomiting, then lethargy, combativeness and a seizure. Temp 37.4 C, HR 120; liver edge 3 cm below the costal margin; no jaundice, rash or neck stiffness.
correlates.workup: AST 420, ALT 380 U/L; ammonia 210 umol/L; PT prolonged; glucose 48; bilirubin normal; CSF: normal cells and protein, high opening pressure; liver biopsy: hepatocytes filled with tiny fat droplets, swollen mitochondria, no inflammation.
correlates.management: ICU supportive care: dextrose-containing fluids, lower intracranial pressure (head up, mannitol or hypertonic saline), vitamin K/plasma for the coagulopathy. Prevention: no aspirin for fever in children (Kawasaki disease is the exception).

correlates.name: Rhabdomyolysis
correlates.presentation: An 82-year-old woman who lives alone is found on her kitchen floor after an unwitnessed fall, probably 2-3 days earlier. She is confused, with dry mucous membranes and swollen, tender thighs. BP 104/62, HR 108. A catheter drains 80 mL of cola-colored urine.
correlates.workup: K+ 6.8 mEq/L, creatinine 2.9 mg/dL (baseline 0.8), creatine kinase 48,000 U/L, phosphate 7.1, calcium 7.6 mg/dL; urine dipstick 3+ blood with 0-2 RBC/hpf; uric acid normal, no recent chemotherapy. ECG: tall narrow-based T waves.
correlates.management: IV calcium gluconate for the ECG changes, then insulin with dextrose and inhaled albuterol to shift K+ into cells; large-volume isotonic fluid to keep urine flowing; hemodialysis if K+ or the kidney injury does not respond.

correlates.name: Rheumatic mitral stenosis
correlates.presentation: A 38-year-old woman from rural Guatemala who had many untreated sore throats as a child has worsening breathlessness on exertion and at night since her last pregnancy. Pulse 118, irregular. A sharp early diastolic sound precedes a low apical rumble, louder lying on her left.
correlates.workup: Echo: thickened leaflets with fused commissures and a narrow orifice (1.0 cm2); left atrium 5.5 cm with appendage thrombus; normal LV size and function. Cath: high wedge pressure with normal LV diastolic pressure. ECG: no P waves.
correlates.management: Rate control (beta blocker) and warfarin for the fibrillation; diuretic for congestion; percutaneous balloon commissurotomy if the anatomy suits, otherwise surgical repair or replacement; penicillin to prevent recurrent strep infection.

correlates.name: Right bundle branch block
correlates.presentation: A 58-year-old man with COPD has no cardiac symptoms; his preoperative ECG before hernia repair is flagged. BP 132/80, pulse 76, afebrile, no syncope. S2 is split in expiration and the split widens further on inspiration.
correlates.workup: ECG: QRS 132 ms; V1-V2 upright with an rSR' (two positive peaks) and T inversion; wide, slurred S waves in I, aVL and V6; no ST elevation.
correlates.management: No specific treatment when isolated and asymptomatic; look for a cause (pulmonary hypertension, PE, ischemia, septal defect) and compare with prior ECGs.

correlates.name: Rocky Mountain spotted fever
correlates.presentation: 16-year-old girl from Oklahoma, back 6 days ago from a week of camping with her dog: T 39.8 C, severe headache, myalgia, vomiting. On day 3 pink blanching macules appeared on the wrists and ankles; now petechial and spreading up the limbs to the trunk, palms and soles.
correlates.workup: Platelets 62,000/uL, Na+ 128 mEq/L, AST 140 U/L, creatinine 1.4 mg/dL. Skin biopsy: small-vessel vasculitis with organisms inside endothelial cells on immunostain. Acute IFA IgG titer still low; it rises by week 2-3.
correlates.management: Start doxycycline immediately on clinical suspicion, at any age, without waiting for serology; supportive care for vascular leak, hyponatremia and organ injury.

correlates.name: Ruptured abdominal aortic aneurysm
correlates.presentation: A 74-year-old male smoker collapses at home with sudden severe left flank and low back pain. BP 78/46 in both arms, pulse 128; he is pale and sweaty, and his abdomen is mildly distended and tender. Urinalysis shows no blood.
correlates.workup: Bedside ultrasound: 7.2 cm infrarenal aorta with surrounding fluid. Hemoglobin 8.9 g/dL and falling. CT angiogram only if he stabilizes: retroperitoneal hematoma contiguous with the aorta.
correlates.management: Call the vascular team for emergent endovascular or open repair; permissive hypotension with blood products instead of large-volume crystalloid; if unstable, skip CT and go straight to the operating room.

correlates.name: Salicylate poisoning
correlates.presentation: 38-year-old woman brought in 4 h after swallowing most of a bottle of her over-the-counter arthritis pills: ringing in both ears, nausea, vomiting and agitation. Temp 38.3 C, RR 32, HR 118, BP 124/78; sweating; lungs clear.
correlates.workup: pH 7.46, PCO2 22, HCO3- 15; Na+ 140, Cl- 105 - gap 20; PCO2 is well below the ~29 that compensation alone predicts (a second, primary respiratory disorder); osmolar gap normal; glucose 88; serum drug level 70 mg/dL.
correlates.management: Activated charcoal; IV sodium bicarbonate to alkalinize serum and urine (ion trapping, urine pH 7.5-8); replete K+; dextrose if confused; dialysis for high levels, severe acidemia or brain/lung injury; if intubated keep ventilation high.

correlates.name: Second-degree AV block, Mobitz type I
correlates.presentation: A 63-year-old woman on verapamil and metoprolol for palpitations feels well but notices her pulse is uneven. Pulse 58 and irregular in a repeating pattern - three beats, then a pause; BP 124/76. No dizziness or fainting.
correlates.workup: ECG: PR 200, then 280, then 340 ms, followed by a P wave with no QRS; the cycle then restarts, giving grouped beats; QRS narrow; R-R intervals shorten before each pause.
correlates.management: Usually observe; reduce or stop the AV-nodal-slowing drugs; atropine only for symptomatic bradycardia; pacing rarely needed.

correlates.name: Second-degree AV block, Mobitz type II
correlates.presentation: A 74-year-old man has had three fainting spells in 2 weeks, each without warning, plus exertional fatigue and breathlessness. He takes no rate-slowing drugs. Pulse 44 and irregular, BP 112/64.
correlates.workup: ECG: PR fixed at 180 ms in every conducted beat, then - with no PR change - a P wave not followed by a QRS (3:2 and 2:1 patterns); conducted QRS wide at 140 ms with a right-bundle pattern.
correlates.management: Permanent pacemaker; transcutaneous pacing if unstable meanwhile (atropine often fails because the lesion lies below the AV node); avoid AV-nodal-slowing drugs.

correlates.name: Secondary adrenal insufficiency
correlates.presentation: A 59-year-old man stopped prednisone 20 mg/day abruptly a month ago after 9 months of treatment for polymyalgia. Now tired, nauseated and lightheaded, with poor appetite. BP 108/70, HR 88; moist mucosa, no edema, no skin darkening.
correlates.workup: Na+ 127, K+ 4.2, glucose 68; serum osm 262, urine osm 420, urine Na+ 40 (euvolemic pattern); TSH normal; 8 a.m. cortisol 2.5 ug/dL with ACTH 8 pg/mL (low); renin and aldosterone normal.
correlates.management: Glucocorticoid replacement (restart prednisone or hydrocortisone, then taper slowly); no mineralocorticoid needed because the renin-aldosterone axis is intact; stress dosing for illness; Na+ normalizes as cortisol is replaced.

correlates.name: Septic embolism
correlates.presentation: 58-year-old man on day 4 of treatment for a 1.6 cm mobile mitral mass: T 38.9 C, sudden sharp left-upper-quadrant pain radiating to the left shoulder, then right flank pain with gross hematuria, then 20 minutes of clumsiness in the right hand.
correlates.workup: CT abdomen: wedge-shaped non-enhancing defects in the spleen and right kidney. MRI brain: several small cortical infarcts. Blood cultures 3/3 coagulase-positive cocci in clusters. TEE: mitral mass now smaller and partly fragmented.
correlates.management: Continue IV antibiotics; urgent valve surgery for a left-sided mass over 10 mm that has already thrown fragments; do not give anticoagulants or thrombolytics (bleeding into infarcts, rupture of infected aneurysms).
avoid: Acute infective endocarditis in a person who injects drugs

correlates.name: Short QT syndrome
correlates.presentation: A 26-year-old man has had bouts of palpitations and two episodes of sudden collapse at rest; his father died suddenly at 35. He takes no medications or supplements. Pulse 70, BP 120/76, normal exam.
correlates.workup: ECG: QT 280 ms at a rate of 70 with tall, narrow, peaked T waves; Ca2+ 9.3 mg/dL and K+ 4.1 mEq/L (normal); no digoxin use. EP study: very brief refractory periods; fibrillation is easily induced in both atria and ventricles.
correlates.management: ICD for arrest survivors and high-risk patients; quinidine (blocks K+ current and lengthens the QT) as an adjunct; avoid drugs that reduce the QT further, such as digoxin.

correlates.name: SIADH
correlates.presentation: A 78-year-old man who smokes a pack a day is admitted with pneumonia. His Na+ falls from 129 to 119 mEq/L despite fluid restriction to 1 L/day and he becomes confused and nauseated. BP 132/80, HR 84; moist mucosa, normal neck veins, no edema.
correlates.workup: Na+ 119, serum osm 250 mOsm/kg, urine osm 890 mOsm/kg, urine Na+ 55; uric acid 2.8, BUN 8; TSH and 8 a.m. cortisol normal. CT chest: right infrahilar mass with an airless, consolidated segment beyond it.
correlates.management: Restrict fluids to 800-1000 mL/day; add salt tablets with furosemide, or a vasopressin-receptor antagonist (tolvaptan), if Na+ stays low; raise Na+ no more than 10 mEq/L per 24 h; treat the cause (the lung mass).

correlates.name: Sick sinus syndrome
correlates.presentation: A 79-year-old woman who takes no beta blocker, calcium channel blocker or digoxin has 3 months of fatigue and two near-faints, one while standing in church. Pulse 42 and regular, BP 128/70; otherwise normal exam.
correlates.workup: Holter: rate 38-45 with a normal P wave before each QRS, plus pauses of 3.8 s with no P wave at all, ended by a junctional escape beat; rate barely rises on exertion. TSH and K+ normal.
correlates.management: Stop any rate-slowing drug; atropine for acute symptomatic slowing; permanent pacemaker for symptomatic bradycardia or pauses.

correlates.name: Spontaneous pneumothorax from paraseptal emphysema
correlates.presentation: Tall, thin 20-year-old man, previously healthy, out jogging with no blow to the chest, suddenly becomes very short of breath with sharp right chest pain. HR 118, RR 30, SpO2 89%. Right chest: no breath sounds, hyperresonant, moves less; trachea pushed to the left.
correlates.workup: CXR: right lung edge seen as a thin white line with no lung markings beyond it; mediastinum shifted to the left. CT after re-expansion: small thin-walled air cysts under the pleura at both apices; the rest of the lung and the ribs normal.
correlates.management: Needle decompression first if hypotensive, then a right chest tube (air rushes out on insertion); stop smoking; after a recurrence, thoracoscopic removal of the apical bullae with pleurodesis.

correlates.name: Stable angina
correlates.presentation: 55-year-old man with hypertension and type 2 diabetes: 6 months of crushing midchest pressure that comes on climbing stairs, lasts about 7 minutes and goes away with rest; the pattern has not changed. Father had an MI at 50. BP 138/84, HR 76, normal exam at rest.
correlates.workup: Resting ECG normal; troponin normal; exercise ECG: 2 mm horizontal ST depression in V4-V6 at 7 minutes with his usual pain, resolving in recovery; angiography, if done: a fixed ~75% LAD narrowing.
correlates.management: SL nitroglycerin every 5 min up to 3 doses, then EMS; a beta-1-selective blocker first (no ISA agents such as acebutolol); add a CCB, long-acting nitrate or ranolazine; aspirin, high-intensity statin; revascularize if refractory.

correlates.name: Stanford type A aortic dissection
correlates.presentation: A 62-year-old man with poorly controlled hypertension has sudden, maximal-at-onset pain in the front of his chest and between the shoulder blades. BP 176/98 right arm, 138/80 left arm; pulse 104. A new soft early diastolic decrescendo murmur is heard at the left sternal border.
correlates.workup: ECG: sinus tachycardia, no ST elevation. CXR: widened mediastinum. CT angiogram: intimal flap with true and false lumens starting in the ascending aorta and running through the arch; small pericardial effusion. If too unstable for CT: TEE.
correlates.management: Emergent surgical repair; until then IV esmolol or labetalol (heart rate <60, systolic BP 100-120); no anticoagulants or thrombolytics. Tamponade and acute valve regurgitation are the usual causes of death.

correlates.name: Stanford type B aortic dissection
correlates.presentation: A 58-year-old man with untreated hypertension who uses cocaine has sudden severe pain between his shoulder blades that is moving down into his lower back. BP 192/110 in both arms, pulse 98. No murmur, normal neurologic exam, abdomen soft without a pulsatile mass.
correlates.workup: CT angiogram: an intimal flap with a false lumen beginning just distal to the left subclavian artery and running down to the renal arteries; ascending aorta and arch normal; no pericardial fluid. CXR: widened mediastinum.
correlates.management: IV beta blocker first (esmolol or labetalol) to lower heart rate and BP and stop propagation; add a vasodilator later; pain control; endovascular or open repair only for malperfusion, rupture or uncontrollable pain.

correlates.name: Statin-associated myopathy / rhabdomyolysis
correlates.presentation: 67-year-old man on a top-dose cholesterol pill for 3 years started clarithromycin for pneumonia 5 days ago; drinks grapefruit juice daily. Now his thighs and shoulders ache and are weak - he can barely rise from a chair - and his urine is tea-colored. Proximal muscles tender.
correlates.workup: CK 18,500 U/L (>10x upper limit); urine dipstick strongly positive for blood but no RBCs on microscopy; creatinine 2.1 (0.9 baseline); K+ 5.4; AST/ALT mildly up; TSH normal.
correlates.management: Stop the cholesterol drug and clarithromycin; IV isotonic fluid for urine output ~200 mL/h; watch K+, Ca2+ and creatinine; after recovery retry a low-dose HMG-CoA reductase inhibitor not cleared by CYP3A4, or ezetimibe or bempedoic acid.

correlates.name: Status asthmaticus
correlates.presentation: 26-year-old man with lifelong asthma, out of his controller inhaler: 2 days of worsening wheeze; 3 hours of nebulized albuterol-ipratropium, IV methylprednisolone and IV magnesium give no relief. Drowsy, speaks 2 words at a time, RR 34, HR 132, SpO2 88%, almost no air movement.
correlates.workup: ABG at 3 h: pH 7.30, PaCO2 50, PaO2 58 mmHg (1 h earlier: pH 7.48, PaCO2 30). Peak flow 25% of predicted and not improving. Systolic BP falls 22 mmHg with each breath in. CXR: hyperinflation, no infiltrate, no collapsed lung.
correlates.management: Intubate and ventilate now (a normal or acidotic pH means he is tiring): slow rate, long expiratory time, accept a high PaCO2; keep up nebulized albuterol, IV steroids and magnesium; consider IV epinephrine or ketamine; ICU care.

correlates.name: STEMI
correlates.presentation: 47-year-old man with hypertension and high cholesterol: 30 minutes of constant, squeezing 10/10 substernal pain at rest spreading to the left shoulder, unrelieved by SL nitroglycerin in the ambulance; sweating heavily. HR 108, BP 104/68, SpO2 95%, lungs clear.
correlates.workup: ECG: 3 mm ST elevation in I and aVL with reciprocal ST depression in III and aVF; troponin and CK-MB rising; bedside echo: lateral wall not moving; cath: abrupt complete cutoff of the left circumflex.
correlates.management: Chewed aspirin, P2Y12 inhibitor, heparin, nitrates if BP allows; emergent PCI, door-to-balloon <=90 min; if PCI is >120 min away, fibrinolysis within 30 min of first contact, then transfer; high-intensity statin; beta blocker within 24 h.

correlates.name: Stress (takotsubo) cardiomyopathy
correlates.presentation: A 67-year-old woman develops crushing substernal chest pain and breathlessness an hour after being robbed at knifepoint outside her shop. No prior heart disease; nonsmoker, normal lipids last year. BP 102/68, HR 104; soft apical systolic murmur, bibasilar crackles.
correlates.workup: ECG: ST elevation V2-V5, deep T inversion by the next day; troponin I 1.8 ng/mL (modest). Cath: no obstructive coronary disease. Ventriculogram: apex and mid-walls akinetic and bulging in systole while the base contracts hard; EF 35%.
correlates.management: Supportive: beta blocker and ACE inhibitor while it recovers, diuretic for congestion; avoid inotropes if the outflow tract is obstructed; anticoagulate if an apical clot forms; function usually returns within weeks.

correlates.name: Subacute infective endocarditis after a dental procedure
correlates.presentation: 62-year-old man with mitral prolapse and regurgitation had a molar pulled 5 weeks ago. Since then: evening temperatures to 38.1 C, night sweats, aching joints, 4 kg weight loss. HR 94; apical holosystolic murmur louder than last visit; spleen tip palpable; pale conjunctivae.
correlates.workup: Blood cultures 3/3 at 36 h: gram-positive cocci in chains, catalase-negative, alpha-hemolytic, bile-esculin negative. TEE: 9 mm mass on the posterior mitral leaflet. Hb 10.4 g/dL, ESR 82 mm/h, rheumatoid factor positive, urine RBCs.
correlates.management: Draw cultures before antibiotics; IV penicillin G or ceftriaxone for 4 weeks, usually curative without surgery; antibiotic prophylaxis before future gum or tooth manipulation.

correlates.name: Supraventricular tachycardia in an infant
correlates.presentation: A 6-week-old boy, well this morning, has been fussy and pale with poor feeding for 3 h. HR 280 and does not change with crying or calming; RR 60, BP 78/50, capillary refill 3 s; afebrile, no murmur.
correlates.workup: ECG: regular, narrow QRS complexes at 280/min with no visible P waves and no beat-to-beat change in rate (sinus rhythm in a baby this age rarely exceeds 220 and varies with activity).
correlates.management: Vagal maneuver first - ice bag over the whole face including the nose, on a monitor, IV placed meanwhile; stable and not converting: rapid IV push adenosine; unstable: synchronized cardioversion; then cardiology for an accessory pathway.

correlates.name: Sustained monomorphic VT
correlates.presentation: A 66-year-old man with an anterior MI 3 years ago (EF 30%) has 1 hour of palpitations and lightheadedness. Pulse 170 and regular, BP 104/68; he is alert and talking, lungs clear.
correlates.workup: ECG: regular wide-complex rhythm at 170/min, QRS 160 ms, every complex identical; P waves march through at 80/min unrelated to the QRS, with an occasional narrow captured beat. Echo: akinetic, scarred anterior wall.
correlates.management: Stable: IV amiodarone (or procainamide, or lidocaine if ischemic); unstable: synchronized cardioversion. Correct ischemia and electrolytes; ICD for secondary prevention; ablation of the scar circuit if it recurs.

correlates.name: Syphilitic aortitis
correlates.presentation: A 64-year-old man had a painless genital ulcer at age 35 that healed without treatment. He now has 6 months of exertional dyspnea and a dry cough. BP 158/52, pulse 84; an early diastolic decrescendo murmur is loudest at the right upper sternal border.
correlates.workup: RPR 1:16, FTA-ABS positive. CXR: thin linear calcification along the ascending aorta. CT angiogram: ascending aorta and root dilated to 5.6 cm, descending aorta spared. Histology: plasma cells around obliterated vasa vasorum.
correlates.management: Penicillin after CSF evaluation (benzathine weekly x3, or IV penicillin G if CSF is abnormal); surgical replacement of the ascending aorta and valve for symptoms or a large root.

correlates.name: Tangier disease
correlates.presentation: 38-year-old man with 3 years of numbness and weakness of both hands and loss of pain and temperature sense over the arms and face; spleen tip palpable; no proteinuria or anemia. His brother had a heart attack at 42.
correlates.workup: HDL 2 mg/dL with apoA-I nearly absent; LDL 60, TG 210 mg/dL; rectal or tonsil biopsy: cholesteryl ester-filled macrophages; his cells cannot move cholesterol to the outer membrane leaflet for loading onto HDL.
correlates.management: No specific therapy: low-fat diet, manage atherosclerotic risk (statin if warranted), supportive neuropathy care; splenectomy or tonsillectomy only for symptoms. Raising HDL with drugs does not help.

correlates.name: Tetralogy of Fallot
correlates.presentation: A 2-year-old boy adopted from abroad has always been small (weight <3rd percentile) and tires fast at play; when he cries his lips turn deep blue and he breathes fast. SpO2 84% at rest, clubbed fingers, RV lift; harsh 3/6 systolic ejection murmur at the left upper sternal border.
correlates.workup: Chest film: normal-sized heart with sparse lung vascular markings. ECG: right axis deviation, tall R in V1. Echo: large VSD with the aorta straddling it; narrow right ventricular outflow, 70-mmHg gradient.
correlates.management: During a blue episode: knees to chest, oxygen, IV morphine and fluids, phenylephrine to raise systemic resistance (beta blocker sometimes); prostaglandin only if flow depends on the ductus; complete surgical repair in infancy.

correlates.name: Third-degree AV block
correlates.presentation: An 81-year-old woman with no tick exposure or recent illness has a week of fatigue, two fainting spells and breathlessness on minimal exertion; she takes no rate-slowing drugs. Pulse 34 and regular, BP 168/60; S1 varies in loudness from beat to beat.
correlates.workup: ECG: P waves at 80/min and QRS complexes at 34/min, each perfectly regular (constant P-P and R-R) but unrelated to each other; more P waves than QRS; QRS 150 ms with secondary T inversion. Lyme serology negative.
correlates.management: Transcutaneous or transvenous pacing if unstable (atropine rarely helps a low escape rhythm), then a permanent pacemaker; look for a reversible cause - ischemia, Lyme disease, drugs.

management: Second-degree AV block, Mobitz type II

correlates.name: Thoracic aortic aneurysm
correlates.presentation: A 67-year-old woman with 25 years of hypertension has 4 months of hoarseness, a dry cough, trouble swallowing solids and a dull upper-back ache. BP 168/96, pulse 76, afebrile. Arm BPs are equal, there is no murmur, and neck veins are normal.
correlates.workup: CXR: widened mediastinum with the trachea pushed to the right. CT angiogram: fusiform dilation of the distal arch and descending aorta to 5.9 cm with mural thrombus, no intimal flap. Image the abdominal aorta - 20% have a second dilation.
correlates.management: Symptoms from compression = repair now: endovascular for the descending segment, open with cardiopulmonary bypass for the ascending. Asymptomatic and <5.5 cm: beta-blocker-based BP control, statin, no smoking, CTA at 6 months then yearly.

correlates.name: Thyroid storm
correlates.presentation: A 34-year-old woman with months of weight loss, heat intolerance and protruding eyes, never treated, becomes agitated and delirious the day after an emergency appendectomy. Temp 40.2 C, pulse 162 and irregular, BP 150/60; drenching sweat, tremor, diffuse non-tender neck swelling.
correlates.workup: TSH <0.01 mIU/L, free T4 6.8 ng/dL, T3 high; TSH-receptor antibodies positive. ECG: fast narrow-complex rhythm with no P waves. Glucose 186 mg/dL, ALT 98 U/L, Ca2+ 10.6 mg/dL.
correlates.management: Beta blocker first (propranolol, or esmolol) to control heart rate before an arrhythmia; then a thionamide (methimazole, or PTU when this severe), iodine an hour later, glucocorticoids; cooling, fluids and treatment of the trigger.

correlates.name: Torsades de pointes (drug- and electrolyte-induced)
correlates.presentation: A 68-year-old woman on furosemide for heart failure was started on IV ondansetron and haloperidol after hip surgery. On day 2 she has two brief faints; between them her pulse is 52 and regular. She has never fainted before and has no family history of sudden death.
correlates.workup: Telemetry: a sinus beat with QTc 590 ms, then a run of wide complexes at 240/min whose amplitude and axis twist steadily around the baseline, ending on its own. K+ 2.9 mEq/L, Mg2+ 1.2 mg/dL, Ca2+ 8.0 mg/dL.
correlates.management: IV magnesium sulfate 2 g first, even if Mg2+ is normal; stop the QT-prolonging drugs; replete K+ to >4; overdrive pacing for bradycardia-dependent runs; cardiovert if unstable, defibrillate if pulseless.

correlates.name: Total anomalous pulmonary venous return
correlates.presentation: A 5-day-old boy has worsening fast breathing, grunting and duskiness: SpO2 78% in arm and leg, little change on oxygen. RR 80, HR 175; fine crackles throughout both lungs; soft systolic murmur at the left upper sternal border; liver edge 3 cm below the ribs.
correlates.workup: Chest film: heart not enlarged; both lungs densely white with streaky, congested markings. Echo: no veins enter the left atrium; a common venous channel drains to the right side and is narrowed; right-to-left flow across the atrial septum.
correlates.management: Urgent surgical reconnection of the lung veins to the left atrium - an emergency if the venous pathway is obstructed; ventilate and support meanwhile; the atrial (and ductal) shunt must stay open until repair.

correlates.name: Transient ischemic attack
correlates.presentation: A 69-year-old man with hypertension and hyperlipidemia had 15 minutes of left face and arm weakness with slurred speech that fully cleared before he reached the ED. His neurologic exam is now normal; a bruit is heard over the right side of the neck.
correlates.workup: MRI with diffusion: no infarct. Carotid duplex: peak systolic velocity 290 cm/s at the right internal carotid origin (~80% narrowing on the outer wall of the bifurcation); CTA confirms and shows normal vertebrobasilar arteries.
correlates.management: Start aspirin (+/- clopidogrel) and a high-intensity statin now; carotid endarterectomy, preferred over stenting, for the symptomatic high-grade lesion; BP control, stop smoking - about 1 in 3 have a stroke after a first episode.

correlates.name: Transposition of the great arteries
correlates.presentation: A 4.1-kg term boy born to a mother with poorly controlled diabetes is deeply blue within hours of birth: SpO2 62% in all four limbs, barely changing on 100% oxygen. RR 60 without grunting or retractions; no significant murmur; single loud second heart sound.
correlates.workup: ABG on 100% O2: PaO2 35 mmHg (never rises above 150). Chest film: mildly enlarged heart, normal-to-increased lung vascular markings. Echo: aorta arises from the right ventricle and the pulmonary trunk from the left; small atrial opening.
correlates.management: Start a prostaglandin E1 infusion to keep the ductus open; balloon atrial septostomy if the atrial opening is too small for mixing; definitive arterial switch operation in the first weeks of life.

correlates.name: Traumatic aortic injury
correlates.presentation: A 27-year-old unrestrained driver hit a tree at about 60 mph. He has anterior chest pain with a steering-wheel bruise across the sternum. BP 100/62, pulse 116, breath sounds equal, neck veins flat, heart sounds normal.
correlates.workup: CXR: mediastinum widened to 9 cm, loss of the knob contour, left apical pleural cap, fractured first rib. CT angiogram: contained outpouching with intimal disruption just distal to the left subclavian artery, at the ligamentum arteriosum.
correlates.management: Tight heart-rate and BP control with an IV beta blocker (systolic <100-120) while other injuries are stabilized, then endovascular stent-graft repair of the isthmus.

correlates.name: Tricuspid atresia
correlates.presentation: A 2-week-old girl is blue (SpO2 75%) and tires after 1 oz of each feed. RR 58, HR 160. Holosystolic murmur at the left lower sternal border; the cardiac impulse is felt at the apex, with no lift over the lower sternum; liver 2 cm below the ribs.
correlates.workup: ECG: superior QRS axis (-60 degrees), tall P waves in II, left ventricular forces dominant. Chest film: normal-sized heart, sparse lung markings. Echo: no flow from right atrium into a small right ventricle; ASD and VSD present.
correlates.management: Prostaglandin E1 to keep the ductus open for lung blood flow; then staged surgery - systemic-to-pulmonary shunt, then superior and later total cavopulmonary connection.

correlates.name: Tricuspid regurgitation
correlates.presentation: A 45-year-old man treated for endocarditis from injecting drugs 3 years ago has leg swelling and abdominal fullness; afebrile. JVP 14 cm with a large systolic wave; pulsatile liver. A blowing holosystolic murmur at the left lower sternal border grows louder on inspiration.
correlates.workup: Echo: dilated right ventricle and atrium with a wide systolic backflow jet into the right atrium and a flail septal leaflet; systolic flow reversal in the hepatic veins. Blood cultures negative.
correlates.management: Loop diuretic for congestion; treat the driver (pulmonary hypertension, left-heart disease); surgical repair or replacement if severe and symptomatic, or at the time of left-sided valve surgery.

correlates.name: Tricuspid stenosis
correlates.presentation: A 44-year-old woman from Haiti with rheumatic heart disease has fatigue, cold hands and feet, ascites and leg edema but no orthopnea. JVP 12 cm with a giant wave just before each carotid pulse; a soft mid-diastolic rumble at the left 4th parasternal space is louder on inspiring.
correlates.workup: Echo: thickened, restricted right-sided AV leaflets with a mean diastolic gradient of 6 mmHg; enlarged right atrium; dilated inferior vena cava that does not collapse with breathing; normal LV.
correlates.management: Diuretics and salt restriction for the venous congestion; balloon or surgical commissurotomy or replacement if severe - often at the same operation as the coexisting rheumatic left-sided valve disease.

correlates.name: Tricyclic antidepressant overdose
correlates.presentation: A 34-year-old woman with depression and chronic neuropathic pain is found confused beside an empty pill bottle and then has a generalized seizure. Temp 38.3 C, pulse 132, BP 84/50. Pupils dilated; skin hot and dry.
correlates.workup: ECG: sinus tachycardia, QRS 150 ms with a tall terminal R wave in aVR and right axis deviation, QTc 520 ms. Salicylate and acetaminophen levels undetectable; anion gap 12; glucose normal.
correlates.management: IV sodium bicarbonate boluses for QRS >100 ms (the sodium load and alkalinization overcome the Na+ channel block); airway, benzodiazepines for seizures, norepinephrine for refractory hypotension; avoid class IA/IC drugs and physostigmine.

correlates.name: Trousseau syndrome (malignancy-associated thrombosis)
correlates.presentation: 64-year-old smoker with 10 kg weight loss over 3 months and upper-abdominal pain into the back. Over 4 weeks, tender red cords have appeared on the left forearm, then the right thigh, then the chest wall, each fading as the next appears. No surgery, travel or family history.
correlates.workup: Duplex: superficial vein clots at each site plus a fresh left popliteal clot; platelets and coagulation tests normal; thrombophilia panel unrevealing; CA 19-9 high; CT abdomen: 3-cm mass in the body of the pancreas.
correlates.management: Anticoagulate with LMWH or a factor Xa inhibitor (warfarin often fails here) for as long as the cancer is active; stage and treat the tumor; any unprovoked clot earns age-appropriate cancer screening and imaging.

correlates.name: True left ventricular aneurysm
correlates.presentation: 62-year-old man 6 months after a large anterior-apical MI: months of exertional breathlessness and palpitations; today sudden right-sided weakness and inability to speak. Broad apical impulse displaced laterally that pushes outward in systole; S3; no neck bruits; BP 128/76.
correlates.workup: ECG: Q waves with ST elevation in V1-V4 still present 6 months after the MI; echo: thin, wide-necked apical segment of scarred myocardium bulging outward in systole, lined by a layered mural thrombus; no communication with the pericardium.
correlates.management: Anticoagulation (warfarin) for the mural thrombus; full HFrEF therapy; ICD or ablation for recurrent VT; surgical resection of the scarred segment only for refractory heart failure or VT - rupture is rare.

correlates.name: Tumor lysis syndrome
correlates.presentation: A 24-year-old man with bulky mediastinal and abdominal lymphoma got his first chemotherapy cycle 36 h ago. Now nauseated, with tingling fingers, twitching muscles and palpitations; urine output has fallen to 15 mL/h. BP 136/84, HR 104.
correlates.workup: K+ 6.9 mEq/L, phosphate 9.8 mg/dL, Ca2+ 6.7, uric acid 15.2 mg/dL, creatinine 2.6 (0.9 before chemo), LDH 2,400 U/L; CK normal. ECG: peaked T waves, QTc 490 ms.
correlates.management: Aggressive IV volume expansion; treat K+ (IV calcium, insulin with dextrose); phosphate binder; rasburicase for the uric acid; early hemodialysis for kidney failure or symptomatic low calcium. Prevention: hydration plus allopurinol.

correlates.name: Turner syndrome
correlates.presentation: 15-year-old girl at the 2nd height centile with no breast development and no periods; normal school grades. Low hairline at the nape and skin folds along the sides of the neck. BP 148/88 in the right arm, 104/70 in the leg; weak, delayed femoral pulses.
correlates.workup: FSH 96 mIU/mL, estradiol undetectable; karyotype 45,X in all 30 cells counted; echo: bicuspid aortic valve and narrowing of the descending aorta near the ductus; renal ultrasound: horseshoe kidney.
correlates.management: Repair the aortic narrowing; high-dose growth hormone for height, then estrogen replacement at pubertal age; search many cells for Y material and remove the gonads if present (gonadoblastoma risk); lifelong aortic imaging.

correlates.name: Type 4 renal tubular acidosis (hypoaldosteronism)
correlates.presentation: 68-year-old man with 15 years of type 2 diabetes, diabetic kidney disease and hypertension; routine labs show K+ 6.1 with a stable eGFR of 42; he feels well. BP 148/88, HR 72, trace ankle edema. Meds: metformin and amlodipine; no K+ supplements, no ACE inhibitor.
correlates.workup: Na+ 137, K+ 6.1, Cl- 112, HCO3- 18 - gap 7 (normal); creatinine 1.7 mg/dL, eGFR 42; urine pH 5.0; plasma renin and aldosterone both low; ECG: tall, narrow, peaked T waves with normal QRS.
correlates.management: Low-K+ diet; stop K+-raising drugs (NSAIDs, ACE inhibitors/ARBs, K+-sparing diuretics); loop or thiazide diuretic; K+ binder such as patiromer; fludrocortisone only if no hypertension or edema; oral bicarbonate if acidemic.

correlates.name: Unstable angina
correlates.presentation: 47-year-old smoker with diabetes and a strong family history: chest pain that used to come only when jogging now comes after one flight of stairs, and today came on walking to the car and lasted 20 minutes at rest; SL nitroglycerin barely helps. BP 146/90, HR 96; exam normal.
correlates.workup: ECG during pain: 1.5 mm ST depression and T-wave inversion in V4-V6; high-sensitivity troponin normal on arrival and again 4-6 h later; CK-MB normal - no myocyte death.
correlates.management: Aspirin plus a P2Y12 inhibitor, heparin, beta blocker, nitrates, high-intensity statin, ACE inhibitor; no fibrinolysis; urgent angiography/PCI within 24-48 h, emergent if pain persists or shock, heart failure or sustained VT appear.

correlates.name: Vascular Ehlers-Danlos syndrome
correlates.presentation: A 26-year-old woman of average height with thin, translucent skin showing the veins over her chest and hands and easy bruising has sudden severe flank pain after lifting a box. Her mother died in her 40s of a ruptured brain artery.
correlates.workup: CT angiogram: dissection and rupture of the left renal artery with retroperitoneal blood. Genetic testing: pathogenic COL3A1 variant (type III collagen), autosomal dominant.
